## R-383. The favourites listing stops at the first short page, so it reads a fraction of the account

**Found:** during the fourth attended sitting, 2026-09-17, verifying the hearts
the first real sweep wrote.

`listing.paginate` ends its walk when a page comes back shorter than the page size
it asked for. That rule is wrong for this provider's favourite tracks listing,
because the provider serves a WINDOW of a counted collection and omits from it the
tracks it will not serve, so a full window arrives short.

**Cause corrected by U65.** This entry originally said the CLIENT drops the
unplayable tracks. It does not. Read against tidalapi 0.8.11, `Favorites.tracks`
hands the response to `map_json`, which maps every item with no filtering, and the
`Track ... is unavailable` line visible during the sitting comes from
`session.track()`, a per identifier lookup off the listing path. The omission is
the API's, and `Favorites.get_tracks_count` documents the other half of it, that
the total it reports "also includes track that may not be available for playback".
The measurements below are unchanged. Walked by hand at the same moment,
the account holds **197 favourite tracks; the shipped read returned 93** and
stopped at the second page. The same read is what `TidalAccount.has_heart`
answers from.

**Not every listing.** Measured in the same sitting: the account's playlists read
599 both ways, and a 197 track playlist's membership read 197 both ways, so this
is the listings the client filters rather than the pagination helper being wrong
everywhere.

**Measured cost, and it is a reporting one that mostly does not bite.** A track
already hearted is read as not hearted, so the sweep hearts it again. The write is
add only and idempotent, so the account ends correct. The listing is ordered
newest first, which is why the damage is bounded: the 93 rows it does return are
the most recent hearts, so the second sweep in the same sitting read all 59
matched rows as already hearted and wrote nothing. What is unreliable is any
question about an OLD heart, and the first sweep's 18 hearted against 41 already
cannot be trusted as a split for that reason. `favorites.placeholders` exclusions and anything else keyed on the
favourites read are affected the same way.

**Why not fixed here.** One rule governs every listing in the product, including
the label crawls and the playlists source, and removing the short page stop makes
a listing whose offset parameter is broken walk forever. That is a unit with a
test per listing, not a late change inside an attended sitting. Phillip's call,
2026-09-17.

**The code half is done, by U65.** Every shape declares its own stop rule and its
own request budget. The favourites read ends on `get_tracks_count`, a count the
provider publishes for the same collection its windows are cut from, so no page
shape ends that walk any more. The unit's own review found that stopping on an
empty page, which was U65's first fix, only moved the boundary: a window whose
every counted item is unservable comes back empty mid collection. Two shapes with
no published count are narrowed rather than closed and carry R-385.

**Still open, and it is the live half.** Nothing here has read the real account
under the new rule, and a live provider call is attended. The closing condition
below is deliberately unchanged.

**Closes when:** the favourites read returns the account's full set on the live
library, 197 both ways at the numbers this entry records, or whatever the account
holds on the day.

**CLOSED 2026-09-23 at the sixth attended sitting, the live half.** `crate intake
playlist favorites` from the pipx install at `1d2136f` read the account under
U65's rule: **215 declared by the provider's count, 206 listed, 9 withheld**, and
the 9 said so, in the `intake-hearts-withheld` warning and in the envelope's
`shortfall` block, which is R-504's report by count. The old rule had read 93 of
197 six days earlier. The account held 197 on 2026-09-17 and 215 on the day, so
the number moved with the account and not with the read, and the walk no longer
ends on a page shape. What the 206 rows then resolved to on the library is
R-664, a different defect in a different module.

## R-384. Every listing now pays one extra request, and on artist releases that is doubled

**Found:** by U65, in its own P6 pass, asking what depended on the old stop rule.

Two of the four shapes end on a count the provider declares, and they pay nothing
for it: the count replaces the request the walk would have spent on the page that
ends it, and for a playlist the count is already parsed onto the object, so
`playlist_tracks` got one request CHEAPER. The other two publish no count and end
on an empty page, which costs one request per walk that the short page rule did
not.

**The arithmetic, and it is not flat.** `account_playlists` is read once per sync,
so the cost is one request. `artist_releases` is read once per release METHOD per
ARTIST, and there are two methods, so a label crawl over A artists pays 2A extra
requests. Almost every artist fits inside one page, which is why the cost is very
nearly the full doubling of that crawl's request count rather than a fraction of
it. The sitting of 2026-09-17 crawled 15 labels of the 47 it swept, and the artist
count behind those labels was not recorded, so the absolute number is unknown.

**Measured cost: none, and that is the point of filing it.** This was reasoned
from the code and the request shape, not observed. No live sweep has run under the
new rule. `fetch_with_retry` already backs off on a rate limit with capped
exponential backoff, so the predicted outcome is a slower sweep rather than a
failed one, and that prediction is also unmeasured.

**Why not fixed here.** The alternative is keeping a page shape rule on
`artist_releases`, which is the shape whose early stop would silently shorten a
label catalogue, and that is this product's core job. Slower beats wrong.

**Closes when:** a live label sweep runs under the new rule and its request count
and wall clock are recorded next to the sitting of 2026-09-17, or the provider
exposes a release count the walk can end on, which would remove the cost entirely.

## R-385. Two listings are narrowed rather than closed, because their provider publishes no count

**Found:** by U65's own review, which found that the fix it had just written moved
R-383's boundary instead of closing it.

No page SHAPE can say where a filtered collection ends. The provider omits items it
will not serve from a window while still counting them in it, so a short page is
not the end and neither is an empty one: a window whose every counted item is
unservable comes back empty in the MIDDLE of a collection. Only a count the
provider declares for the collection it is serving closes the class.

`favorite_tracks` and `playlist_tracks` have one, `get_tracks_count` and
`numberOfTracks`, and they end on it. The other two do not:

* `account_playlists` serves `playlistsAndFavoritePlaylists`. The near miss is
  `Favorites.get_playlists_count`, and it must not be used: it counts the root
  collection folder through `my-collection/playlists/folders`, a different
  collection that excludes the playlists the account merely follows. A count of
  the wrong collection is a wrong answer arriving with a confident number.
* `artist_releases` has no count on either release listing.

Both therefore end on an empty page, which is safer than a short one and is not
safe.

**Measured cost: none observed, and the input is not known to be reachable.** It
takes a run of consecutive unservable items one page long to break: 50 for account
playlists, 100 for artist releases. Nothing has been driven that produces such a
run on either shape. On the favourites listing the producer is plausible, since
that listing is ordered by date added and a label catalogue is hearted in one
batch, which is why that shape was the one worth closing properly. Two shapes were
checked for a producer and neither was driven.

**Closes when:** the provider exposes a count for either collection and the shape
ends on it, or a producer is driven that builds a page length run of unservable
items on one of these two shapes, which would turn this from a narrowing into a
measured defect.

## R-386. One member of the listing guard's method set is carried and never tested

**Found:** by U65's mutation table, row `F2_the_structural_guard_loses_a_method_name`,
confirmed zero on the full suite at 7584 collected.

`acquire.listing.GUARDED_METHODS` names the four provider listing methods no
module outside the wrappers may call. Removing `get_ep_singles` from that set
kills nothing. The structural guard would stop catching a hand written
`get_ep_singles` pagination loop and the suite would stay green, because every
test that drives the guard drives it through `tracks` or
`playlist_and_favorite_playlists`.

**Measured cost: none today, and the shape is the point.** The guard exists for
call sites nobody has written yet, which is where this defect came from all three
previous times in the source system. A member of the set that no test exercises
is a member that can be deleted in a refactor with a green suite, and the loss
shows up only when somebody writes the call it was there to catch.

**Not fixed here** because U65's two fix rounds were spent, one on the review's
finding that the empty page rule narrows rather than closes R-383, and one on the
refusal that was being slept on for 31 seconds. The fix is small: a case in
`test_the_guard_catches_a_hand_written_pagination_loop` per guarded method name,
driven from `GUARDED_METHODS` itself so adding a name arms its own case.

**Closes when:** every member of `GUARDED_METHODS` has a case that fails when that
member is removed from the set, and the parametrisation is derived from the set
rather than written beside it.

**Closed 2026-09-17 on `unit/u66-every-guarded-listing-method-has-a-plant`.**
`test_the_guard_catches_a_hand_written_pagination_loop` now has one case per

## R-388. A snapshot whose listing fails tells the person to take a backup

## R-390. `crate job resume` re-arms failed items without reading retryable

**Found:** at the R-380 review, 2026-09-18, one file over from the engine
verdict.

`jobs.retry` re-opens a FAILED job and flips every failed item back to pending.
`cli.jobs.resume` calls it whenever the named job is not open. Neither looks at
the job cause's `retryable` flag. R-380 stopped the job from *telling* a person
to resume permanent failures. Typing the resume verb still does the work.

**Measured cost:** unmeasured on a live run. The sitting's person followed the
printed remedy, which is what R-380 closed. This is the remaining hole if
someone types the verb anyway.

**Why not fixed here.** The issue brief said do not change `jobs.retry`. The
resume verb is that function's only shipped caller.

**Closes when:** a resume of a job whose every failure is non retryable refuses
rather than re-arming those items, or the verb's help says it will retry them
regardless.

**Closed 2026-09-22 on `relay/99`.** `jobs.retry` refuses a closed job whose
cause carries `retryable` false, with the reserved `job-not-retryable` on
PRECONDITION, steps rather than a token, the job's own cause nested inside,
and the mixed reasons at its own top level when the job cause has them. Items
stay as the failure left them. A cancelled job carries a retryable cause and
re-arms; a FAILED job with no cause re-arms, because a missing verdict is not
a permanent one. The resume verb relies on the engine and adds no check.

**What the refusal exposed.** `retryable` defaults to false on every cause, so
a shell that never set the flag was read as having proven its failure
permanent. Eleven tests in six suites re-armed through `jobs.retry` after a
fake failure. Six modelled a transient failure with a fake that recorded it as
permanent, and the fakes changed. Three were backup transfer exits, where the
shell itself never set the flag: a dropped connection mid mirror was recorded
permanent, the job said resume could not succeed since R-380, and this unit's
refusal made the verb agree, so the per portion ledger the backup job exists
for could never be used. `backup-transfer-failed` now carries `retryable`
true and those three tests make the claims they made before. The two that
remain over a module's own permanent verdict are R-656.

orders. The all failed envelope keeps the last item nested, since its own

**Found:** during R-352's review, 2026-09-18.

## R-395. The missing extra message prints a bare pip command that is wrong for a pipx install

**Found:** while rewriting the README install around pipx, 2026-09-18.

When a module is switched on without its extra, both the parser stub and the
worker refusal tell the reader to run `pip install 'cratekit[analysis]'` (or
`vocals`). The text comes from `install_command` in `cli/render.py` and from two
literals in `analysis/cli.py` and `analysis/vocals.py`. The README now installs
with pipx, which keeps Cratekit in its own private environment. A bare `pip` runs
against whichever Python the shell finds first, not the environment `crate` runs
in. The command that works for a pipx install is `pipx install --force '.[analysis]'`
from inside the clone, and it is in the README. The developer hint in
`cli/doctor.py`, `pip install -e '.[dev]'`, is correct for the virtual
environment used in development and is not part of this finding.

**Measured cost:** a pipx user who follows the printed command gets an error, or
an extra installed where `crate` never reads it, and the same refusal appears
again. The pipx install and update commands were run against a clean clone in a
scratch folder. The printed message was not run under pipx, so the failure above
is read from the code, not observed.

**Closes when:** the printed command installs into the environment `crate` is
running from, for a pipx install and for a plain virtual environment, or the
message points at the README instead of naming a command. The three tests that
assert the literal `pip install 'cratekit[analysis]'` change with it.

**Closed 2026-09-21 on `relay/109`.** The command has one source,
`modules/extras.py`, read by the parser stub through `render.install_command`
and by both worker refusals. It sits in the modules layer because the analysis
workers may not import the CLI and nothing below modules may spell a package
manager line; `cli.registry.DISTRIBUTION` is re-exported from it. A process
whose `sys.prefix` holds `pipx_metadata.json` prints `pipx install --force`
against the source pipx recorded, with the extras it recorded kept, since
`--force` reinstalls from exactly the spec given and naming only the missing
extra drops the other. Any other process prints `<its interpreter> -m pip
install 'cratekit[x]'`. Driven live in a scratch pipx home: the vocals refusal
printed the pipx form against the clone, the printed analysis command was run
from an unrelated folder, librosa imported afterwards, the next vocals command
named `[analysis,vocals]`, and `pipx reinstall` kept librosa. The built in
review raised one finding, fixed in round one: the fallback discarded the
recorded extras. What this leaves is R-646. Table `docs/mutation/r395.md`, read
in `r395-notes.md`.

## R-396. A restore into a scratch directory still takes the live library's lock and still needs rekordbox closed

**NARROWED 2026-09-20, by U96 on `relay/141`, in its last paragraph only.**
`core.restore.bare_metal_session` now HAS a caller in `src`, the recovery verb,
so the sentence below saying it has none is no longer true. That does not move
this finding. The session refuses unless the recorded library is genuinely
unreachable, so it cannot serve a rehearsal, which by definition runs while the
library is present, and U96 was scoped not to loosen the rehearsal's gates.
Everything else here is open exactly as written, and "a gate set that fits a
target" is still unbuilt for the case where the library is alive.

**Found:** 2026-09-18, landing the restore rehearsal target, and named in that
unit's brief as the leftover it would file.

**395 is skipped on purpose.** Main's highest number at branch time was R-394,
which is what the brief said to number above, and by the time this was written
GitHub issue 109 carried R-395 in its title for a different finding, the
missing-extra message printing a bare pip command. An issue title is a surface
this document cannot see and is why a renumber is forbidden, so the fresh
number moved rather than the one already given. A gap is fine.

`crate restore run --from-backup --target SCRATCH` restores the database into
a directory the live library is not in and does not contain. It reaches that
work through `restore.recovery_session`, which is the live restore's gate set
unchanged: the backup acknowledgment, the volume identity check, the library
lock, an analysis-files watch over the library root, and a session record
written on the live volume. `backup.plan_restore` then refuses while rekordbox
or its agent is running. None of those describes anything the rehearsal
touches. The run writes only under the target.

Driven: the suite's `test_a_rehearsal_is_still_refused_while_rekordbox_is_running`
refuses a scratch restore with `rekordbox-running` and exit 21, and the
session log gains a recovery record for a run whose every write landed in a
temporary directory.

**Measured cost:** a person cannot rehearse a restore while they are using
rekordbox, which is the moment a rehearsal costs them least, and every
rehearsal leaves a recovery session in the log of a library it did not touch.
The conservative direction: nothing is lost, the gates are the ones the live
restore passes, and no state is at risk. Unmeasured how often a person would
want to rehearse with the application open.

**Why not fixed here.** Loosening the gates for a target is its own unit with
its own blast radius. The lock is not obviously wrong even here: the target is
not the library, and the SNAPSHOT the restore is planned against is the live
library's, so a write session committing mid-rehearsal changes what the
rehearsal is evidence about. `core.restore.bare_metal_session` already exists
for recovery onto a volume that is not this one, has no caller in `src`, and
is the place a gate set that fits a target belongs.

**Closes when:** a rehearsal runs under gates chosen for a target that is not
the library, or the decision is recorded that a rehearsal keeps the live
gates and the session record is written somewhere it cannot be read as a
recovery of this library.

## R-397. The unwired guard is a name ban, so a mark wired through another name walks past it

**Found:** during the code half of R-358, 2026-09-18, writing the guard that
holds the production path unwired.

`tests/test_sync_all.py::test_the_pass_composes_no_mark_step_while_no_sweep_writes_an_importable_file`
parses `src/cratekit/sync/cli.py` and asserts that neither `mark_swept` nor
`rename_playlist` appears as an attribute, a name, or an imported name. That is
this file's own recorded shape "a test that forbids a feature by naming the last
implementation's symbols". It forbids those two names, not the act. A session
wiring the mark step through a helper called anything else, or through
`getattr`, passes it.

**Driven:** row `T1_unwired_guard_reads_names` in `docs/mutation/r358.md` killed
zero on the full suite, 0 of 7672, which is the same fact from the other side:
nothing asserts the guard's own breadth, so nothing can tell a narrow version
from a wide one.

**Measured cost.** Bounded and small today, because the thing on the other side
of the guard is one function with one caller and the guard is one of two things
holding the line, the other being that no sweep writes an importable file at
all, which `marks.apply_deferred` refuses on independently of any name. An
unattended session that wired a differently named mark step would still be
refused `sync-marks-blocked` before it reached a real account. Not observed.

**The conservative call made here.** Keep the name ban and say what it is. The
alternative, asserting a property rather than a name, needs a definition of "the
mark step" the code does not carry, and inventing one to be guarded is how a
guard starts describing its own fixture.

**Closes when:** the live half of R-358 is done and the guard is deleted, which
is the same moment, or the production path gains a declared mark step the guard
can ask about by role instead of by name.

**CLOSED 2026-09-19 on `relay/127`, U82, by the second condition.** The name ban
is deleted. The mark step is now a declared verb with its own explicit gate, so
what is left to hold is that the ungated pass never renames, and
`tests/test_sync_all.py::test_a_pass_renames_nothing_even_over_a_recorded_playlist_with_its_file_landed`
holds that by the act: it binds the account seam, meets every condition a mark
needs, runs the pass and asserts nothing was renamed, whatever a future mark
step is called.

## R-398. The deferred mark's file check can raise a bare OSError between two syscalls

**Found:** during the code half of R-358, 2026-09-18, reading the failure paths
of the engine this unit became the first caller of.

`sync/marks.py::apply_deferred` opens with
`if not local_output.is_file() or local_output.stat().st_size == 0`. Two
syscalls over one path, with a window between them. A file that exists at the
first and is gone at the second raises `FileNotFoundError` out of `stat`, which
is a bare `OSError` reaching the caller rather than the `sync-marks-blocked`
refusal three lines below that describes exactly that situation.

**Driven:** not driven. `git grep -n apply_deferred -- src` had one hit before
this unit, the definition itself, so this unit is the engine's first caller and
owns its unreviewed failure paths under METHOD's own rule. The window was read
rather than raced, and the report says so.

**Measured cost.** Unmeasured, and reachable only by something this repository
does not have yet. Nothing on the production path calls `mark_swept`, and the
importable file a future caller would hand it is one the same run just wrote, so
the window needs a second writer removing it mid pass. The cost if it happened is
a traceback instead of a refusal, at the one step whose whole design is that it
refuses rather than marking.

**Why not fixed here.** `sync/marks.py` is out of this unit's brief, which names
it as a key file for wiring and not for change, and the fix belongs with whoever
gives the engine its first production caller, who will also know whether the
answer is a `try` around the `stat` or a single `os.stat` read.

**Closes when:** the file check reads the path once, or a caller exists that can
reach the window and the decision is recorded that a raw `OSError` is the right
answer there.

**CLOSED 2026-09-19 on `relay/127`, U82, by the first condition.**
`marks.require_output` makes one `os.stat` and answers all three questions from
it, and every `OSError` out of it is the `sync-marks-blocked` refusal. A
`PermissionError` is chained as the cause, so `core.cause` re-slugs it
`path-permission-denied`, which is a declared refusal with the remedy that
works and is asserted. Row `A1_stat_oserror_is_the_refusal` in
`docs/mutation/u82-a.md` kills 4. The same two read shape stands at four other
sites, which is R-485.

## R-399. `crate tag folder` writes genre and no album art, and nothing else in the product writes any

**Found:** 2026-09-18, by a parity audit run against DJ_tools after a user asked
whether Cratekit could replace it for bringing favourites in.

The source system's tagger fetches artwork, re-encodes it to a CDJ compatible
800x800 baseline JPEG, embeds it across FLAC, MP3, AIFF, WAV and M4A, and
repairs already broken picture blocks in place without re-downloading:
`DJ_tagging/tag_new_tracks.py:147-164` builds the JPEG, `:178-214` embeds it,
`:317` and `:329` repair existing art, `:378-395` fetches when art is absent.

`tagging/tag.py:122-148` writes the genre tag and stops. `SearchHit.art` is
declared at `tag.py:50` and no code reads it. `tagging/searchers.py` never
returns art bytes. `core/tags.py` has no picture writer, and a search for
`APIC` or `Picture` over `src/cratekit` outside `_vendor` returns nothing.

**The declaration is live.** `cli/registry.py:907` summarises the verb as "tag a
folder of audio with genre and album art". That is the same shape as R-144's
colour write, a declared half with no implementation behind it.

**It is worse than absent, because the shipped downloader emits the defect the
source system repaired.** `_vendor/tidal_dl_ng/metadata.py:102-109` sets the
picture mime type and never sets width, height or depth, which is the zeroed
PICTURE block Pioneer players render blank. The source system carried a repair
pass for exactly this. Cratekit ships the producer and not the repair.

**Measured cost:** every track acquired through Cratekit reaches the CDJs with
no artwork, and a FLAC acquired through the vendored downloader carries a
malformed picture block that no pass in this product will ever correct. Not
measured on a live library, because no acquisition workflow completes today.

**Why not fixed here.** Found by an audit, not by a unit, and art is a module
sized piece of work: a source, a re-encoder, a per container writer and a
repair pass over already acquired files.

**Closes when:** `tag folder` embeds art on the containers the source system
covered, and a repair pass exists for files already carrying a zeroed block, or
the registry summary stops claiming art.

**Narrowed 2026-09-19 on `relay/128`, U83. The engine exists and no verb calls
it.** `core/art.py` holds the re-encoder and the per container reader and
writer: `to_cdj_jpeg` makes a baseline RGB JPEG under a byte cap, 800 by 800 or
native resolution, `write_front_cover` embeds it in FLAC, MP3, AIFF, WAV and
M4A with the FLAC block's width, height and depth measured by Pillow, and
`read_pictures` reports a zeroed block as zeroes and a progressive picture as
progressive. Driven in `tests/test_art.py` on ffmpeg synthesized containers, 25
of 25 guards killed across `docs/mutation/u83-a.md`, `u83-b.md` and `u83-c.md`.
**Still open, all of what a user sees:** `tag folder` fetches and embeds
nothing (U85), no repair pass runs over files already carrying a zeroed or
progressive block (U84), and the registry summary still claims art. Whether a
Pioneer player renders what this engine writes is unmeasured and owed to an
attended sitting, one file on a real CDJ or XDJ.

**Narrowed 2026-09-19 on `relay/129`, U84. The repair clause is closed.**
`crate tag folder` now repairs art a FLAC already carries, in place and without
the web, on every file it walks, tagged or not. `core/art.py`'s
`repair_in_place` re-encodes any block declaring a zero width, height or depth,
or holding data that is not a baseline JPEG, at native resolution, shrinking
into the 800 pixel box only when the byte cap cannot be met otherwise, and
fills the dimensions from the new bytes. `tagging/tag.py`'s `tag_one` calls it
before the has-genre return, and the status reaches the item artifact as
`art_repair` and the job summary as zero filled counts. Driven in
`tests/test_tagging_engine.py` and `tests/test_tag_workers.py` on the vendored
shape, a zeroed block built with mutagen, and measured in
`docs/mutation/u84-a.md`, `u84-b.md` and `u84-a4.md`. **Still open:** `tag
folder` fetches and embeds nothing for a file with no art (U85), the repair is
FLAC only, which is parity, and the registry summary still claims art. Whether
a Pioneer player renders the repaired block is unmeasured and owed to the same
attended sitting.

**CLOSED 2026-09-19 on `relay/130`, U85.** `crate tag folder` now fetches and
embeds art for a file carrying no picture, so the registry summary at
`cli/registry.py` "tag a folder of audio with genre and album art" is true.
`SearchHit.art`, the bytes field nothing read, is gone and `SearchHit.art_url`
replaces it, carried off the SAME best scored row as the genre: Beatport's
`release.release_image_uri` resized to 1400, Bandcamp's listing image or the
track page's `og:image` at `_10`, and nothing from Traxsource, which is parity.
`tagging/tag.py:tag_one` searches unless a file has both a genre and a picture,
embeds through `core/art.py`'s `to_cdj_jpeg` and `write_front_cover` only when
the file has no picture at all, and reports `art_fetch` as `embedded`,
`present`, `unavailable`, `error` or `unchecked`. A failed fetch or bytes that
are not an image are `unavailable` and never fail the item. The worker binds
`searchers.for_images()` at call time, and the summary counts every status.
Driven against fakes in `tests/test_tagging_engine.py`,
`tests/test_catalogue_searcher.py` and `tests/test_tag_workers.py`, 23 of 25
guards killed across `docs/mutation/u85-a.md` and `u85-b.md`, the two zeros
maintainer facing. **Owed to an attended sitting, and not what closes this:**
one live folder run, because payload drift cannot be seen from fixtures
(R-495), and one file shown on a real CDJ or XDJ.

## R-400. Nothing in the product can produce the list document `acquire download` reads

**Found:** 2026-09-18, by the same parity audit, as the common cause under four
separate workflow gaps.

`acquire download` takes a provider list document or a hand typed text list.
`acquire/match_cli.py:226-266` and `:312-354` read that format. A search for a
producer finds only readers. `docs/cutover.md:111-112` recorded the consequence
for one workflow on 2026-09-16, that the download smoke test used a hand written
document. The audit found it is not one workflow's problem: it is the seam every
acquisition entrance stops at.

The entrances, each of which resolves work and then has nowhere to put it:
`intake set` (R-401), the label sweep and label import (R-402), `sync all`
(R-403), the playlists source (R-359), and the favourites source (issue #110).

**Measured cost:** Cratekit cannot complete any acquisition workflow end to end.
A person can identify, match, resolve, verify and review, and then has to retype
what they want into a text list by hand before a single file downloads. This is
the reason the source system is still the live system, stated more precisely
than `docs/cutover.md` states it.

**Why not fixed here.** Found by an audit. Which surface owns the producer is a
product decision: a shared emitter every source calls, or a document each source
writes. R-359 already carries the narrower version of the same decision for the
playlists source and is on the board as issue #104.

**Closes when:** a verb in this product writes a document `acquire download`
accepts, from work the product itself resolved.

**Narrowed 2026-09-18 on `relay/113`, U68. The engine half is closed and the
verb half is open.** The product decision is made: ONE shared emitter, not a
document per source. `src/cratekit/acquire/listdoc.py` turns rows the product
resolved, `Wanted` tracks or `frozen_tracks` items, into `<name>.list.json`,
which `match_cli.read_list` and `acquire.cli.frozen_tracks` read back to the
same ids in the same order. It also writes a `<name>.manifest.json` provenance
sidecar, since the list's keys are closed. Every listed row is read back through
`match.read_row` before anything is written. A row without a provider id, or
from another service, comes back `unlisted`. A different existing file refuses,
an identical one is a no-op, and no listable row writes nothing. Driven in
`tests/test_listdoc.py`. Mutation table `docs/mutation/u68.md`, 20 of 23
killing, with the zeros read in `docs/mutation/u68-notes.md`. The author's
table, not an independent one. **Still open:** no verb calls `listdoc.write`
yet, so a person still cannot get from a resolved entrance to a download.
That is the entrances' units, R-401 to R-403, R-359 and issue #110.

**Narrowed again 2026-09-18 on `relay/114`, U69. The intake entrance is
closed.** `crate intake missing --job JOB` reads a succeeded intake job's
committed reports with the frozen config and hands only the missing rows to
`listdoc.write`. It writes `intake-JOB.list.json` under
`<download_staging>/lists/`, or under `--out`. It refuses a job of another
verb, a job that is not succeeded, a job with no items, and reports that do
not cover the items one for one by identifier. It also refuses a job whose
missing rows none carry a provider id. The default human output names the
path and the literal `crate acquire download` command. Driven in
`tests/test_intake_missing.py`, including the written list queued and
downloaded by the real download verb against `FakeAdapter`. That covers the
playlist source and the account's hearts, since from U70 both go through
`intake playlist`. Mutation table `docs/mutation/u69.md` and `u69-b.md`, 19 of
20 killing, and the zero is read in `docs/mutation/u69-notes.md`. **Still
open:** a verb that lists from the label sweep, the label import and `sync
all`, which is R-402 and R-403, and from an identified set, R-401, whose
tracks carry no provider id. The one real run, `intake playlist`, then `intake
missing`, then `acquire download` on a small playlist, is owed to an attended
sitting.

## R-401. An identified set cannot be handed to acquisition

**Found:** 2026-09-18, parity audit.

`dj-pipeline full <url>` ran ingest, identify, diff, playlist creation, download
and tag, then spliced the set into the library as its own playlist in play
order: `DJ_setid/setid.py:554-562`, `:248-277`, and
`DJ_setid/setid_lib.py:401-570`.

`crate intake set` identifies and resolves and stops at a per track report of
OWNED, OFFERED and MISSING. `intake/cli.py:21-32` states it: "It does not
acquire ... no intake file is written from an offer", and `:714-756` hardcodes
`"acquired": False`. The collection splice that builds a per batch intake
playlist exists at `intake/ingest.py:207-226` and is reached only by
`pipeline.ingest_file`, whose only caller is `intake_file` under `--export`.

**Measured cost:** a person who identifies a set in Cratekit has a list on
screen and no way to act on it inside the product. The missing tracks are
retyped by hand into a text list. Not measured live; `intake set` has had no
attended sitting.

**Why not fixed here.** Found by an audit. It is R-400's seam reached from the
set door, and composing acquisition spends real downloads, so it is attended.

**Closes when:** a resolved set produces something `acquire download` reads.

**Closed 2026-09-19 on `relay/123`, U78.** `crate intake missing --job JOB`
over a finished `intake set` job now writes the list `acquire download` reads.
Each missing row with no provider id is asked of the catalogue by ISRC through
the new `Catalogue.tracks_for_isrc`, and a row whose ISRC the provider files
under exactly one distinct id is listed with that id. Every other row, no ISRC,
a malformed one, none filed, several filed (R-356), is written to
`intake-JOB.unlisted.json`, a text list `match run` reads, with its reason, and
reported as a failing check. Driven through a real set job over the recognition
fakes and a fake catalogue. What the source system also did and this does not,
the set spliced into the library as its own playlist in play order, is R-475.
**Owed to an attended sitting:** one real set, identified, listed, downloaded
and landed, which is also the first attended sitting `intake set` has had.

## R-402. A label is discovered, verified and reviewed, and never enters the library

**Found:** 2026-09-18, parity audit.

The source system's label workflows ended with the label's releases downloaded,
tagged, spliced into the collection and filed under
`Record Labels / <Label> / <Label> <year>` as one importable file:
`DJ_label/label_batch.py:154-183` downloads, `:185-232` runs the tail,
`:233-249` and `:324-332` produce it, and `DJ_label/label_library.py:1136-1151`
writes the tree.

Both claiming Cratekit verbs stop at the review queue. `label/cli.py:827-830`
says it plainly: "NOTHING IS PRODUCED. The sweep writes no file: it OFFERS into
the review queue ... `LabelSource.acquires` is False, so the increment writes no
intake file." Answering the review changes nothing, because `cli/review.py:426-470`
records a verdict and produces no acquirable output. The tree writer
`write/trees.py:542-597` `insert_record_labels_tree` exists and its only
references in the repository are its definition, its `__all__` entry and three
test files.

**Both scripts, one gap.** `label/cli.py:786-833` serves `sync.labels` and
`label.import` from the same worker.

**Not covered by R-140, which is closed.** R-140 explicitly took the other arm,
recording that "an acquisition recorded only after a review decision ... is not
what landed and is not owed by this entry". `CUT.md` defers only the Tidal
playlist folder script and says of the library import that it "is Feature 22 and
does ship".

**Measured cost:** the label sweep is the workflow with the most live evidence
behind it, 15 of 47 labels swept on 2026-09-17, and none of that work can reach
the library. The review answers a person gives are currently discarded.

**Why not fixed here.** Found by an audit, and it is R-400's seam plus a tree
write, which is two units rather than one.

**Closes when:** an approved label release is acquired and filed under the
record labels tree.

**Narrowed 2026-09-19 on `relay/120`, U75, the acquire half closed.**
`crate label approved` reads every accepted release on the label queue, reads
its tracks again through a new catalogue member, `release_tracks`, resolves each
with the match engine and writes the missing ones through `listdoc.write`, with
a manifest carrying `source` label, `label_id`, `label_name`, `year` and
`release_id`. `acquire download` reads the list, pinned by a test that hands the
written file to `match_cli.read_list`. A review answer is therefore no longer
discarded. Mutation tables `docs/mutation/u75-a.md`, `u75-b.md`, `u75-c.md` and
`u75-zeros.md`, 25 rows, all killing after two tests were written for the zeros,
read in `u75-notes.md`. Landed against fakes: the first live call of
`release_tracks` and the 98 live offered releases are owed to an attended
sitting.

**Still open:** the tree half. Nothing files a landed label track under
`Record Labels / <Label> / <Label> <year>`, and `insert_record_labels_tree`
still has no caller. That is U77, which reads the manifest this unit writes.

**CLOSED 2026-09-19 on `relay/122`, U77, the tree half.**
`crate intake land --manifest M` reads the manifest U75 writes. After the move
and the splice it ties each label row to a landed file with
`match.resolve_one` over `match.index_library` of the batch folder only, and
writes the matched track ids under `<Label> / <Label> <year>` in the catalog
tree, into the same intake file. `insert_record_labels_tree` has its first
caller, through `insert_record_labels_trees`, which writes every label in one
read and one replace. Everything the writer can refuse is asked of a copy
before the first move. An approved label release is therefore acquired by
`acquire download` and filed by the landing, which is what this entry said it
closes on. Landed against fakes. **Owed to an attended sitting:** import one
labelled intake file into rekordbox and read the tree it makes. What the unit
left open is R-455 to R-459.

**Found:** 2026-09-18, parity audit.

The source system's sync produced one importable file and closed with rekordbox
import instructions: `DJ_sync/finalize.py:1-5` and `:41-49`.

Cratekit's composer plans and queues all three sources correctly and each source
stops short: labels offer without acquiring (R-402), playlists resolve without
acquiring (R-359, issue #104), favourites is outbound only (issue #110). The
combined writer is unreachable rather than merely unused: in `sync/run.py:183-199`
`_append_intake` and the watermark sit below an early return taken when a source
declares `acquires` False, and the only caller of `run.increment` in the package
is the labels worker at `label/cli.py:775-783`, which declares exactly that.

`TRACK Name` listing, not a Fresh Export splice" and that U37 owned the real
emitter. U37's emitter landed on the `intake file` path at
`intake/ingest.py:193-226`. `sync/run.py:107-122` still writes the stub, and
that the writer is now unreachable entirely is not recorded anywhere.

**Measured cost:** the orchestrator's product is one file to import, and it
cannot produce one. Live on 2026-09-17 it queued 18 playlists and one labels
job and landed nothing, which was read at the time as the sources being
incomplete rather than the writer being unreachable.

do.

**Closed 2026-09-18 on `relay/118`, U73.** The combined importable file is
`crate intake land --name <run>_synced`, as the brief decided, and not
`run.increment`. What was missing between a pass and that landing was one list
for the whole pass, and `crate intake missing --run RUN_ID` is it,

names the download command and `intake land --export XML --name
<run>_synced`. `crate sync all` ends with one `sync.next` check naming the verb
whenever the pass filed an intake job, driven in the default human output. The

## R-404. No acquisition path exists for a track the configured provider does not carry

**Found:** 2026-09-18, parity audit.

`dj-pipeline fetch-others` searched SoundCloud and then YouTube with `yt-dlp`,
ranked the candidates, wrote a review file for a person to judge, and on
`--apply` downloaded the picks into the same tail as everything else. It was the
one sanctioned lossy exception, marked downstream:
`DJ_setid/fetch_others.py:1-20` and `:33`, registered at `DJ_setid/setid.py:902-909`.

Cratekit has the downstream half and not the act. The lossy marker exists at
`core/naming.py:141` and `:285`. `core/review.py:320-328` declares the
`other_platforms.csv` work queue and states that "the fallback pass reads it and
produces candidates", and no such pass exists. `core/binaries.py:102-104` knows
the `yt-dlp` install hint and nothing invokes it. `acquire/cli.py:548` builds
exactly one adapter from configuration and `:577-578` refuses a track the
adapter did not return.

**Measured cost:** every set holding a bootleg, a white label, an unreleased
promo or anything else absent from the configured provider ends permanently
short, with no route inside the product to close it. Feature 7 is dispositioned
a policy row rather than a module, so nothing about this is deferred by design.

**Why not fixed here.** Found by an audit. Note before taking it that the source
system's queue had no writer either, so a person hand authored the CSV there
too; the gap is the acquisition pass, not the queue.

**Closes when:** a track the configured adapter cannot supply has a route to a
second source that respects the lossless policy's marking rules.

**Narrowed 2026-09-19 on `relay/125`, U80. The search half is closed and the
download half is open.** `crate acquire fallback PATH` reads the unlisted text
list, or any list `match run` reads, resolves every row against the library,
and searches SoundCloud and then YouTube through a `FallbackSearcher` for each
row still missing. The shipped searcher is `acquire/fallback.py`'s
`YtDlpSearcher`, yt-dlp in flat playlist mode through an injectable runner,
which no test runs. Ranked candidates are offered on the `fallback-source`
queue under the kind `fallback-candidate`, one item per row, each option an
upload page URL, and none is picked. A row carrying the provider's own id, or
waiting on or accepted as a provider candidate, is not searched. A second run
searches nothing it already offered. A failed search refuses
`unavailable-transient` naming every item already offered, a missing yt-dlp
refuses `yt-dlp-missing` with the install hint, and no candidate anywhere
refuses rather than reading as nothing to do. Driven in
`tests/test_acquire_fallback.py`, 25 rows in `docs/mutation/u80.md`, all
killed after `u80-b.md`.

What is still open is the act and the marking. An accepted candidate is
reported with its URL and nothing downloads it, so the verb says "nothing in
this build downloads them yet" on every run that holds one. The source
system's `--apply` downloaded bestaudio into the set's download folder with
clean tags from the row, and the lossy marker at `core/naming.py:141` and
`:285` is still the downstream half that download has to reach. The source
system's `URL` column override, a lossless purchase link forced per row, has no
counterpart either.

**Closed 2026-09-19 on `relay/126`, U81.** `crate acquire fallback-fetch
PATH` is the act. It resolves the list through the same helper `acquire
fallback` now calls, `fallback_cli.missing_rows`, and queues one job item per
row whose `fallback-candidate` item a person ACCEPTED with a named upload,
keyed on the review item id, with the row's artist, listed title and the
upload URL frozen in the payload. A row the library holds, a row with a
provider route, and a row waiting, rejected or stalled are not queued. The
worker `handle_fetch` refuses the strict policy per item with `lossy-refused`
before any download, refuses a name already taken with `output-exists` before
the download and again after it, downloads through the `FallbackFetcher` seam
into the item's own `staging_dir`, passes the landing through
`checked_landing`, marks it through `marked_name`, strips every tag the upload
carried with the new `core.tags.strip_tags`, writes artist and title from the
ROW, and commits into the download staging root, so the ordinary tag, name
and land tail picks it up. A missing yt-dlp parks the job. The shipped
`YtDlpFetcher` extracts MP3 at the best variable quality, the source system's
recipe. `acquire fallback` names the new verb where it said nothing downloads
accepted candidates. Driven in `tests/test_acquire_fallback_fetch.py`, 25 rows
in `docs/mutation/u81-fetch-a.md` and `u81-fetch-b.md`, one zero fixed and not
re-measured, read in `u81-fetch-notes.md`. What stays open is filed apart:
R-498, the real download, and R-499, the per row purchase link override.

## R-405. No verb writes a star rating, so a sorted library is an unrated one

**Found:** 2026-09-18, parity audit.

Every source system sort run set a 1, 3 or 5 star rating from the energy value,
on tracks whose rating was still zero, in the same pass as the filing:
`DJ_maintenance/sort_inbox.py:214-218` plans it, `:387-389` and `:448-449` apply
it, and `sort_unplaced.py:173-177` with `:207-208` does the same.

Cratekit holds both halves and calls neither. The planner
`write/metadata.py:413` `plan_rating_backfill` and the byte writer
`write/rbxml.py:1301` `apply_rating_changes` are reached only from
`tests/test_rbxml.py:295` and `tests/test_xml_splice_golden.py:303`. The
claiming verbs write membership and nothing else: `write/routing_cli.py:250-269`
for the inbox and `:362-369` for unplaced.

**R-275 is adjacent and not the same finding.** R-275 records the energy to
rating write having a planner and no worker in the `analyze restamp` context.
Nothing ties the missing rating write to `route.inbox` and `route.unplaced`,
which are the verbs claiming the scripts that performed it. R-275 also does not
record that `plan_rating_backfill` is fill-if-empty by construction, so it
cannot re-spread ratings after a recalibration even once wired, which is the
other half of what the source system's re-rate did.

**Measured cost:** a person who files their library with Cratekit gets every
track placed correctly and every one of them unrated. Not measured live.

**Why not fixed here.** Found by an audit, and a rating write is a guarded
database write behind a gate rather than a wiring change.

**Closes when:** a filing pass writes ratings, and a recalibration can re-spread
ratings it did not originally set.

**Narrowed 2026-09-18 on `relay/132`, U87. The first clause is closed; the
re-spread stays open.** `crate route inbox --export X` now fills the star
rating of every intake track it places whose export `Rating` is empty or
`"0"`, from the energy the routing decision already read, through
`routing.energy_rating` and `routing.rates`, into the same bytes before the
file is written, through `trees.apply_rating_changes`, now its first caller in
`src`. The scale is the export's, which is the taxonomy's own, so R-414's
database scale is not on this path. A rating a person set is never touched, a
`rates = false` bucket is skipped, a track with no energy reading is not
rated, and a row with no `Rating` attribute is not planned since the writer
cannot add one. The rating rides each item, inside the digest the person
approves. A pass that only rates still writes a file, so a filed and unrated
track is not answered `nothing-to-route`. Driven in
`tests/test_routing_workers.py`, 12 tests; mutation tables
`docs/mutation/u87.md`, `u87-b.md`, `u87-c.md`, read in `u87-notes.md`.
`route unplaced` has no export medium and rates nothing, as it files nothing
through one. **Still open:** the second clause. A re-spread after a
recalibration overwrites ratings, which needs a record of which ratings
automation set, and nothing keeps one. Also open, R-441: whether a rekordbox
import carries the rating onto a track already in the collection.

## R-406. The "Sets and Long Tracks" playlist is never built

**Found:** 2026-09-18, parity audit.

`dj-sort-unplaced` collected every collection track longer than 20 minutes and
created a root playlist for them on every run: `sort_unplaced.py:38` sets the
threshold, `:179` collects, `:210-211` writes, and `:76-82` inserts the root
playlist.

Cratekit ported the writer, `write/rbxml.py:1331`, and calls it nowhere outside
`tests/test_rbxml.py:313`. `write/routing_cli.py:362-369` emits identifier and
path items only, and no code under `src/cratekit` reads a track's duration for
any tree.

**Measured cost:** the standing separation between sets and tracks is gone, and
a person mixing from the library meets full length sets in genre playlists with
nothing marking them. Not measured live.

**Why not fixed here.** Found by an audit. It needs a duration read the tree
path does not currently perform.

**Closes when:** a filing pass builds the long track playlist, or the taxonomy
declares it and the tree writers fill it.

**Closed 2026-09-18 on `relay/133`, U88.** `crate route inbox --export X`
adds every collection track whose `TotalTime` is over the declared bound to one
playlist, a direct child of the playlist root, in the same pass and the same
written file as the filing and the ratings. The name and the bound are the
taxonomy's new optional `[long_tracks]` section, shipped as "Sets and Long
Tracks" over 1200 seconds, the source system's values, and the bound is strict
as `sort_unplaced.py:179` is. `TotalTime` was confirmed as seconds on the
fixture and on this project's own emitter. The write is
`trees.add_to_root_playlist`, which calls `rbxml.insert_root_playlist` once,
now its first caller in `src`, with the members the playlist already held
written back ahead of the new ones. A row with no readable length is counted
in `totals.duration_unreadable` and never guessed. A same named playlist inside
a folder is neither read nor touched; a FOLDER of that name at the root is a
`route-write-skipped` warning and is left alone. The source system rebuilt the
playlist on every run; this pass only adds, which R-442 records. Owed to an
attended sitting: the playlist seen in rekordbox after one import.

## R-407. `crate name apply` renames library files without consulting the collection

**Found:** 2026-09-18, parity audit. **This is a hazard rather than a missing
capability, and it is the only finding in this block that can lose data.**

`dj-path-repair` refused to rename any file the collection already referenced,
and said so per file: `DJ_maintenance/path_repair.py:225-227` tests the location
attribute against the export's bytes and prints `imported-do-not-touch`.

`name.apply` has no such check. `write/naming_cli.py:144` defaults its root to
`cfg.library.root` when `--root` is omitted, `:102-109` walks that root with
`rglob`, and `:152-171` renames every file whose rendered name differs and then
writes tags. The module opens no database: a search for database, collection or
splice access in `write/naming_cli.py` returns nothing.

**The guard and the rename ended up in different verbs.** `repair paths`, which
claims `dj-path-repair`, only queues proposals at `intake/repair_cli.py:44-58`.
The verb that renames is the one without the guard.

**Measured cost:** unmeasured, and the exposure is the whole library. Run
against a library whose files rekordbox has imported, this renames them and
leaves every affected collection row pointing at a path that no longer exists.
The author's library carries 9937 collection rows. A gate does stand in front of
the write and the plan lists each rename, so a person who reads the plan can
abort, but the plan states old and new filenames and says nothing about which
files the collection references, which is the fact that decides whether the
operation is safe.

**Why not fixed here.** Found by an audit rather than a unit. The fix is a read
of the collection on the rename path plus a refusal, which is a guarded surface
change, and the alternative fix of re-pointing rows after a rename is a larger
product decision.

**Closes when:** `name apply` refuses to rename a file the collection
references, or re-points the row in the same guarded session.

**Closed 2026-09-18 on `relay/112`, U67.** The first branch of the closing
condition, refuse. `_plan_for` reads the collection through a read only open
and splits the candidates into `rename` items and `referenced` items, both in
the digest, with `totals.referenced`. `name_apply` reads the collection again
after the gate and re-checks each item just before `path.rename`, so a row
rekordbox adds while the gate waits still protects its file. A row counts by
its path as recorded and by its prefix mapped path, NFC normalised and
casefolded, and a tombstoned row counts. A candidate matches by its absolute
or its resolved spelling. The check runs for every `--root`. A collection that
cannot be read refuses as `collection-unreadable` carrying the inner cause and
its remedy; there is no force flag. The read is skipped when nothing would be
renamed, because the collection cannot change that outcome and the
conformance suite drives this verb over a library with no database. Mutation
tables `docs/mutation/u67.md` and `docs/mutation/u67-round-2.md`, 21 rows,
every row killed once the round two collision test and composite landed. The
author's table, not an independent one. **Owed to an attended sitting:** one
plan only run against the live library to read the `referenced` count.

## R-408. The size guard that kept live sets out of vocal scoring is gone

**Found:** 2026-09-18, parity audit. Not driven, so the claim is that the guard
is absent, not that a crash was observed.

The source system stat'ed every file, tagged anything over 250 MB as `voxlevel`
zero and never handed it to the model, because loading one hung or exhausted the
worker: `DJ_analysis/vocal_restamp.py:92-101` with `DJ_analysis/vocal_detect.py:39-48`.

Cratekit has no size check on either path. `analysis/vocal.py:66-72` decodes the
whole file at 32 kHz float32 in a pool whose worker budget is 1 GiB
(`analysis/vocals.py:35-36`), and `vocals/cli.py:286-300` skips nothing. Chunked
inference bounds the forward pass and not the decode.

**Measured cost:** unmeasured. It bites only folders holding full length sets or
mixes, and the author's library holds both.

**Why not fixed here.** Found by an audit, and reproducing it costs a real
scoring run over a large file.

**Closes when:** a file too large to decode is refused or short circuited rather
than handed to the decoder.

**NARROWED AND HALF CLOSED, U92, issue #137, `relay/137`, 2026-09-20.** The
VOCAL half is closed. `analysis/vocals.VOCAL_MAX_BYTES` is the source system's
250 mebibytes, `is_oversize` is a stat and a comparison, and the guard sits in
`vocals.analyse` ahead of both the model load and the decoder, so `analyze
vocals` and the vocal stage of `analyze run` refuse the file with a fifth named
reason, `vocal-audio-too-large`. It is NOT tagged `voxlevel` zero the way the
source system tagged it, because a zero in this package means the model heard
the track, so the refusal is an absence with a name instead.

**What is still open is the LIGHT half, and it is now R-583.** This entry said
"no size check on either path" and only one path is guarded. `analysis/detect.py`
decodes the whole file before the vocal pass is reached on `analyze run`, so the

`analyze vocals` and false of `analyze run`. Read this entry as closed for the
vocal decoder and read R-583 for the rest.

## R-409. `analyze restamp` and `analyze calibrate` read one folder, so no library-wide pass exists

**Found:** 2026-09-18, parity audit.

The source system walked the whole library in one command:
`DJ_analysis/energy_calibrate.py:44-47` recurses under the processed tracks
directory, and `energy_restamp.py:99` and `vocal_restamp.py:82` use it.

Cratekit's item set is one level of one folder, `analysis/cli.py:126-144`, used
by calibrate at `:916` and restamp at `:629`.

**R-376 records this for the vocals verb only.** The same shape on restamp and
calibrate is not recorded. Calibrate is the worse half: a threshold or a decile
fit taken over one genre folder is not the library's distribution, so the
numbers it writes are wrong in a way a person cannot see, where restamp is
merely laborious. The author's library holds 343 leaf folders.

**Measured cost:** a back catalogue restamp is 343 invocations, and a
calibration run the honest way is the same. A calibration run the convenient
way, over one folder, silently fits the wrong population.

**Why not fixed here.** Found by an audit. Whether a recursive mode belongs on
the verb or in the job engine is a design question, and R-376 covers the third
verb, so the three should move together.

**Closes when:** a library-wide analysis pass exists, or calibrate refuses a
sample it cannot treat as representative.

**NARROWED 2026-09-20 on `relay/138`, U93, to the calibrate half.** `analyze
restamp` now takes `--recursive` and queues a whole tree as one resumable job,
so the restamp half of this entry is closed with R-376. What is still open is
the half this entry itself calls the worse one: `analyze calibrate` still reads
`_audio_in` at one level, `analysis/cli.py`, and a decile fit or a vocal cut
taken over one genre folder is still not the library's distribution. U93
deliberately left it alone rather than giving calibrate the same flag, because
a recursive calibrate that a person can ask for is not the same answer as a
calibrate that refuses an unrepresentative sample, and choosing between those is
U94's. Until U94 lands, the convenient way to calibrate still silently fits the
wrong population.

**CLOSED 2026-09-20 on `relay/139`, U94, on its second arm: calibrate refuses a
sample it cannot treat as representative.** `analyze calibrate` takes
`--recursive`, `--sample N`, default 500, and `--accept-partial`, and a new
check row, `calibrate.sample`, answers before anything is measured. The only
walk it treats as the library is the library root, or the music folder under
it, walked recursively with nothing left out. One genre folder, the root read
one level deep, a recursive walk of a subtree, and a root walk that declined a
linked folder or could not list one all fail the row and write nothing. With
`--accept-partial` the fit goes ahead, the row reads skipped and not ok, the
envelope carries `calibration-partial-sample`, and the note in both files says
`fitted over N of M under ROOT` and how many folders were not walked. The
energy half measures an even stride over the sorted walk, so the same tree
gives the same sample, and the vocal half reads every tagged file.

Two readings stricter than the brief, both deliberate. The brief refused "a
folder that is not the library root" when `--recursive` is absent and was silent
on the root read one level deep and on `--recursive` over a subtree. Both are
partial here, because one level of a root that holds genre folders is only its
loose files and a recursive walk of one genre is still one genre. And one
reading wider: the brief named the root alone, and every module that places a
track places it under `root / music_dir`, so that folder qualifies too.

The first arm, a library wide PASS for calibrate as a resumable job, is not
built and is out of U94's scope by the brief. What that leaves is R-602.

## R-410. `crate setbuild` cannot anchor on a track the library does not own

**CLOSED 2026-09-21, by U98 on `relay/143`.** The closing condition is met: an
anchor outside the library is accepted with a supplied key.
`crate setbuild --unowned LABEL --key 8A [--bpm N]` resolves the label through
the engine's `resolve_anchor` against an EMPTY index, so no fuzzy owned match
can happen, and the envelope's anchor carries `owned` false and
`key_needs_confirming` true. The key is required and parsed at the parser, so a
code off the wheel is a status 2 and a missing one refuses as
`setbuild-unowned-key-missing`. `--bpm` is a ranking input only and nothing is
written. A key or tempo beside a path anchor refuses as
`setbuild-supplied-needs-unowned` rather than being ignored. No web lookup.

**Two things were found closing it that the finding above does not say.**

1. With an unowned anchor, a label naming an owned track exactly came back with
   the library's own copy as its best companion, at the perfect key tier. The
   owned form drops a copy by match key inside `build_pool`, and an unowned
   anchor has no track to carry that key. `plan_for` now drops exact match key
   copies and reports their paths as `totals.held`. Only exact, R-621 is what
   that leaves.
2. `build_plan` placed an `either` companion on BOTH sides of the anchor, so one
   same-key companion of equal energy was the whole sequence twice, its only
   position 2. That was on main for owned anchors; an unowned anchor, whose
   companions are nearly all `either`, hit it on most runs. The after side now
   draws from what the before side left, pinned through `plan_for` and
   `build_set`.

**Original finding, kept as written:**

**Found:** 2026-09-18, parity audit.

The source system took a provider identifier or URL as the anchor and accepted a
hand supplied Camelot key, which is the "should I buy this" workflow the
operator skill documents: `DJ_setbuilder/cli.py:86` and `:89`.

Cratekit accepts only a path under the library, `setbuilder/cli.py:117-120`, and
refuses anything absent from the index at `:321-332`. The engine still supports
both, `modules/tools/setbuilder.py:725` `resolve_anchor`, and nothing reaches
it. The verb's docstring at `setbuilder/cli.py:17-23` states the cost, so this
is a known decision rather than an oversight, and the capability exists in no
other shape.

**R-187 and R-188 are not this.** They cover the fuzzy lookup and the missing
cache.

**Measured cost:** the workflow that decides a purchase is unavailable. Lowest
impact of this block, because the set building it blocks is speculative rather
than something the library already contains.

**Why not fixed here.** Found by an audit, and the refusal is deliberate, so
reversing it is a product decision rather than a repair.

**Closes when:** an anchor outside the library is accepted with a supplied key,
or the decision to require ownership is recorded as final.

## R-413. An acquired file cannot leave download staging, so no batch of downloads becomes an importable file

**Found:** 2026-09-18, by two independent reads made while planning the close of
R-400, one designing the acquisition seam and one checking the parity audit for
what it missed. Read, not driven.

`acquire download` commits each file to the staging root,
`acquire/cli.py:545-549` and `:602-618`. `intake/ingest.py:58-70` `place_files`
refuses any path under staging, and its only caller is `pipeline.ingest_file`
with one path, reached only from `intake file --export`, `intake/cli.py:623-639`.
Nothing in `src` moves a file out of staging: the only renames are same
directory, `write/naming_cli.py:150-167` and `analysis/cli.py:523`.
`core/config.py:2188-2194` describes staging as "where fresh downloads land
before they are moved into the library", and `processed_dir` at `:2176` has no
consumer. `docs/GUIDE.md:143-155` tells a person to tag and name in staging and
never says how the files reach an intake file.

The source system's pipeline stages 7 to 11 moved a batch into the library and
spliced the folder into one importable file.

**Why it matters more than its size.** R-400 reads as the last seam. It is the
second to last. With a list document produced and downloaded, the files still
sit where ownership cannot see them, `acquire/match_cli.py:846-863` walks
`library.root / music_dir` only, so a downloaded track reads as missing on the
next pass and is offered for download again.

**Measured cost:** not measured live, because no acquisition workflow completes
today. Every acquisition entrance ends here once R-400 closes.

**Why not fixed here.** Found while planning. It is an engine and a gated verb,
two units.

**Closes when:** a shipped verb moves a staged batch under the library and
writes one intake file naming every moved track.

**Narrowed 2026-09-18 on `relay/116`, U71. The engine half is closed and the
verb half is open.** `src/cratekit/intake/landing.py` does the move. `plan`
lists a staging folder one level deep, audio only, skipping dotfiles and the
unfinished download directory, and fingerprints each item by name, size and
modification time. `apply` lists the folder again and refuses a stale
fingerprint as `decision-stale`. Then, before any file moves, it refuses:
- an absent library root
- a source folder inside the library that is not staging
- a target under staging
- a staging folder on another device, by name and never copied
- an existing intake file
- every export refusal `place_files` can make, tried on a copy

A file with no declared sub is left in staging with a sentence naming `crate
tag folder`. Driven, the shipped taxonomy never produces that, because an
untagged file lands in `electronica_other` / `unsorted`. Moves are `os.replace`
only. A file whose target exists is refused alone and never replaced, and the
rest land. `place_files` then runs over the moved paths, so no Location is
stamped from staging. A failure after the first move names the moved files,
which stay in the library, and leaves no intake file and no empty batch folder.
Driven in `tests/test_landing.py` against real tagged FLAC containers. Mutation
tables `docs/mutation/u71.md`, `u71-b.md` and `u71-c.md`, 25 rows, all killing
after one test was strengthened, read in `docs/mutation/u71-notes.md`. This is
the author's table, not an independent one. **Still open:** no verb calls
`landing.apply`, so a person still cannot land a downloaded batch. That is the
verb unit. R-432, R-433 and R-434 are what the engine leaves for it.

**Closed 2026-09-18 on `relay/117`, U72.** `crate intake land [FOLDER]
--export XML [--name NAME]`, `src/cratekit/intake/land_cli.py`, registry entry
`intake.land`, `plan/1`, one confirm gate `intake.land.confirm` with apply and
abort and `digest_source="plan"`. The folder defaults to download staging and
the batch name to the run id without its colons. The intake file is
`library.root / NAME_inboxed.xml`. The first run stops at the gate with the
files, the batch folder and the intake file on the gate screen, and moves
nothing. The digest covers the folder, the batch, the target, the intake file,
the export and the engine's fingerprint, so a recorded answer is stale for any
other plan. An answered run lands through `landing.apply` and ends PENDING with
a `rekordbox_import` action naming the intake file, verified by
`route.pending`, blocking nothing. A file the engine refused is a warning. An
empty folder is a plan of nothing and a NO_OP, on the `name apply` and `route
inbox` precedent, because conformance 3 drives every gated verb to OK on an
empty library. Driven in `tests/test_intake_land.py` through `cli.run` in both
output modes against real tagged FLAC containers. GUIDE's acquisition
walkthrough names the step. Mutation tables `docs/mutation/u72.md` and
`u72-b.md`, 24 rows, all killing, the author's own. Owed to an attended
sitting: one real staged batch landed and its intake file imported into
rekordbox, which is the same sitting U71 owes.

## R-414. The rating planner puts an export scale value into a database field

**Found:** 2026-09-18, reading `write/metadata.py` to plan the close of R-405.
Read, not driven, and the database scale is unconfirmed.

The shipped taxonomy's rating cuts are on the export scale, 51 to 255,
`templates/taxonomy.default.toml:99-105`. `plan_rating_backfill`,
`write/metadata.py:434-441`, puts `cut.rating` straight into a database `Rating`
change, and `tests/test_metadata_policy.py:128-132` asserts `row.Rating == 255`.
A rekordbox export spells five stars 255. The database is believed to store 0
to 5. If that is right, the first verb to drive this planner writes 255 into a
field that holds 5, and the test that should catch it pins the wrong number,
which is METHOD's fourth defect pattern, a measurement taken on a fixture.

**Measured cost:** none today, since the planner has no caller. It is the
entry condition for whoever binds it.

**Why not fixed here.** The scale needs one read of a real database on a
disposable copy, which is attended.

**Closes when:** the database scale is read off a real library and the planner
and its test agree with it, or ratings are written through the export medium
only, where the taxonomy's scale is already the right one.

**Read 2026-09-24 at the eleventh attended sitting, A4, issue #177, and
narrowed to its planner half.** The live database was copied once, rekordbox
and rekordboxAgent both gone, from the configured library database, the path
`rb_writer.live_db_path` resolves, with its wal and shm sidecars into a fresh
temporary directory, 281,153,536 bytes, and the copy was opened through `rb_writer.open_db` from the attended
worktree at `a5b30cf`. The distinct `Rating` values on the rows not soft
deleted, with their counts: 0 on 539, 1 on 1,659, 2 on 996, 3 on 2,994, 4 on
1,434, 5 on 2,376. Six values, 0 to 5, and no 51, 102, 153, 204 or 255
anywhere. **The database stores stars.** The belief above is confirmed, so
`plan_rating_backfill` would write 255 into a field whose largest value is 5,
and `tests/test_metadata_policy.py` pins that wrong number. The second arm of
the closing condition is gone since R-688: an export cannot rate an owned row,
so the database path is the only one that can land a rating, and the planner
has to agree with the scale before #212 applies one. **What remains is the
planner and its test on the 0 to 5 scale**, filed for the feeder as this
residual's own card. The taxonomy's cut values stay on the export scale for
the export writer, and where the conversion lives is that card's decision.
The live file was not opened and the copy was deleted after the read.

**CLOSED 2026-09-24 on `relay/214`, issue #214, the planner half.** The
closing condition's first arm holds: the scale was read off a real library
above, and the planner and its test now agree with it.
`write/metadata.py` gains `database_stars` beside `rating_for`, the one home
of the conversion. It folds 51, 102, 153, 204 and 255 to one through five,

`tests/test_metadata_policy.py` pins star 5 where it pinned 255, reads the

scale and over a mixed curve. Mutation table `docs/mutation/r414.md`,

lookups of one curve disagree above the last cut), and R-711 (the provider
gate's two process timing test fails under load).

## R-422. Identification alone reports owned tracks as missing, drops the tracklist, and pays for recognition twice

**Found:** 2026-09-18, completeness check. Read, not driven.

`intake/cli.py:515-530` with `intake/pipeline.py:53-66`: the identify only path
never consults the library, so every identified row is reported missing, and the
tracklist text is computed and dropped. `intake/acrcloud.py` keeps no cache of a
recognition result, so `intake identify` followed by `intake set` over the same
recording pays for every chunk twice. R-304 records that the spend is not
resumable and does not record the cache.

**Measured cost:** a false "missing" on every owned track in an identified set,
and doubled recognition spend on the ordinary two step use.

**Closes when:** identify consults the library and writes its tracklist, and a
second pass over an unchanged recording spends nothing.

**CLOSED 2026-09-19 on `relay/148`, U103.** The (read) line was confirmed in
plan mode before anything was built on it. All three halves are closed and
each is driven in `tests/intake/test_workers.py` through the real dispatcher.
(1) `intake identify` resolves its rows through `match_cli.resolve_list`, the
body of `match_list` lifted out and called by both verbs, so an owned track is
`matched`, a version the library may hold is offered to the review queue under
the verb's own key and reported `needs_review`, and an open question is a
pending action exactly as it is for `match run`. The registry entry is
`adjudicates` and its doctor checks gain `library.mounted`. (2) The tracklist
is written as `<stem>-<twelve digest characters>.tracklist.txt` into `--out`,
defaulting to `tracklists` under download staging, and `match_cli.read_list`
reads it back row for row. `match/1` is closed at three arrays, so the path
rides a `tracklist-written` note on the warnings channel. (3) Recognition
answers are kept at the transport boundary in the new declared state entry
`identify_cache`, one document per recording, named by a sha256 over the
recording's bytes and the whole chunk plan, offsets, chunk length, interval,
sample rate and host. Only a match or a miss is kept, in both directions, so a
chunk that got no answer is paid for again and nothing else is. The second of
identify then set makes zero transport calls, writes nothing to the ledger and
never retrieves a credential, and a changed file, a changed plan or another
host misses. `--refresh` on both verbs pays for every chunk again, and a pass
that read kept answers says how many on a `recognition-cached` note. The code
review raised ten findings and eight were applied, among them an absent music
folder refused BEFORE the spend (its empty index had reproduced this entry's
own false "missing" by unplugging a drive) and a tracklist named by stem alone
that a recorder calling every set REC001 would have overwritten. Mutation
tables `docs/mutation/u103-a.md` and `u103-b.md`, 25 of 25 killing, the
author's tables and not independent ones; table a's one first pass zero got a
test and was re-run killing. R-512, R-513 and R-514 are what this unit found
and did not fix. **Owed to an attended sitting:** one real identify then set
over a real recording, which is where the second pass is shown to cost nothing
on the account's own counter and where the kept raw answers meet a real
answer's shape.

## R-425. `name apply` over a library with cloud sync on exits as unreadable rather than as an external writer

**Found:** 2026-09-18, U67's review, driven by
`tests/test_naming_apply_cli.py::test_a_library_with_cloud_sync_on_refuses_and_names_the_real_cause`.

The collection read goes through `rb_writer.open_db` with `require_closed`
False, and its canary still refuses a library whose cloud sync is ON as
`cloud-sync-active`. `write/naming_cli._recorded` wraps every failed read as
`collection-unreadable`, so the process exits 25, `LIBRARY_UNREADABLE`, where
the inner cause alone would have exited as `EXTERNAL_WRITER`. The message
carries the inner cause's words and the remedy is `disable-cloud-sync`, so a
person is told the right act; a script branching on the exit code is not.

**The decision taken here, conservatively.** Sync on still refuses, the same
refusal every other collection reader makes. Whether a read with sync on
should block renames at all, and whether the outer slug should yield to a
more specific inner one, is a person's call.

**Measured cost:** exit code only. Nothing is renamed and the words are true.

**Closes when:** the refusal's exit code agrees with its inner cause for the
cloud sync case, or a person decides the folded code is the contract.

## R-428. A list written from frozen download items re-reads as the plain record

**Found:** 2026-09-18, U68, by the unit's `/code-review`, driven.

`listdoc.rows_of` accepts `acquire.cli.frozen_tracks` output as well as `Wanted`
tracks. The freeze keeps only the split title, the artist and the ISRC. It drops
the version, the key and the source's own spelling. A list written from a
frozen mapping therefore freezes back identically, which is all `acquire
download` reads, and re-reads to the PLAIN record for anything that matches or
tombstones by title. A provider row for `Sun Path (feat. Mira)`, version
`Extended Mix`, key 8A, is written as `Sun Path` with no version and no key.
`test_a_frozen_mapping_carries_no_version_so_none_is_written` pins the
behaviour and the `rows_of` docstring says so.

**Measured cost:** none today, since no caller writes from frozen items. A
future caller that did, and then handed that list to `match run`, would ask
about a different recording from the one the provider listed.

**Why not fixed here.** The emitter cannot write fields the freeze discarded,
and the brief asks for the frozen input. Widening the freeze changes what
`acquire download` queues, which is outside this unit.

**Closes when:** the frozen input is removed from `rows_of`, or the freeze
carries the version, key and spelling through.
