## R-431. A deleted track the tombstone consult cannot reach is listed for download

**Found:** 2026-09-18, U69, driven. The brief named the class: R-69, R-71 and
R-72 each record a shape where the match engine reports a track plain missing
when it should not. That was minor while missing led nowhere. `crate intake
missing` makes missing lead to `acquire download`.

**Driven.** A tombstone recorded by the real recorder,
`deletion.stores.record_tombstone`, for `Aurora Bloom - Sun Path (feat. Mira)
(Nightwave Remix)`, and one heart the provider spells as title `Sun Path` and
version `Nightwave Remix`. `intake playlist favorites` resolves the heart
missing, not suppressed, and `intake missing` writes it to the list.
`test_a_deleted_track_the_tombstone_consult_cannot_reach_is_listed_as_recorded`
in `tests/test_intake_missing.py` pins exactly that, so the test fails on the
day this closes. The shape is the one entry in `UNRECONCILED` in
`tests/test_match_states.py`. A deletion the consult does reach, a plain
`Lumen Drift - Salt Road`, resolves suppressed and is not listed, driven in
`test_a_track_deleted_on_purpose_is_suppressed_and_not_listed`.

**Measured cost:** a track a person deleted on purpose is written into a list
whose next command downloads it, and the report counts it as missing, not as
deleted. That is board bar (b), the product saying something false. It is
(a) as well, since a later run re-acquires a file the person removed. Only
the R-69 shape was driven. R-72's unenumerated dash shapes and R-71's
index side miss, where an owned file is reported missing and would be
downloaded twice, are the same cost by the same path, argued from their
entries and not driven here.

**Why not fixed here.** Excluding it at this verb would need a second
tombstone consult wider than the engine's, and `tombstone_fold` rejects
widening by name, since an over eager suppression silently withholds music
somebody wants. The fix belongs to whoever owns the tombstone identity, as
R-69 and R-72 already say.

**Closes when:** the deletion pass records a normalized identity the provider
side can reach, R-72's closing condition, which also retires R-69's
`UNRECONCILED` entry. Or `intake missing` gains a review step that offers
each missing row sharing an artist and recording with a tombstone rather
than listing it.

**CLOSED 2026-09-19 on `relay/179`, by the first of the two.** The second was
weighed and not taken: `intake missing` only reads the states `intake playlist`
committed, so a review step at the list verb would have left the intake report
itself saying missing, which is the false statement this entry is about.

`deletion.stores.record_tombstone` now writes a COMPANION beside the tombstone
of any row whose composed title carries a bracketed credit: the same identity
with the credit groups taken out by `core.tombstone.uncredited_title`, under a
kind of its own, `version-uncredited`. `match.standing_tombstone` asks under
that kind second, through `Wanted.uncredited_spellings`. Driven end to end with
the real recorder: the heart spelled `Sun Path` and `Nightwave Remix` resolves
SUPPRESSED at `intake playlist`, and `intake missing` writes no list. The pin
flipped and was renamed
`test_a_deleted_track_whose_row_kept_a_credit_is_suppressed_and_not_listed`.
`UNRECONCILED` is empty, and
`test_the_verbatim_consult_alone_still_misses_the_credited_row` pins that the
verbatim consult did NOT widen to get there.

**It widens nothing the engine did not already call one version, measured.**
While the credited row is held, the listing that spelled no guest resolves
`matched`, `exact`, because a credit names a performer and comes off the
matching title. `test_the_companion_reaches_exactly_what_ownership_reached`
drives both sides of the deletion.

**What keeps it out of the over eager direction, each guard removable alone and
each killing in `docs/mutation/r431-a.md` and `r431-b.md`, 25 of 25.** A row
with no credit writes no companion, so a deletion of the plain record withholds
nothing. The companion has its own kind, so the label sweep,
`suppressed_version` and `tombstone_predicate` cannot land on it. And "this
listing spelled no credit" has to be something the `Wanted` saw: one that
spelled a bracketed credit, one built by hand, which the verb builds from a
held file whose credits the index already took off, and one whose provider row
billed more than one artist all ask nothing. That last field travels through
the intake freeze, and a payload frozen before it existed reads as billed.

**Revocable stays true of a deletion that is two records.** Recording is one
store write and so is lifting, through `DecisionStore.record(beside=)` and
`DecisionStore.revoke(also=)`, because the deletion pass puts the file back
when the record raises. Two deleted rows crediting two guests share one
companion, and it stays until the last of them is lifted, decided by a pointer
on each tombstone first and by stripping second.

**The identity stamp did not move.** `uncredited_version_of` sits on top of
`version_of` and is not reachable from it, so `is2_5b356bbb451de9cc` still
holds and no record this build wrote falls to the row lookup.

**The code review raised ten findings.** Eight held and were fixed, among them
the two writes, the lift decided outside the lock, and the three consult
guards above. Two are recorded, R-517 and R-518. What the guards cost is R-519,
and R-71's index side and R-72's unenumerated shapes stay open as they were,
argued here and not driven.

## R-432. The landing engine checks a target is free and then replaces it, and a file can arrive between the two

**Found:** 2026-09-18, by the `/code-review` of U71 on `relay/116`. Read, and
the window was driven only with a substituted `os.replace`.

`intake/landing.py` refuses a file whose target under `Music/<batch>` already
exists. It asks that question twice, once before the batch folder is made and
again just before each move. Then it moves with `os.replace`, which replaces
an existing target without a word. A file that reaches the same name between
the second check and the rename is overwritten. Only a second writer into the
same batch folder at the same moment can do that, for example two landings of
different staging folders under one batch name.

`os.link` followed by an unlink would refuse atomically, but the library
volume this product targets is commonly exFAT, which has no hard links. The
platform's exclusive rename is not exposed by Python's standard library.

**Measured cost:** none today, because no verb calls the engine. The re-check
at the move is pinned by
`test_a_file_arriving_between_the_passes_is_not_replaced`. The window after it
is not measured.

**Why not fixed here.** The fix is a lock that one landing holds over the
batch folder, and where that lock lives is the verb's choice, since the verb
owns the job and its resume.

**Closes when:** the verb that calls `landing.apply` holds a per batch lock
across the moves, or the move uses an exclusive rename where the volume
supports one.

**Reachable since 2026-09-18, `relay/117`, U72.** `crate intake land` calls
`landing.apply` and holds no lock, so the window is now a shipped verb's. It is
narrowed and not closed: the batch name defaults to the run id, unique per run,
so two landings meet in one batch folder only when a person passes the same
`--name` to both and both reach their moves at the same moment. The same window
covers the intake file, which the engine checks absent before the first move and
`place_files` then writes with a plain overwrite. Still not measured. It meets the
board bar, since a landed file can be overwritten, and is issue #180.

**CLOSED 2026-09-19 on `relay/180`, by the first of the two.** `crate intake
land` holds `landing.batch_lock` across the whole of `landing.apply`, one lock
per batch name, exclusive and non blocking, so a second landing under a held
name is refused as `job-driver-held` with nothing moved, the batch and the
holder named, and two steps: wait and run again, or take another `--name`,
because a first landing that succeeds keeps the name through its intake file.
The lock files sit under a new installation scoped state entry,
`landing_locks`, on the local state disk and never the library volume. The
primitive is `jobs.driver_lock`, never unlinked, released by the kernel when
its holder dies, which a test drives with a holder in a second process that is
killed. The key is a digest of the casefolded, normalized name, so two
spellings of one folder share a lock. The plan and the gate screen take no
lock. The window itself was still not measured: what is measured is that the
second landing never reaches it. Mutation tables `docs/mutation/r432-a.md` and
`r432-b.md`. What the lock does not hold is R-534 and R-535.

## R-433. `place_files` leaves its intake session record open, on success and on every refusal after it opens

**Found:** 2026-09-18, by U71 reading the failure paths of `place_files` as
its first multi file caller. Read, not driven.

`intake/ingest.py` `place_files` calls `session.open_session` before the per
file placement refusal and the playlist refusal, and never calls
`close_session` or `routing_pass.close_run`. So every call leaves an `OPEN`
intake record, and a refused call leaves one with no routing intents. The
landing engine makes both of those refusals before any move, on a copy of the
export and from each file's tags, so through landing they are reached only if
the tags change between the check and the splice.

**Measured cost:** none found. A search of `src` for readers of
`SessionState.OPEN` outside `core/session.py` found none, so an open intake
record blocks nothing today. It is debris in the session directory, and it is
a record that says a run is in progress when it is not.

**Why not fixed here.** `ingest.py` is outside this unit's files, and the
single file caller has the same shape.

**Closes when:** `place_files` closes the session it opened, through
`routing_pass.close_run` on success and as refused on a refusal, or opens
it only after its last refusal.

**Corrected 2026-09-19 in the attended worktree, sweep finding 117.1.** The
search above missed a reader. `core/tree_registry.py` `assert_cutover_ready`
asks `not record.terminal` and refuses `cutover-open-run` on exactly this
record, driven. R-501 carries the cost.

**CLOSED 2026-09-19 on `relay/182`, by neither half of the closing line as
written, and the reason is worth keeping.** The first half, close through
`routing_pass.close_run` on success, cannot be done: `place_files` has just
recorded the run's deferred placements, and the gated close refuses a run that
holds one. So the session ends the call `awaiting-import`, which is not open and
is the state the record should always have been in, with the pending action
persisted on it. On a refusal the session is opened after the last refusal that
needs none, and any failure after the open abandons it through the ungated
close and removes the intake file when this call made it. Both driven, in
`tests/test_intake_imported.py`. R-501 has the whole design.

## R-434. A landed batch marks no file lossy, whatever its name says

**Found:** 2026-09-18, by U71. Read, not driven.

`place_files` takes one `lossy` flag for the whole batch, and it decides
whether the rekordbox Name carries the configured lossy marker.
`landing.apply` passes the default, False. `acquire download` puts the marker
in a lossy file's filename, in `acquire/cli.py` `marked_name`, but
`ingest.read_meta` builds the Name from the title tag and the flag, not from
the filename. So a lossy file landed through the engine may reach rekordbox
without the marker a person relies on to see it is lossy.

**Measured cost:** not measured. Whether an acquired lossy file's title tag
already carries the marker was not driven.

**Why not fixed here.** A batch can mix lossy and lossless files, so the fix
is a per file flag in `place_files`, and `ingest.py` is outside this unit's
files.

**Closes when:** a lossy file landed through the engine is driven to a Name
carrying the marker, or `place_files` takes the flag per file.

## R-436. A landed batch names `route pending` as its import check, and on a library with no database native tree that verb answers OK without reading anything

**Found:** 2026-09-18, by U72 on `relay/117`, choosing the pending action's
`verify_verb`. Read, not driven.

`crate intake land` ends with a `rekordbox_import` pending action whose
`verify_verb` is `route.pending`, the choice the brief made, because that verb
closes the intake session `place_files` opens once the session's routing intents
settle, `write/routing_cli.py` `_close_if_settled`. But `route_pending` returns
OK before it opens anything when no tree is database native,
`write/routing_cli.py:503-507`, and every library is in that state until a tree
is cut over, which is U29 and attended. So before cutover the verb named as the
proof of an import answers OK whether or not the import happened, and the intake
session stays open.

**Measured cost:** not measured. Whether any surface reads a pending action's
`verify_verb` and treats its OK as the action done was not traced. The human
output prints the verb name as `verify: route.pending`, driven.

**Why not fixed here.** `route pending`'s semantics before cutover are U19's
and U29's, and the brief fixed the verify verb unless an established import
check existed. None does, `core/session.py` `pending_import` takes the verb as
a parameter.

**Closes when:** an import check exists that reads the collection for the
landed Locations and the pending action names it, or `route pending` refuses or
says so when no tree is database native.

**CLOSED 2026-09-19 on `relay/182`, by both halves.** `crate intake imported`
reads a Fresh Export for every Location the run recorded in the routing ledger,
compared by `routing_pass.track_id`, and a landing's pending action names it as
the `verify_verb`. `route pending` with no database native tree is now a no-op
carrying a `no-native-tree` warning that says nothing was read and names the
verb that does prove an import. Both driven. The cost this entry left
unmeasured was measured by the sweep and is R-501.

**Found:** 2026-09-18, by U86's `/code-review` on `relay/131`. Driven.

The item list `route inbox --export` returns is the plan the apply gate's

skipped, because the routing tree, a genre folder or a sub is not in the
export, the item still names that destination. The same run carries a
`route-write-skipped` warning naming the missing piece, `totals.inserted`
counts what landed, and a run that inserted nothing answers `route-blocked`.

writer to report which keys each warning covers, which it does not.

**Found:** 2026-09-18, by U87's `/code-review` on `relay/132`. Read, not

## R-442. The long track playlist only adds, so a track is never taken out of it

**Found:** 2026-09-18, U88 on `relay/133`, by the brief's own decision, and
restated by that unit's `/code-review`. Driven by
`test_a_track_is_never_removed_from_the_playlist` in
`tests/test_routing_workers.py`.

`route inbox --export` adds to the "Sets and Long Tracks" playlist and removes
nothing. A member whose collection row is gone, a member now under the bound
after a person raised `over_seconds`, and a member a person dragged in by hand
all stay. A long track a person took out of the playlist in rekordbox is added
back on the next pass, since the pass cannot tell a removal from a track it
has not seen, and that pass then writes a file and ends PENDING again.

The source system rebuilt the playlist from scratch on every run, so it
dropped stale members and also undid a hand removal. This build keeps a hand
added member, which the source system did not.

**Measured cost:** a playlist that can only grow, and a person who wants a set
out of it has to delete the `[long_tracks]` section or raise the bound. Not
measured live.

**Why not fixed here.** Removal is out of the brief's scope, and whether a
removal is a person's curation or a stale member needs a record of who put a
track there that nothing keeps.

**Closes when:** the pass removes stale members while keeping a person's
choices, or the decision to only add is confirmed at an attended sitting.

## R-443. The rebuild resume asks the engine for the vocal gap rather than reading the report the rebuild made

**Found:** 2026-09-19, R-316 on `relay/107`, as a decision the brief did not
foresee.

The brief for R-316 told `_resume` to read `not_compared` from "the
ConvergenceReport the rebuild already wrote". Nothing persists that report.
`rebuild_governed_tree` returns a `RebuildReport` to `handle`, the brief
forbids changing `handle`'s None return, and the driver keeps no per item
result, so by the time `_resume` holds the envelope the report is gone.

Two ways remained. Run `report_convergence` again over each item's tree after
the job, which opens the database a second time, walks and reads the tags of
every file in the music directory, and can refuse after a job that succeeded.
Or ask the engine the same question with no input and output at all, since the
gap depends on the declaration and the threshold and never on the library.
The second was taken: `rebuild.governed_not_compared()` applies
`not_derived`, the rule `derive_from_taxonomy` itself calls, to the shipped
taxonomy with no threshold, the two inputs `rebuild_governed_tree` derives
with. `test_the_gap_rule_is_the_derivations_own` pins the agreement.

**Measured cost:** none today. It becomes a cost the day a worker hands
`rebuild_governed_tree` a threshold or a taxonomy other than the shipped one,
because `governed_not_compared` would then still answer for the defaults. The
day either changes, the warning has to come from what the item actually
derived, which means a place for a worker to leave it.

A second, smaller shape of the same choice: the warning is added whenever the
resume drove the job, so a job still open on entry whose every item was
already done gets the warning from a pass that compared nothing. The state is
unusual and was not driven.

**Why not fixed here.** Either fix changes `handle`'s return or `jobs.drive`,
both out of the brief's scope.

**Closes when:** the vocal gap on a resume comes from the derivation that ran,
or the decision is confirmed at an attended sitting.

**Narrowed 2026-09-19 on `relay/134`, U89.** The workers now hand the engine a
threshold, the day this entry named. `governed_not_compared` takes the
threshold, and each resume reads it through the same loader, at the path the
same frozen configuration names, as its worker, so the warning no longer
answers for None over a calibrated job. Still open: the taxonomy half, since
both sides still assume the shipped one, and the two reads happen at different
moments, which R-445 records.

## R-444. A read that opens the database is not told it needs the binding pin, and the pins check cannot say only that

**Found:** 2026-09-19, R-313 on `relay/106`, by the review and then driven.

The writer checks the binding pin on every open, read or write, and the
application pin only on a write. `route.unplaced` now declares
`rekordbox.pins` for that reason. `converge` does the same kind of read,
`rb_writer.open_db(cfg=cfg)` in `src/cratekit/cli/converge.py`, and declares
only `library.mounted`, so its declaration under-claims the pin its open
enforces.

The fix is not simply to add the key, because `rekordbox.pins` is one check
over two pins. It FAILs on an unset application pin, "so every database write
refuses", and a verb that only reads is not refused by that. A read verb that
declares it is told about a pin it does not need, and one that does not is
not told about a pin it does.

**Measured cost:** none a person can see today. Doctor's requirement is taken
over every verb a profile switches on, and `requires_check("rekordbox.pins",
...)` is True in `slim`, `full` and `custom` because the core write verbs
declare it. It becomes a cost if doctor ever reports per verb.

**Closes when:** the pins check is split into a binding pin every database
open needs and an application pin only a write needs, and each verb that
opens the database declares the one it reaches.

## R-445. A queued job reads the vocal calibration as it stands when it runs, not as it stood when it was queued

**Found:** 2026-09-19, U89 on `relay/134`, by the review. Read, not driven.

A job freezes its configuration (KTD9), and the vocal calibration is not
configuration: it is a state file the frozen configuration only locates. The
rebuild and resort workers read it through `load_vocal_threshold` when each
item runs, and the resume reads it once just before driving, for the warning.
So a calibration written between queueing and resuming changes what the job
files under "with vox", and no drift warning says so. Between the resume's read
and an item's read the file can also change, and the warning then answers for
a cut the item did not use.

**Measured cost:** none driven. The new cut is the one a person most likely
wants, which is why this was taken rather than freezing the value on the
payload.

**Why not fixed here.** Freezing the cut means a payload field, read by the
worker in place of the file, which changes what a job records at queue time,
outside the brief. It is a choice for the person.

**Closes when:** the cut is frozen with the job, or reading it live is
confirmed at an attended sitting.

## R-447. Four tree inserts still assume a CRLF before the close line, and over a bare LF they write a file no parser reads

**Found:** 2026-09-19, U91 on `relay/136`, by the hunt after the review, as
the first caller of the creating writer. Driven on the engine.

Every lead broken insert in `write/rbxml.py` lands its node at the close line's
start minus two bytes, which is right only when the line before ends in CRLF.
rbxml's own header says real exports still carry bare LF lines an old splicer
wrote. Over one of those the node lands a byte early and splits a `/>` in two.
U91 fixed the one it binds, the create branch of `splice_into_subplaylist`, with
`_break_before`, which answers None and turns the write into a warning. The same
arithmetic is still in `insert_root_playlist`, `insert_genre_folder`,
`insert_intake_playlist` and `insert_empty_subplaylist`. Driven:
`insert_empty_subplaylist` over a genre folder whose last sub line ends in a
bare LF returns `created=True` and no warning, and the document then fails
`xml.etree` at the line it split.

**Measured cost:** a corrupt routed file reported as a success, which a person
is then told to import. Two shipped verbs reach two of the four:
`route inbox --export` calls `insert_root_playlist` through the long track
playlist and `insert_empty_subplaylist` through the vocal pass. Reachability on
a real export is unmeasured: the live library is off limits, and no export here
was read for a bare LF line before a close.

**Why not fixed here.** `insert_root_playlist` and `insert_intake_playlist`
delete an existing node before they compute the insert point, so a refusal
there has to come before the delete to keep "a failure writes nothing", which is
a change to two writers this unit does not call.

**Closes when:** each of the four asks `_break_before` before its first
mutation and answers with its own warning shape, with a test per writer over a
bare LF line.

## R-448. `label approved` reads every accepted release from the provider again on every run

**Found:** 2026-09-19, U75 on `relay/120`, by the unit's `/code-review`.

The brief decided there is no handed off state: ownership makes a second run
idempotent. The cost of that decision is that an accepted item is never
consumed. Each run asks the provider for every accepted release again, an album
read and at least one page of tracks, including a release whose every track
landed months ago. The review store is also opened once per release that holds
a question.

**Measured cost:** none driven against the provider. By count, N accepted
releases cost at least 2N requests per run, for as long as the queue holds
them, so run time and rate limit exposure grow with review history. The 98 live
offered releases are the first size this meets.

**Why not fixed here.** A handed off marker is the state the brief ruled out,
and a cache of fully owned releases is a second record of ownership that can
disagree with the library.

**Closes when:** a release whose tracks are all owned stops being asked for, by
a record that cannot outlive the ownership it stands for, or the cost is
accepted at a measured queue size.

## R-449. A list `label approved` wrote and nobody downloaded is listed again under a new name

**Found:** 2026-09-19, U75 on `relay/120`, by the unit's `/code-review`.

Owned means landed in the library. A track that is listed, or downloaded into
staging and not landed, still resolves missing, so a second run before landing
writes a second list that holds everything the first did plus whatever was
accepted since. The name carries a digest of what is written, so the two never
collide, and nothing marks the first as superseded.

**Measured cost:** none driven. A person who runs `acquire download` on both
lists fetches the shared tracks twice. `docs/GUIDE.md` and the labels skill say
to download the newest list and ignore the older, which is advice and not a
guard. `intake missing` is not the same shape, because its list is named for a
job whose reports do not change.

**Closes when:** a run names the earlier lists it supersedes, or
`acquire download` declines a track already staged, or the advice is accepted.

## R-450. The shared unavailable classifier reads the digits 404 out of a message that carries the request URL

**Found:** 2026-09-19, U75 on `relay/120`, by the unit's `/code-review`, in this
unit's own adapter, and then by the hunt for the same shape elsewhere.

`acquire.adapter.classify_unavailable` answers permanent for an exception whose
text holds "404" or "not found". The provider client's HTTP errors carry the
request URL, and the URL carries the identifier asked for. Driven directly: an
exception with a 401 status and the text "401 Client Error: Unauthorized for
url: .../albums/24040417" classifies as `unavailable-permanent`. U75's adapter
stopped using the classifier for that reason and reads gone from the class name
or a 404 status alone, pinned by
`test_an_identifier_holding_the_digits_404_does_not_make_a_rejection_a_withdrawal`.

Two other callers still ask it: `acquire/vendored.py:268`, which returns on
permanent BEFORE it asks whether the failure was an authentication failure, and
`modules/outbound/tidal_account.py:89`, whose `_not_found` turns a permanent
answer into "the provider has nothing for this".

**Measured cost:** the classifier was driven and the two producers were NOT, so
the reachability is unmeasured. If it is reachable, a rejected session on a
track whose identifier holds those digits is reported as a track that does not
exist, which is the product saying something false, and on the download path
the dead session is never reported as one.

**Closes when:** the classifier reads a status or a class before any text, or
each caller is driven with such an identifier and shown not to reach it.

## R-451. `label approved` and `intake missing` carry near copies of one reporting tail

**Found:** 2026-09-19, U75 on `relay/120`, by the unit's `/code-review`.

`label/approved_cli.py` and `intake/missing_cli.py` each hold their own `--out`
resolution, their own translation of `ListDocRefused`, their own refusal for
missing tracks none of which can be listed, and the same five check rows. The
label verb also builds `listdoc.document` once for the name and lets
`listdoc.write` build it again, because the emitter takes a name and not a
function of what it lists.

**Measured cost:** none to a person. A fix to one copy misses the other, and
R-452 is the first instance.

**Why not fixed here.** Lifting the tail means changing U69's verb and U68's
emitter, neither of which this unit's tables measured.

**Closes when:** the write and report tail is one function beside `listdoc`,
called by both verbs, and the emitter names a list from what it lists.

## R-452. A write the disk refuses reaches a person from `intake missing` as an internal error

**Found:** 2026-09-19, U75 on `relay/120`, by the hunt after a review fix, for
the same shape one file over.

`intake/missing_cli.py` catches `ListDocRefused` around `listdoc.write` and
nothing else. The emitter converts what it READS and lets a failed write
through. In `label approved` the same gap was driven: with
`atomic_write_bytes` raising `ENOSPC`, the verb now refuses
`label-list-unusable` and names the folder. A permission failure is not part of
this, because the cause constructor already reclassifies it as
`path-permission-denied`, driven and pinned in U75.

**Measured cost:** driven in the label verb, NOT driven in `intake missing`, so
the reachability there is unmeasured. If it is reachable, a full disk tells a
person to report a defect.

**Closes when:** `intake missing` converts an `OSError` from the write into its
own refusal, with a test, which R-451's shared tail would do for both.

## R-453. How rekordbox folds a folder name on import was never measured, so the catalog writer's fold is a choice

**Found:** 2026-09-19, U76 on `relay/121`, from the brief's hazard.

The catalog writer compares sibling names after NFC normalisation and nothing
else: a composed and a decomposed `Café` are one folder, and `Kompakt` and
`KOMPAKT` are two. R-129's record says rekordbox merges an imported folder "by
name" and does not say how it compares. If rekordbox folds case, a document
holding `Kompakt` and `KOMPAKT` side by side doubles on import the way R-129
did, and this writer would not refuse it. If it does not fold canonical
equivalence, merging a decomposed spelling into a composed one renames nothing
but joins two folders rekordbox would keep apart.

**Measured cost:** none driven. No caller of the writer exists in `src` yet,
and the live comparison needs an import.

**Closes when:** an attended sitting imports a two folder payload that differs
only by case, and one that differs only by normalisation, into a scratch copy
of a library, and `rbxml._folded` is set to what rekordbox did.

## R-454. The other writers that locate a sibling by name take the first of two and say nothing

**Found:** 2026-09-19, U76 on `relay/121`, by the hunt for the same shape one
file over.

`rbxml.direct_child` returns the first direct child carrying a name. The
catalog writer now asks `_sole_child`, which refuses two. `insert_root_playlist`,
`insert_genre_folder`, `insert_intake_playlist`, `insert_empty_subplaylist` and
`remove_folder_node` still ask `direct_child`, so over a document already
holding R-129's shape each writes into, replaces or removes the first copy and
leaves the second, reporting success.

**Measured cost:** not driven. These writers emit single nodes at the
playlist level rather than a folder import, so the doubling R-129 describes is
not what they produce; the cost is a clean answer over a document that already
carries duplicates. Reachability is unmeasured: the producer would be a fresh
export of a library that R-129's import already doubled.

**Closes when:** each of those writers asks `_sole_child` or a public form of
it, with a test per writer, or the decision to leave them is recorded with a
driven reason.

## R-455. The landing asks the tree writer about every label the manifest names, not only the ones that land

**Found:** 2026-09-19, U77 on `relay/122`, by the author, and raised again by
the unit's `/code-review` as a question of where the matching belongs.

`landing._check_export` trials the catalog writer over a copy of the export
before the first move, because a refusal after the moves leaves a batch in the
library with no labels. Which rows land is known only once the batch folder is
indexed, and the brief fixed that index as `match.index_library(batch_dir)`,
after the moves. So the trial covers every label and year in the manifest. An
export holding two folders of a label this batch does not carry refuses the
whole landing.

**Measured cost:** driven for a label the batch does carry,
`test_an_export_holding_a_label_folder_twice_refuses_before_any_file_moves`.
The case of a label the batch does NOT carry was not driven. Nothing moves
and what the refusal says is true of the export, so the cost is a landing
that has to wait for an export the person had to mend anyway.

**The alternative the review named:** resolve the manifest rows against the
staged files before the move. The tags and names are the same on both sides of
`os.replace`, so the trial would be exact, the gate could show what will be
filed instead of what is listed, and the filter on this run's placed files
would not be needed. Not taken here because the brief made the other decision
and the difference is an over refusal, not a wrong write.

**Closes when:** the rows are resolved against the staged files and the trial
names only what will be written, or the over refusal is driven on a real
manifest and the decision to keep it is recorded.

## R-456. A label tree the disk refuses after the moves leaves its rows filed nowhere, and no verb files them later

**Found:** 2026-09-19, U77 on `relay/122`, by the author.

`landing._label` runs after `place_files` has written the intake file and
recorded a routing intent for every landed file. A failure there is reported,
one `label-tree-unwritten` warning per row, and the intake file is kept as the
splice left it, because taking it back would leave intents pointing at rows
nothing will ever import. The files are out of staging by then, so
`intake land` cannot be run over them again, and no other verb takes a
manifest.

**Measured cost:** driven with a faked `OSError` from the writer and from the
index, `test_a_tree_the_disk_refuses_after_the_moves_is_named_and_the_file_stays`
and `test_a_batch_folder_that_cannot_be_indexed_reports_every_label_row`.
Reachability on a real disk is unmeasured. Every refusal the writer itself can
make, the database owned tree included, was driven to refuse BEFORE the first
move, and the registry is read once before it, so the candidates left are a
full or failing volume between the splice and the label write.

**Closes when:** a verb files a manifest's label rows over files already in
the library, or the landing writes the intake playlist and the label tree in
one replace so there is no second write to fail.

## R-457. An unmatched label row cannot tell a track an earlier landing filed from a download that never arrived

**Found:** 2026-09-19, U77 on `relay/122`, by the unit's `/code-review`.

The index is of the batch folder only. A manifest of 200 rows landed in two
halves, the workflow `docs/GUIDE.md` describes, gives the second landing about
100 rows that resolve to no file it placed. Each is a `label-row-unmatched`
warning and an `unfiled` item. The sentence was false when the review found it,
it claimed a file had landed, and is now true of both cases. The noise is not
fixed: the warnings that matter, a download that never arrived, read the same
as the ones that do not.

**Measured cost:** the sentence was driven and fixed,
`test_a_label_row_no_landed_file_matches_is_reported_by_name`. The count on a
real second landing is unmeasured, since no live label list has been landed.

**Closes when:** the landing reads the export's own label playlist and says
"already filed" for a row whose track is there, which needs the row tied to a
collection row by more than a name, or the unmatched rows are reported as one
line with a count when the export already holds the label's folder.

## R-458. A catalog tree that has cut over to the database makes every `--manifest` landing refuse

**Found:** 2026-09-19, U77 on `relay/122`, by the first caller hunt.

`rbxml.insert_catalog_folder` calls `_refuse_wrong_medium` first, which raises
`TreeModeRefused` when the registry records the catalog tree as database
native. The landing's check catches it before the first move and refuses with
the writer's own reason, pinned by
`test_a_catalog_tree_the_database_owns_refuses_before_any_file_moves`. That is
the correct refusal, and it means a library whose catalog tree has cut over
cannot file a label through the landing at all. The person can still land
without the manifest, and the refusal does not say so.

**Measured cost:** not reachable today. One candidate producer was read and
not driven: a cutover is U29's work, which is attended and has recorded no
catalog tree.

**Closes when:** the catalog tree has a database writer the landing can call
for a tree that has cut over, or the refusal names landing without the
manifest as the way through.

## R-459. The label index reads every landed file's tags again, straight after the splice read them

**Found:** 2026-09-19, U77 on `relay/122`, by the unit's `/code-review`.

`place_files` reads each file's tags to build its collection row, and
`match.index_library` then opens each file again for the artist, the title and
the key. The review's other efficiency finding, a rewrite of the whole intake
file per label, is fixed: `insert_record_labels_trees` is one read and one
replace, pinned by
`test_the_intake_file_is_rewritten_once_however_many_labels_it_carries`.

**Measured cost:** not measured. It is a second tag read per landed file on
the library's volume, and a label batch is hundreds of files, not thousands.

**Closes when:** the index is built from what `place_files` already read, or
a measurement on a real batch shows the second read does not matter.

## R-460. No verb clears a label's seeds or its track limit back to none

**Found:** 2026-09-19, U99 on `relay/144`, building `crate label registry set`.

`set --seed` replaces the held seed list and `set --track-limit` replaces the
limit, and neither can say "none". An empty `--seed` refuses as a blank seed, a
zero limit refuses at the parser, and `RegistryStore.edit` is the only caller
that can pass an empty tuple. The brief decided the verbs and did not name a
clearing flag, so none was invented.

**Measured cost:** a person who wants the label's own artist page alone, or the
default limit again, removes the label and adds it back. Removal keeps the
identifier and its watermark, so nothing is lost, and the person retypes the
match needle.

**Closes when:** `set` takes a clearing form for each field, or the decision
not to is recorded.

## R-461. An adopt whose every accepted label failed exits zero

**Found:** 2026-09-19, U100 on `relay/145`, the built in review of
`crate label registry adopt`.

When every accepted harvest item is refused, a name with no identifier or an
item naming no label, adopt adds nothing and reports `no_op` with status 0. Each
failure is a FAIL line to a person and is listed under `summary.refused` or
`summary.nameless` to a reader of json. A script that reads only the exit code
sees the same success as a run with nothing to do. Driven in
`test_a_name_with_no_identifier_fails_alone_and_the_rest_land` and
`test_an_accepted_item_naming_no_label_is_reported_not_skipped`.

**Measured cost:** none on any producer driven. `harvest.from_tracks` offers
only names the catalogue confirmed, and the one candidate that reaches this
path, a `review import` carrying such an item, was driven only through
`review.offer` directly.

**Closes when:** adopt exits non zero when it refused something, or the decision
that a per item failure is not a run failure is recorded.

## R-462. The genre gate's share is over the releases accepted this run, not the label's output

**Found:** 2026-09-19, U101 on `relay/146`, the built in review of
`crate label approved`.

`label/approved_cli.py` `_gated` hands `gate_decisions` the genres of the
label's releases that were ACCEPTED and READ this run. The source system judged
a family against the label's whole classified catalogue. Rejected and
unanswered releases are never read by this verb, a contract
`test_an_accepted_release_is_listed_and_a_rejected_or_open_one_is_never_read`
pins, and releases accepted and landed in an earlier run are not counted either.
So a label whose only accepted release this sitting is off genre is that
family's whole share and is never held.

**Measured cost:** unmeasured on any producer, because no shipped catalogue
reports a genre (R-420). Against the fake catalogue the direction is timid:
fewer releases in the set means larger shares and fewer holds, and every
release so kept was accepted by a person in review.

**Options:** read every release the sweep offered for the label, which spends a
provider read per rejected release; keep a per label genre tally across runs; or
record that a person's acceptance outranks the share. The conservative call,
taken here, keeps the verb's read contract.

**Closes when:** the share is computed over the label's output rather than one
sitting's acceptances, or the decision that acceptance outranks it is recorded.

## R-463. A release the genre gate holds has no way through short of editing the gate

**Found:** 2026-09-19, U101 on `relay/146`, while writing the held line.

`crate label approved` holds a release a person accepted in review when its
family is under the share for its label. The held line names the numbers and
offers no act, because none exists: the verb reads the shipped taxonomy through
`taxonomy.default_taxonomy()`, so even editing a library's own template does not
move it. The source system let a heart override the gate for favourites.

**Measured cost:** none today, because nothing is held in the shipped build
(R-420). Once a genre is reported, an accepted release a person wants and the
gate holds reaches the list only through another intake verb.

**Closes when:** a held release can be passed by a named act, or the decision
that the gate outranks an acceptance is recorded.

## R-464. Harvest offers a label the registry already holds

**Found:** 2026-09-19, on `relay/161`, looking one file over from R-259 for the
same shape, METHOD's fifth pattern.

`harvest.from_tracks` offers every confirmed label name into the label release
queue and is handed nothing about the registry, and `label.cli.harvest_playlist`
passes it nothing (`src/cratekit/label/harvest.py:111-144`). Driven on
2026-09-19 through the real dispatcher with the fake catalogue: `Anjunadeep`
added with `crate label registry add`, then `crate label harvest` over a
playlist whose one track carries `2026 Anjunadeep`. Exit 0, and the queue held

which a person declines or accepts to no effect: `registry adopt` resolves a
held name and does not file it twice (U100), so nothing is damaged. Harvest is

**Closes when:** a harvest leaves a name the registry already resolves out of
the queue, and says how many it left out.

## R-465. A label sweep reads the tracks of every owned release on every sweep

**Found:** 2026-09-19, by `/code-review` on `relay/161`.

`OwnedReleases` keeps its answers for one item and nothing across sweeps. An
owned release does not count toward the per label cap, so a sweep of a label
whose back catalogue the library holds verifies and then reads the tracks of
every owned release it lists, on every sweep, an album read plus paged track
reads each (`TidalCatalogue.release_tracks`). Before R-259 it verified them
and offered them, and `review.offer` made the repeat offers free.

**Measured cost.** Provider reads, against a rate limited endpoint; not
measured against the live provider, which is attended. A read that fails is
answered not owned and three in a row stop the asking, so an outage degrades
to offering rather than refusing the label.

**Options:** skip the ownership read for a release the label release queue
already holds a decided item for, which is a local question and is exactly
where the repeat offer used to be absorbed; or keep owned release identities
across sweeps. The first is cheap and was not taken here because it changes
what a declined release means to the sweep.

**Closes when:** a release already owned, or already decided, is not read
again on the next sweep.

## R-466. A release whose ownership could not be read is offered and nothing says why

**Found:** 2026-09-19, on `relay/161`, choosing what a failed track read does.

When `Catalogue.release_tracks` raises for a confirmed release, or after three
such failures in a row, `OwnedReleases` answers not owned and the release is
offered. The worker's envelope is exactly `job_state/1` (KTD7) and carries no
warning, so a person reviewing it cannot tell an offer the library was checked
for from one it was not. Offering is the conservative call: refusing withheld
every new release on the label, which is what the first draft did and what
`/code-review` flagged.

**Measured cost.** None driven against the live provider. With the fake
catalogue a release the library holds in full is offered when its read fails
(`test_a_track_read_the_provider_could_not_answer_offers_the_release`).

**Closes when:** an offer whose ownership was not read says so on the review
item or the job, or the decision that it need not is recorded.

## R-467. A rate limit on a discovery album search is skipped as if that query was read

**Found:** 2026-09-19, on `relay/162`, looking one function over from R-393
for the same shape, which is METHOD's fifth pattern.

`TidalCatalogue._discover` issues eighty album searches per label and skips a
query whose search raises anything but a `CratekitError` or an
`AuthenticationError` (`src/cratekit/label/tidal_catalogue.py`, the first loop
in `_discover`). R-352 chose that on purpose: a 429 on one query must not
refuse the label. R-393's fix made a skipped artist LISTING a recorded
`Unread` that fails the sweep after its offers, and left the skipped QUERY
silent. An artist credited only on a compilation that query would have found
is never enqueued, and the sweep reports success.

**Measured cost.** Read and not driven end to end. The suite pins the skip
(`test_a_rate_limit_on_one_album_query_does_not_discard_the_own_page`) and no
test asks what a person is told. Unmeasured live how often a search 429s.

**Why not fixed here.** The brief's out of scope is anything the entries do not
name, and the query skip is a decision R-352 made one unit ago. The fix is the
same shape as R-393's: record the query as `Unread` and let the worker's
refusal name it.

**Closes when:** a sweep whose discovery skipped a search query says so where
a person reads it, or the decision that a skipped query need not is recorded.

## R-468. A held artist whose discovery listing fails is not expanded, and nothing says so

**Found:** 2026-09-19, on `relay/162`, in the fix for `/code-review`'s
finding.

The BFS walk lists every credited artist, including the seeds and the label's
own page, to find collaborators on releases that credit the label. A held
artist whose listing fails there is now NOT recorded, because the roster lists
it again and that read decides its releases. That is right for the releases.
It is not right for the walk: the collaborators credited on that artist's
releases were never enqueued, so an artist discovery would have reached only
through them is missing, and the sweep reports success.

**Measured cost.** Read and not driven. It needs a held artist whose listing
fails during discovery and then succeeds for the roster, which is a 429 that
clears inside one label's crawl.

**Why not fixed here.** Recording it as `Unread` names an artist whose
releases were read, which is what the review finding was about. Closing it
means walking the roster's own listing for collaborators instead of listing
twice, which changes the discovery walk rather than its reporting.

**Closes when:** discovery expands from the roster's read of a held artist,
or a failed expansion is named without naming the artist's releases unread.

## R-469. A sweep with both a rate limit and a missing listing is told to resume

**Found:** 2026-09-19, on `relay/162`, choosing the refusal's remedy.

`label.cli._refuse_unread` is `resume-job` and retryable when ANY unread part
is transient. When one artist hit a 429 and another member lacks a listing, a
resume can read the first and can never read the second, so the resumed item
fails again on the missing method, now as `report-defect`.

**Measured cost.** One extra resume before the person is told the true remedy.
No test drives a mixed set; the mutation row that would flip `any` to `all` was
logged as dropped in `docs/mutation/r261-rows.toml`.

**Closes when:** a mixed refusal names both remedies, or the decision that the
resume comes first is recorded.

## R-471. The art encoder stretches a non square image to the square instead of cropping or padding it

**Found:** 2026-09-19, on `relay/128`, U83, as a decision taken from the source
system rather than measured.

`core/art.py::to_cdj_jpeg` resizes any image to `size` by `size`, so a 1200 by
1000 cover comes out 800 by 800 with its content squeezed by a sixth. That is
what `DJ_tagging/tag_new_tracks.py:152-153` does, and parity was the
conservative call for an unattended unit. The options are a centre crop, which
loses the edges, a pad onto a flat colour, which keeps everything and adds
bars, or the stretch as shipped.

**Measured cost.** None measured. How many covers the providers return non
square was not counted, and nothing calls the encoder yet.

**Closes when:** Phillip picks one of the three, or the share of non square
covers from a real tagging run is counted and is small enough to leave.

## R-472. `write_front_cover` removes every embedded picture, not only a previous front cover

**Found:** 2026-09-19, on `relay/128`, U83, as a decision taken from the source
system rather than measured.

The FLAC branch calls `clear_pictures()`, the ID3 branch `delall("APIC")`, and
the MP4 branch replaces `covr` whole. A back cover, an artist photo or a label
logo another tagger embedded is deleted by an art write and nothing reports it.
That is the source system's behaviour, `tag_new_tracks.py:183` and `:211`, and
it is what makes a second write a replacement. It is also the safer reading for
a player, since a progressive or zeroed picture of another type left in the
file may be the one a CDJ picks up. Both halves are unmeasured.

**Measured cost.** None measured. Reachable only once U84 or U85 calls the
writer. `tests/test_art.py` pins the behaviour in both directions, so a change
to keep other picture types is a visible edit and not a drift.

**Closes when:** a CDJ is shown a file with a good front cover and a bad picture
of another type and the result is recorded, or the deletion is reported by the
verb that performs it.

## R-473. At native resolution the art encoder refuses a picture that misses the cap at the quality floor

**Found:** 2026-09-19, on `relay/128`, U83, by the built in code review, and
left to the repair unit by the brief's own decision.

`to_cdj_jpeg(data, size=None)` keeps the native resolution, which is what a
repair of art already in a file wants. If the picture is still over `max_bytes`
at quality 50 it raises `ArtError` rather than returning bytes over the cap. At
800 by 800 that is close to unreachable. At 3000 by 3000 it is not: the review
drove a noise image that size and it was refused, and whether a real cover that
size fits in 450,000 bytes at quality 50 was NOT measured. A refused repair
leaves the file with the blank rendering art it had.

**Measured cost.** None on a real cover. No caller exists until U84.

**Closes when:** U84 decides what a repair does on that refusal, a downscale
toward 800, a larger cap passed to both the encoder and the writer, or a named
line in its report, and drives it on a large real cover.

## R-474. The art writer and reader inherit `write_tags`' quiet failure reporting

**Found:** 2026-09-19, on `relay/128`, U83, by the built in code review.

`write_front_cover` catches every exception from the open, the edit and the
save, logs it at debug, and returns False, exactly as `tags.write_tags` does. A
read only volume, a mutagen API change and one awkward file are the same False
to a caller, and nothing above debug says which. The review also named the
reader's full Pillow decode of every picture, kept on purpose because a
truncated picture opens cleanly and fails only on load, as a cost on a library
wide sweep: not measured on a library.

**Measured cost.** Maintainer facing until a verb calls the writer. Then it is
the caller's report that decides whether 500 False results read as 500 awkward
files.

**Closes when:** the verbs that call the writer (U84, U85) report a failure
count with a cause a user can act on, or the shared convention in `tags` and
`art` is changed in one place.

## R-476. A repeat listing of the same job refuses when the provider's ISRC answer changed

**Found:** 2026-09-19, on `relay/123`, U78, by the built in code review.

`intake missing` names its files after the job or the run, and `listdoc.write`
refuses a file of that name holding other bytes. Before U78 those bytes came
from the job's committed reports alone. Now they also come from the provider:
a row one ISRC named is listed, and the same row after the provider files a
second release under that ISRC is handed on. The second run then refuses
`intake-list-unusable`. The order of identifiers inside a reason is sorted, so
provider order alone cannot cause it, pinned by
`test_the_order_the_provider_answers_in_does_not_change_the_files`. The trap is
the one filed at
`docs/solutions/integration-issues/a-list-named-from-its-identifiers-meets-the-emitters-whole-file-comparison.md`.

**Measured cost.** A refused repeat run whose remedy, move the files aside, is
stated and works. How often the provider's answer for one ISRC changes is not
measured.

**Closes when:** the list's name carries a digest of what it lists, as
`label approved` does, or a repeat run is decided to replace its own earlier
files.

**Reached a second way, 2026-09-19, `relay/183`.** Since R-502 closed, a
repeat listing of a job some of whose missing rows the library gained since
lists fewer rows and refuses over the job's earlier list the same way. The
refusal names how many rows were gained. Driven in
`test_a_shorter_rerun_over_the_jobs_earlier_list_refuses_and_says_why`.

## R-477. `TidalAccount.match_track` reads `InvalidISRC` as no match, and the client raises it for outages

**Found:** 2026-09-19, on `relay/123`, U78, hunting the same shape one file over.

`modules/outbound/tidal_account.py:75` puts `InvalidISRC` in `NOT_FOUND_NAMES`,
so an ISRC lookup that raised it is answered as no match and never retried.
tidalapi 0.8.11's `get_tracks_by_isrc` catches every `HTTPError` the request
layer re-raises, which is every status but 404 and 429, and raises
`InvalidISRC`. A server error or a rejected session on that endpoint is
therefore reported as an unmatched row. Driven with a client raising the
library's own `InvalidISRC`: `match_track` returned None after one call, no
retry. The client's behaviour was read from its source at 0.8.11 and not
driven against the live endpoint.

**Measured cost.** Outbound hearts and exports report a track unmatched over a
lookup that failed, a clean report over state the product could not read, and
the track is not hearted. U78's own adapter member does not share it:
`tracks_for_isrc` treats only `ObjectNotFound` as an answer and pins
`InvalidISRC` climbing the ladder.

**Closes when:** `match_track` treats `InvalidISRC` on a well formed ISRC as a
failure that climbs the retry ladder, and a test pins it.

## R-478. A handed on row that cannot be spelled as an `Artist - Title` line is in no file

**Found:** 2026-09-19, on `relay/123`, U78, by the built in code review.

An artist carrying the text separator, a leading ordinal or a leading `#` reads
back from a text line as another track or as none, so `listdoc.text_line`
refuses it and `intake missing` names the row on a failing
`intake.missing.unwritable` check and in the summary with `in_file` false,
rather than refusing the whole verb, which was the review's driven finding. When
no row at all is written the verb refuses.

**Measured cost.** The row is on the screen and in the envelope and in no file,
so it is carried forward by hand. How many real artist names take one of those
shapes is not measured.

**Closes when:** the text list can quote a line, or such rows go to a document
that carries artist and title as fields.

## R-479. A well formed ISRC the provider rejects refuses the whole listing after the retry ladder

**Found:** 2026-09-19, on `relay/123`, U78, planning the adapter member.

The client raises `InvalidISRC` for a malformed code and for an outage alike
(R-477), and `tracks_for_isrc` treats it as a failure, so it climbs the ladder,
31 seconds, and `intake missing` refuses `unavailable-transient`. The verb keeps
malformed codes from being asked by checking the twelve character shape first.
If the provider answers 400 to a code of the right shape, every run refuses.

**Measured cost.** Unmeasured: whether the provider rejects a well formed ISRC
was not observed.

**Closes when:** a live lookup of an unknown but well formed ISRC is observed at
an attended sitting and the adapter's reading of the answer is pinned to it.

A text list row is one `Artist - Title` string, so a handed on row's ISRC
survives only inside the reason comment, and `match run` over the file builds

## R-481. A pass still reports the mark as unbound now that a verb binds it

**Found:** 2026-09-19, on `relay/127`, U82, deciding what the pass should say.

`sync.playlists.report` puts `"mark": "unbound"` on every playlists block, and
that was the whole truth while nothing could mark. `crate sync mark` now can.
The value is still true of the PASS, which resolves tracks, writes no importable
file and renames nothing, and a guard holds that by the act. It no longer says
where the mark went.

**The conservative call made here.** Leave the token. It is asserted in
`tests/test_sync_all.py` and read by whatever consumes `summary.playlists`, and
a new word for the same fact is a schema change the brief did not ask for. The
options are a new token such as `deferred`, or a `sync.next` style line naming
`crate sync mark` once a pass has recorded a playlist.

**Measured cost.** Wording. A person reading the block is not told the verb
exists. GUIDE names it in the acquisition walkthrough.

**Closes when:** the block or a check beside it names the verb, or the token is
decided to stand.

## R-482. A track accepted through review still holds its playlist's mark back

**Found:** 2026-09-19, on `relay/127`, U82, fixing `/code-review`'s first finding.

`sync.mark_cli._settle` resolves every offered or missing track with
`match.resolve_one` over `match_cli.library_view`, which is the library and the
tombstones. It does not run `match_cli.adjudicate`, so the review store is never
consulted. A track the pass OFFERED, which a person has since accepted as the
record they own, still resolves `needs_review`, is reported outstanding, and its
playlist is never planned.

**Driven:** the offered half, by
`test_a_track_the_pass_offered_for_review_holds_its_playlist_back`. The accepted
verdict half was read and not driven.

**Why not fixed here.** `adjudicate` files review items as it reads, and a verb
that stops at a gate having written to the review queue on the way has moved
state for an answer of abort. Reading verdicts without filing needs a seam the
review engine does not expose yet.

**Measured cost.** Errs toward not renaming. The playlist stays unprefixed on
the account, so the source system offers it again, which is R-358's original
cost for that one playlist. **Meets the board bar, (c), and its issue is owed**,
to be filed after this merge is on `main`.

**Closes when:** `_settle` reads an accepted verdict as settled without filing
anything, and a test drives the accepted half.

## R-483. A pass that found nothing missing can never be marked

**Found:** 2026-09-19, on `relay/127`, U82, reading what `sync mark` needs.

The mark waits for an importable file, which is `sync/marks.py`'s rule. A pass
whose every track was already owned lists nothing, downloads nothing and lands
nothing, so no intake file carries its name and `crate sync mark` has nothing to
be handed. Its playlists are recorded in the cursor and never prefixed.

**Measured cost.** The source system sweeps those playlists again and finds
every track owned, so the cost is a repeated listing and no download. Not
observed live.

**Closes when:** a pass with nothing owed may be marked without a file, which is
a change to the rule in `sync/marks.py` and therefore a decision, or never.

## R-484. A mistyped intake file name is a gated no-op and not a refusal

**Found:** 2026-09-19, on `relay/127`, U82, meeting conformance 3.

An intake file whose name no playlist job on this library spells is a plan of
nothing: the explicit gate is asked and the run ends NO_OP under the warning
`sync-mark-no-pass`. That is `intake land`'s precedent for an empty folder and
is what lets conformance 3 drive the verb on an empty install. It also means a
landing made under a `--name` other than the one `intake missing --run` printed
is answered at a gate before the person learns the file matched nothing, since
the gate screen says so and the refusal it replaced said so sooner.

**Measured cost.** One wasted answer. Nothing is renamed.

**Closes when:** the verb takes the run identifier as well as the file, or
never.

**Found:** 2026-09-19, on `relay/127`, U82, looking for R-398's shape one file
over, as METHOD asks after a fix.

`modules/tools/mastering.py:672`, `core/tree_registry.py:795` and

calls on one line, so a check split across lines was not counted.

## R-486. A retried tagging item reports its art as ok when the same job fixed it

**Found:** 2026-09-19, on `relay/129`, U84, by `/code-review`.

`tagging/tag.py`'s `tag_one` repairs a file's art first and saves it, then asks
the catalogue for a genre. A catalogue nobody could read raises out of the
item, by design, so the item fails with no artifact. The retry finds the art
already sound and commits `art_repair: "ok"`, so the summary's `fixed` count
misses a file this job rewrote and the artifact calls art sound that was
broken when the job began.

**Driven:** not driven end to end. Read from the source, and the order of the
two steps in `tag_one` is what produces it.

**Measured cost.** Nothing on disk is wrong: the art is repaired and says so.
Only the count is low, and only for items that failed once on an unreadable
catalogue and were retried.

**Closes when:** a failed item's repair status survives to its retry, or the
summary documents that `ok` means sound at the time of the committed attempt.

## R-487. A FLAC block declaring the wrong nonzero dimensions is read as sound

**Found:** 2026-09-19, on `relay/129`, U84, while writing the repair's test.

`core/art.py`'s `_needs_repair` follows the source system exactly: a block is
broken when a declared dimension is zero or its data is not a baseline JPEG. A
block declaring 1280 by 1280 over an 800 by 800 image passes both checks and
is left alone. Whether a Pioneer player renders such a block is not known.

**Driven:** not driven. No producer is known. The vendored downloader writes
zeroes, which the repair catches, and U83's writer measures the bytes it
writes.

**Measured cost.** Unmeasured. It needs a third tool that fills the block from
a figure other than the image, and a player that trusts the block over the
image.

**Closes when:** the repair compares declared dimensions with decoded ones and
repairs a mismatch, or a player is shown to render such a block.

## R-488. The candidate floor and the search query were never measured against a live provider

**Found:** 2026-09-19, on `relay/124`, U79, by the author.

`intake/candidates.py` shows a hit that is not exact only when its recording
scores 60 or more against the row, `CANDIDATE_FLOOR`, by the scorer the
library's own near match uses. The library's floor of 82 was tuned on pinned
examples. This one was not tuned on anything: no live search answer has been
read by this product. The same holds for the query, the artist, the title and
the version when the row names one, and for the page of 50.

**Driven:** on fakes only. The floor and the scorer never list anything, so a
wrong floor cannot download a wrong track.

**Measured cost.** Unmeasured. Too high, and a candidate a person would have
accepted is not shown and the row is reported as having no candidate. Too low,
and review items fill with hits that share one word with the row. A query the
provider ranks badly pushes the wanted track off the page, and a full page is
then offered rather than listed, which is the safe side.

**Closes when:** the attended sitting's real typed tracklist is run, the
offered items are read, and the floor and the query are kept or moved on what
they showed.

## R-489. One row whose search fails on every run refuses the whole list

**Found:** 2026-09-19, on `relay/124`, U79, by the unit's `/code-review`. Read,
not driven.

`missing_cli._searched` refuses the verb `unavailable-transient` when any one
search raises, after the adapter's retry ladder, with no candidate offered and
no list written. That is deliberate and is U78's rule for the ISRC read: a
partial pass would report the unasked rows as having no candidate. An ISRC is
a fixed twelve character code. A text query is whatever the row says, so a row
the provider's client fails on deterministically would refuse every run of
that list.

**Driven:** no. No producer is known: no query that makes the client raise
every time was found, and a live provider call is not a session's to make. The
refusal now names taking the row out of the list as the way past it.

**Measured cost.** Unmeasured reachability. If reachable, one line holds back
every other line of a tracklist until a person edits the file. This would meet
the board bar under (c) and is NOT on the board, because nothing shows the
input exists. Drive a producer first.

**Closes when:** a failing row is reported under a state of its own while the
rest are listed and offered, with a bound on failures in a row as
`label approved` has, or a sitting shows no query fails deterministically.

**Found:** 2026-09-19, on `relay/124`, U79, in the fix for the review's first
finding.

The found list is named with a digest of its rows and provenance, because the

answer lists more than the run before it. The cost of that fix is that the
earlier list stays in the lists folder. It holds a subset of the new one.

**Driven:** the two lists, yes, in
`test_the_run_after_an_answer_lists_more_than_the_first_and_is_not_refused`.
Whether `acquire download` fetches a track again when handed both lists was

## R-494. The second source search was never run against the real program

**Found:** 2026-09-19, on `relay/125`, U80.

Everything `YtDlpSearcher` assumes about yt-dlp is read from the source system
and never driven here: the flat mode `--print` shape, that a search with no
hits exits zero with nothing printed, that a network failure exits nonzero
once `--ignore-errors` is gone, and the 180 second timeout. The score's
weights, `LIKELY_MIX_SECONDS` and `MIX_FACTOR` are the source system's, and
`SEARCH_LIMIT` of 4 a platform is too.

**Driven:** no. The suite drives the searcher through a fake runner only, by
the brief's decision.

**Measured cost.** If a search with no hits exits nonzero, every row with no
upload reads as an outage and the verb refuses `unavailable-transient` on it
every run, so the row blocks the rows after it. Unmeasured.

**Closes when:** one attended search is run, the U80 brief's owed item, with
one row that has uploads and one that has none.

## R-497. A tagged file whose track names no picture is searched again on every run

**Found:** 2026-09-19, on `relay/130`, U85.

The brief's decision makes art and genre independent needs, so a file with a
genre and no picture is searched. When the catalogue that carries it names no

## R-498. The shipped fallback fetcher has never downloaded anything

**Found:** 2026-09-19, on `relay/126`, U81.

`acquire/fallback.py`'s `YtDlpFetcher` is driven only through a fake runner.
The argv it builds, `--extract-audio --audio-format mp3 --audio-quality 0`,
`--postprocessor-args "ExtractAudio:-map_metadata -1"`, a fixed
`fetched.%(ext)s` output and `--` before the address, was never handed to the
real tool, and `landed_in`'s rule that exactly one MP3 is left in the item's
directory was never checked against what the tool leaves beside it. The
metadata drop is known NOT to apply to an upload already served as MP3, read
at yt-dlp 2026.6.9 `postprocessor/ffmpeg.py:510-514`, which is why the worker
strips every tag itself; that strip is driven on a real MP3 carrying a tempo
frame.

**Measured cost:** unmeasured. The worst case is a refusal, not a wrong file:
an argv the tool rejects exits nonzero and fails the item as
`unavailable-transient`, and a landing that is not exactly one MP3 does the
same.

**Closes when:** one real accepted upload is downloaded at an attended sitting
and lands marked, tagged from its row, with no tempo frame.

## R-499. The source system's per row purchase link override has no counterpart

**Found:** 2026-09-19, on `relay/126`, U81, carried from R-404's narrowing.

The source system's review file had a `URL` column a person could fill with a
lossless purchase link, forced for that row over any search result. Cratekit's
second source queue offers only what the search found, so a lossless copy
bought elsewhere cannot be routed through `acquire fallback-fetch`, and the
fetch is lossy by construction.

**Measured cost:** a workflow step, not a loss. The bought file can be ingested
with `crate intake file`, so nothing is blocked, and the lossy fetch of the
same row stays refusable by leaving its candidate unaccepted.

**Closes when:** a person can name a URL for a row in review and the fetch
honours it, or the override is dispositioned as cut.

## R-500. `name apply` renames a file the library names when its row sits under an unmapped volume

**Found:** 2026-09-19, by an independent review of U67's merged diff, sweep
finding 112.1 in `docs/ideation/2026-09-19-fable-review-sweep.md`. Driven
against a disposable library in the attended worktree.

U67's guard holds back a rename when a collection row names the file. With an
empty `location_prefix_map`, a row recorded under another volume name is keyed
only by its old spelling, no candidate matches it, and the file is planned as
an ordinary rename. Driven, the plan read `count 2, referenced 0` and the apply
renamed the file the row names. No warning, no count, exit ok.

**Measured cost:** the R-407 outcome the guard exists to stop, a row left
naming a path that is gone. R-372 measured this library at 9937 of 9937 rows
under the drive's old volume name, and setup writes the map empty. The
author's own configuration now carries a prefix rule for the renamed drive, so
the live library is covered. A fresh setup is not. The deletion pass refuses on
an unmapped row where this verb proceeds, and no test covers an unmapped row.
The case sensitive half of the finding, a rule differing from the recorded
volume only in case, was read and not driven.

**Why not fixed here.** The sweep session records and does not change code.

**Closes when:** `name apply` refuses, or holds the file back and says so, when
any collection row's recorded prefix matches no rule, the way the deletion pass
does, with a test driving an unmapped row.

**CLOSED 2026-09-19 on `relay/181`, by the refusal.** `_referenced` in
`write/naming_cli.py` now collects every DARK row and refuses the whole verb as
`collection-row-unmapped`, exit PRECONDITION, count first and the first location
named, before any item is classified or renamed. It sits on the checking path,
so the plan read and the re read after the gate both get it. Reproduced red
first: the new test read `count 2, referenced 0` before the guard existed.

Dark is two facts together, no rule resolves the row AND its recorded file is
not on this machine. The first cut refused on every unmapped row and the built
in review rejected it, correctly: a track imported from a downloads folder, or
the demo tracks rekordbox installs, sits under no rule with its recorded
spelling on disk, so the recorded key already protects it, and two of U67's own
tests only passed once given an identity rule. The existence test fails closed.

The case half, read and not driven when this was filed, is now driven and
PINNED TO THE REFUSAL. The shared resolver compares a prefix exactly, so a rule
differing only in case leaves the row unmapped to every writer, and matching it
here alone would make this verb the second locate sweep finding 112.7 warns
about. The refusal quotes the decoded location so the difference can be seen.

The locate is lifted IN PART. `trees.located` is public, decodes once and hands
back the decoded path beside the resolution, and both `trees._comparable` and
this verb call it. The keying, a casefold and the as recorded spelling, stays
in `naming_cli`, because the guard errs toward holding back and the writers
need one exact row, so casefolding their index would manufacture ambiguity.

Fifteen mutation rows in `docs/mutation/r500-a`, `r500-b` and `r500-c`, fifteen
killed, null control zero on the full suite in each. The author's table, so a
kill reads as "the author could kill it". What this left open is R-523 to
R-527.

## R-501. Every landing leaves an open session and an intake file that each refuse the cutover precheck

**Found:** 2026-09-19, sweep finding 117.1. Driven. **This corrects R-433**,
whose measured cost says an open intake record blocks nothing today.

Driven on a disposable library with no database native tree. `crate intake
land` of one file ended `PENDING_HUMAN` and left its session record `OPEN`.
`crate route pending` then answered exit 0, outcome ok, and the record was
still `OPEN`, because the verb returns before `_close_if_settled` while no tree
is native. `tree_registry.assert_cutover_ready` refused `cutover-open-run`
naming that session. With the record forced terminal, it refused again,
`cutover-xml-pending`, naming `<root>/<batch>_inboxed.xml`. Only with that
file deleted by hand did the precheck pass.

R-433 searched for readers of `SessionState.OPEN` and found none. The reader is
`core/tree_registry.py`, which asks `not record.terminal`.

**Measured cost:** the first cutover cannot pass its precheck on any library
that has landed a batch. The session closes only through `route pending`,
which closes it only once a tree is native, which takes a cutover. No shipped
verb closes or abandons an open intake record: `session release` is the lock,
and `session.abandon` takes only `committed-unverified`. The refusal's step,
close or abandon every open run, names an act no verb offers. The landing's
pending action says to import the file and run `route pending`, and never says
the imported file must then be removed. What limits the cost today is that no
shipped verb calls `tree_registry.flip`, a search of `src` and `scripts` found
only the function itself, so this is paid at the attended cutover, U29, and by
every landing on the live library before it, each of which leaves one more
record and one more file for that sitting to clear. `intake file` has the same
shape through the same `place_files`.

**Why not fixed here.** The sweep session records and does not change code.

**Closes when:** `place_files` closes the session it opened, or the record is
moved to `awaiting-import` and the precheck and a shipped verb agree on how a
person clears it, and an imported intake file has a stated end: a verb that
retires it, or a pending step that says to remove it.

**CLOSED 2026-09-19 on `relay/182`, by the second half, with one thing the
closing line did not foresee.** `place_files` leaves its session
`awaiting-import` through the existing builder, with the pending action
persisted on the record. A new verb, `crate intake imported --export`, proves
the import against a Fresh Export taken after it, retires the intake file by
renaming it to `NAME_inboxed.xml.imported`, which the pending scan does not
walk, and moves the session out of `awaiting-import`. The precheck's refusal
over a waiting run now carries that run's own recorded steps, which name the
verb. Driven end to end through the command line: land, follow every step,
and `assert_cutover_ready` passes with no hand deletion, for `intake land` and
for `intake file`.

**What was not foreseen: the run cannot be CLOSED before a cutover.** Every
close goes through `routing_pass.close_run`, two AST guards enforce that, and
it refuses while the run holds a deferred placement. `place_files` records one
per track, and only a database native tree can place one. So a proven run
stays `open`, holding no capture, with `import_verified` recorded, and the
precheck excuses exactly that record, `session.owes_only_deferred_routing`,
since the only thing it owes is what the cutover unlocks. After a cutover
`route pending` places the tracks, records the pass as the proof when it routed
at least one, and closes the run. R-528 records the choice and the other one.

**The same shape one file over, looked for.** The precheck walks three
suffixes. Three were looked at and only `_inboxed.xml` has a reachable writer:
`_synced.xml` comes from the writer R-437 records as unreachable, and nothing
in `src` writes `_favorites.xml`. One neighbour was found and fixed: `sync
mark` finds its pass from the intake file's name, so it now reads the same
pass off a retired name.

Mutation tables `docs/mutation/r501-a.md` to `r501-d.md`, 25 rows, 25 killed,
the author's own. Residuals R-528 to R-533.
