## R-502. A second `intake missing` over a job lists tracks the library has since gained

**Found:** 2026-09-19, sweep finding 114.2. Driven.

The verb lists from the job's committed reports, whose states were fixed when
the job ran, and rechecks nothing. Driven: a hearts job with two missing rows,
`intake missing` wrote two, `acquire download` fetched both. The staged audio
was removed as a landing would, and both tracks were put in the library. A
second `intake missing` over the same job answered exit 0, outcome ok,
`missing 2, written 2`, and printed the same `next: crate acquire download`
line. That download queued a new job over the same two ids and fetched both
again. Neither verb raised a check or a warning.

**Measured cost:** a repeat run hands a person a download command for tracks
they already hold, and the report calls them missing. `acquire download` does
not consult the library either, so nothing downstream catches it. A track
tombstoned after the intake is listed the same way, read and not driven, which
the module docstring says the verb will not do. R-431 covers only tombstones
the consult cannot reach at intake time, and R-449 sets this verb aside as a
different shape.

**Why not fixed here.** The sweep session records and does not change code.

**Closes when:** the listing rechecks ownership and tombstones at listing time
for each row it is about to write, or says in a failing check how old the
job's answers are, and a repeat run over rows since acquired lists none of
them.

**CLOSED 2026-09-19 on `relay/183`, by the first of the two.** `_listed` in
`intake/missing_cli.py` hands every missing report to `_still_missing` before
anything is named or written, for `--job` and `--run` alike. Each row is
resolved again with `match.resolve_one` over `match_cli.library_view`, the
worker's consult, and a question the library raises goes through
`match_cli.adjudicate` under the job's own verb, so an answer a person already
gave still decides it. A row now held, deleted on purpose or held in another
version is counted as `owned_since`, `suppressed_since` or `offered_since`, on
a new `intake.missing.since` check, and is neither listed nor handed on.
`missing` is now what is still missing. The committed reports are not
rewritten, so `sync mark` reads what it read before. **The library as it is
now, not as the job froze it**: the code review found the first draft read the
frozen root, which refused a moved library as unmounted, and it now reads the
current configuration as `--list` and `sync mark` do. An absent music folder
refuses `library-volume-unmounted` before any row is asked again, and only
when there is a missing row to ask about; `intake.missing` declares
`library.mounted` to doctor.

**What the second run writes, decided here.** A library that gained nothing
writes the same bytes and is recognised, pinned by reading them. One that
gained every row writes nothing, names no download, answers `no_op`, and leaves
the first list where it was. One that gained some composes a shorter list,
which `listdoc.write` refuses over the job's earlier list of the same name,
since the name is fixed by the job; the refusal gains a step saying how many
rows were gained and to move that file aside. That is R-476's fixed name,
recorded there, and closes with it. Driven in
`test_rows_acquired_since_the_job_are_not_listed_and_name_no_download` and
`test_a_shorter_rerun_over_the_jobs_earlier_list_refuses_and_says_why`, with
nine more in `tests/test_intake_missing.py`. Mutation tables
`docs/mutation/r502-*.md`, summary in `r502-notes.md`: nineteen rows, the
author's own, every user facing row killing after two tests were fixed; two
maintainer zeros. The earlier list itself still names what was gained, and
`acquire download` over it still fetches it, which is out of this entry's
scope.

## R-503. An offered track never becomes listable, whatever the review answer

**Found:** 2026-09-19, sweep finding 114.1. Driven.

The offered check reads "offered for review and not listed until answered; see:
crate review list". Driven: a job with one offered row. `review list` showed
one `version-match` item, `review resolve --verdict rejected` answered ok, and
`review list` came back empty. A second `intake missing` still counted
`offered 1, written 2`. Resuming the succeeded job answered exit 0 and changed
nothing, and a third listing read the same.

**Measured cost:** the check promises a path that does not exist. A track held
in another version, which a person has said is not the one they want, never
reaches a download list from that job. The only route is to queue the whole
playlist again. One correction to the sweep's wording: resuming a succeeded
job does not refuse, it answers ok and does nothing.

**Why not fixed here.** The sweep session records and does not change code.

**Closes when:** a rejected version match makes its row listable on the next
`intake missing`, read from the review store at listing time, or the check
stops promising it and names what a person must do instead.

**CLOSED 2026-09-19 on `relay/184`, by the first of the two.** The review key
did not need rebuilding: every report the worker has committed since U57 names
the item it offered, `review_item`, which is `adjudicate`'s own `held.item_id`.
`_listed` in `intake/missing_cli.py` now looks each offered report's item up
by that identifier through the new `_answered`, read only, opening the review
store only when a job has an offered row. An unanswered row stays offered on
the check it always had, nothing is asked again and the library is not walked,
so a job whose questions nobody answered lists as before. An answered row joins
the missing rows in the consult R-502 built, renamed `_asked_again`, in report
order and in one library walk, so the answer decides it as the worker would:
rejected is missing and listed unless a tombstone stands, a yes bound to a copy
still held is owned, a yes about a copy that is gone stays a question. The
counts say what each row is now, `offered` is what is still a question, and
the new `answered_missing`, `answered_owned`, `answered_suppressed` and
`answered_offered` say how many got there by an answer, on a new
`intake.missing.answered` check. The offered check now ends "see: crate review
list, then list this again". The reports are not rewritten. `--job` and
`--run` share `_listed`, so both have it.

**The refusal over the job's earlier list, found by the code review.** A
rejected row makes the job's list longer than an earlier copy of the same name,
which `listdoc.write` refuses (the fixed name is R-476 and R-508, out of scope).
The first draft said why from counts of what changed since the JOB ran, which
says nothing about when the earlier LIST was written: a rejected row listed and
then landed refused with no reason, and a row gained after a listing already
naming an answered row was reported as new to it. The step is now read from the
earlier list document itself, by the new `_changed_since`: the tracks it names
that this one does not, and the reverse, by name. An earlier file that is not a
list gives no reason rather than a wrong one. R-502's step was reworded with
it, since it had the same shape.

Driven in `test_an_offered_row_rejected_since_is_listed_and_no_longer_offered`,
`test_an_offered_row_accepted_since_is_owned_and_not_listed`,
`test_an_offered_row_nobody_answered_is_unchanged_and_asks_nothing` and
`test_a_run_lists_an_offered_row_a_person_answered_as_a_job_does`, with five
more in `tests/test_intake_missing.py`. Mutation tables
`docs/mutation/r503-a.md` and `r503-b.md`, summary in `r503-notes.md`:
twenty one rows, the author's own, every user facing row killing, three
maintainer zeros. The same shape one file over was looked for: `sync mark`
already resolves an offered report against the library at marking time, so it
does not carry this defect.

## R-504. The hearts listing returns short with no error when the provider withholds unservable hearts

**Found:** 2026-09-19, sweep finding 115.2. Driven at the adapter with a fake
provider shaped as R-383 measured the real one.

`TidalCatalogue.favourite_tracks` says "this read is complete or it raises".
`listing.favorite_tracks` ends its walk on `get_tracks_count`, which counts
hearts the provider will not serve, and each page leaves those hearts out.
Driven: 197 declared, 12 unservable, two pages read, 185 rows returned, nothing
raised. Nothing compares the rows returned with the declared total.

**Measured cost:** the job reports owned, offered and missing over the short
listing as if it were the account, and the withheld hearts appear nowhere, not
as missing and not as a warning. The `Catalogue.favourite_tracks` contract
promises completeness. The sweep says the guide repeats the promise, and a
search of `docs/GUIDE.md` found no such sentence. R-383 measured the mechanism live on
this account at 197 against 93. R-423 owes the live count to an attended
sitting, and this entry does not change that. The size of the shortfall on the
live account today was not measured here.

**Why not fixed here.** The sweep session records and does not change code.

**Closes when:** the hearts read compares what it returned with the declared
total and carries the difference to the verb as a failing check or a warning
naming the count, and the contract says what the read can and cannot
promise.

**CLOSED 2026-09-19 on `relay/185`.** Every half of the closing line is built
and driven. `listing.favorite_tracks_declared` returns the rows with the count
the walk ended on, recorded as the walk asked for it rather than read again,
and `None` where the provider published no usable count. The adapter compares
them and a short listing raises the new seam exception
`catalogue.HeartsShortfall`, carrying the rows it did serve and the count, with
one spelling of the numbers, "197 declared, 185 listed, 12 withheld by the
provider". An exception and not a second return shape, so a caller that does
not know it still fails closed as an unreadable listing.
`favourite_tracks_or_refuse` catches it first and returns the rows beside it.
`crate intake playlist favorites` queues what came back and carries an
`intake-hearts-withheld` warning naming the three numbers and a `shortfall`
block under `progress`, and a listing where EVERY heart was withheld is a
no-op that still warns rather than reading as an account with none. `crate
sync all`'s inbound block gains `shortfall`, and its check fails naming the
same numbers, including over an empty listing, where it used to say the
account lists no hearts. The seam contract now says the read promises every
heart the provider serves and raises when that is fewer than it counts.
Nothing pads the listing or guesses which hearts were withheld. Driven with a
fake shaped as R-383 measured the provider, 197 counted and 12 left out of the
pages, through the real adapter and the real dispatcher in
`tests/test_label_tidal_catalogue.py`, and at the seam in
`tests/test_intake_missing.py` and `tests/test_sync_all.py`. Mutation tables
`docs/mutation/r504-a.md` and `r504-b.md`, 22 rows, 22 killing, the author's
own. **Still open:** the job the short listing queues does not carry the
count, so `intake missing` over it says nothing of the withheld hearts; the
warning says so in its own words. R-423 still owes the live count, and R-516
records the decision to fail the check rather than warn.

## R-511. The provider client drops an ISRC's unreadable ids before the adapter can count them

**Found:** 2026-09-19, sweep finding 123.10. Confirmed by reading the installed
client, tidalapi 0.8.11. Not driven against the provider.

`Session.get_tracks_by_isrc` reads each id the open API files under the ISRC
with `self.track(id)`, and on `ObjectNotFound` it continues to the next id. So
an ISRC filed under ids A and B, where the read of B answers not found in this
region, comes back as `[A]`. `tracks_for_isrc` returns what it was handed, and
`intake missing` lists the row as naming exactly one id.

**Measured cost:** unmeasured live. The rule that a row is listed only when
its ISRC names one distinct id cannot be guaranteed by the adapter, because
the narrowing happens inside the client. The sweep's second half, that a
single id whose track is not streamable is listed and fails only at download,
was not checked. R-477 records that two ISRC readers disagree, not this.

**Why not fixed here.** The sweep session records and does not change code.

**Closes when:** the adapter reads the open API answer itself, or counts the
ids before the per id reads, so a dropped id is seen and the row is handed on
as several, or an attended sitting shows the case does not occur.

## R-512. An absent music folder is read as an empty library by `match run` and by the intake worker, so every owned track reports missing with a clean exit

**Found:** 2026-09-19, at U103's code review. DRIVEN on both producers.

`match.index_library` guards its walk with `if root.is_dir()` and returns an
empty index when the folder is not there. `match_cli.library_view` hands that
index on with nothing said. Two shipped paths resolve against it. `match run`
over a one line list whose track the library holds reported `[1, 0, 0]`,
matched, needs review, missing, and after the music folder was removed
reported `[0, 0, 1]` with outcome ok, exit 0 and no warning. An `intake set`
job queued over three identified tracks and resumed with the music folder
gone ended `succeeded`, exit 0, `owned 0, offered 0, missing 3`. The producer
is an external library volume that is not mounted, which is the ordinary state
of a laptop away from its drive. `intake missing --list`, `acquire fallback`
and, since U103, `intake identify` each refuse this state as
`library-volume-unmounted` in their own verb, which is three copies of a check
the shared view does not make.

**Measured cost:** the product says something false, board bar (b). Every
owned track in a list is reported missing, and the next step reads `missing`
and acquires it again. Not measured against a real unmounted volume, where
the library ROOT is absent and `config.load` may refuse first; the drive
removed the music folder under a root that was there.

**Why not fixed here.** Outside U103's brief, and the fix belongs in
`match_cli.library_view`, which eight call sites in seven modules share
(`git grep` on this branch: `fallback_cli`, `match_cli`, `intake/cli`,
`missing_cli`, `label/approved_cli`, `label/cli`, `label/sweep`,
`sync/mark_cli`), so it is a unit with its own table rather than a line in
somebody else's. The label and sync callers were NOT driven.

**Closes when:** the shared view refuses an absent music folder once, the
three verb level copies call it, and `match run` and the intake worker are
driven refusing. **An issue is owed for this entry**, since it meets the board
bar and a Relay session cannot file one after the merge that carries it.

## R-513. The recognition cache key leaves out the account, the cache is never evicted, and its lock is pinned by a file and not by an exclusion

**Found:** 2026-09-19, during U103 and at its code review.

Three facts about `intake/acrcloud.py`'s `RecognitionCache`, none driven
against a real account. (1) The key is the recording's bytes and the chunk
plan, host included, and NOT the access key. A person who points the same host
at a second project with a different catalogue bucket is served the first
project's answers. It was left out on purpose: putting it in means retrieving
the credential before the cache is read, and a fully kept pass would prompt
the keychain to spend nothing. `--refresh` is the way out. (2) Nothing evicts a
document. One is about a megabyte for a two hour set, written 0600 under the
installation state directory, so the cost is disk and is measured in sets
identified. (3) Mutation row A17, the cache write without its sibling lock,
was DROPPED from table a rather than run, because the only test that could see
it asserts the lock file exists, which pins the file and not the exclusion.
The merge itself is measured, row A10, one death.

**Measured cost:** none measured. (1) is a stale tracklist for somebody who
changes ACRCloud project and does not pass `--refresh`, which nobody using
this product is known to do.

**Closes when:** the key carries something that names the account without
retrieving a secret, or the attended binding shows one project per host is
the only case; and a test holds the lock from a second process and shows the
writer waits.

## R-514. `intake identify` names its tracklist on the warnings channel, and goes pending where `intake set` does not

**Found:** 2026-09-19, during U103. Two decisions a session made because
nobody could be asked, recorded with the options.

(1) `match/1` is closed at three arrays and `payload_problems` refuses an
undeclared field, so the tracklist's path has no field to ride in. The options
were a fourth field, which moves the schema fingerprint and every `match`
consumer, a move of the verb to `diagnostic/1` on `intake missing`'s
precedent, which breaks whoever reads identify's three arrays, or a note on
the warnings channel. The third was taken as the conservative one. The human
renderer prints it as `warning [tracklist-written]`, and it prints nothing
else of a match payload, so a person at a terminal sees a warning that is not
one and no tracks at all. The same is true of `recognition-cached`.

(2) The brief said identify resolves "with the same rule `intake set` uses".
The engine rule is the same, one `library_view`, `resolve_one` per row,
`adjudicate`. What differs is the exit: the intake worker reports an offered
track and ends ok, and identify now ends PENDING_HUMAN over an open version
question, because it shares `match run`'s whole step and R11's argument, that
a caller reading `missing` next never learns four tracks were a version away
from owned, applies to identify's caller as it does to match's.

**Measured cost:** none measured. A script that treated a non zero exit from
identify as a failure would now stop on a set holding a version question.

**Closes when:** the human renderer renders a match payload and a note that is
not a warning has a channel, and a person says whether identify should gate.

## R-515. A playlist or release listing returns short with no error when the provider withholds unservable tracks

**Found:** 2026-09-19, on `relay/185` while closing R-504, hunting the same
shape one file over.

`listing.playlist_tracks` ends on `num_tracks`, which counts tracks the
provider will not serve, and each window leaves those tracks out, which is
the argument its own docstring makes for the declared total stop rule. It
compares nothing with that count. Driven at the listing: a playlist declaring
10 with 2 left out of its window returned 8 rows and raised nothing. Three
readers take it: `harvest.playlist_tracks`, which `intake playlist <id>`, the
`sync all` playlists sweep and `label harvest` list through, the adapter's
`release_tracks`, and the outbound account's playlist read.

**Measured cost:** driven at the listing and NOT at the verb. By the same path
R-504 had, `intake playlist <id>` would report owned, offered and missing over
the short listing as if it were the playlist, and the withheld tracks would
appear nowhere. How often a real playlist holds a track the account cannot
play was not measured. The outbound `has_heart` reads the hearts through
`listing.favorite_tracks` without the comparison R-504 added, so a withheld
heart reads as not hearted there; whether a sweep can reach such a track was
not measured either.

**Meets the board bar**, (b), a clean report over state the tool could not
read. **Its issue is owed**, since a Relay session cannot file one after the
merge that carries this entry.

**Closes when:** the playlist and release reads compare their rows with the
declared count and carry a shortfall to each verb that lists through them, as
R-504 does for the hearts, or an attended sitting shows the provider never
withholds from a playlist.

## R-516. The hearts inbound check fails on every pass while the provider withholds any heart

**Found:** 2026-09-19, the code review on `relay/185`, not driven against a
live account.

R-504's brief asked for a failing check, and `sync all`'s `favorites inbound`
row now fails whenever the hearts listing comes back short, with no remedy,
since nothing a person does makes the provider serve an unplayable track. The
review's point: if the live account permanently holds hearts the provider will
not serve, which R-383's 197 against the pages suggests, that row fails on
every pass and never clears, and a row that always fails teaches a person to
ignore the rows that fail for a reason, such as a listing that could not be
read at all. `intake playlist favorites` carries the same fact as a warning on
an ok run, so the two verbs grade it differently.

The options were a fail as briefed, a note, which renders as `note` and is
easy to miss over a listing that is not the account, or a fail only when the
count withheld grows past what the last pass saw, which needs a remembered
count this unit does not keep. The brief's fail was kept as the conservative
one, since the cost R-504 records is a report that passes off a short listing
as the account.

**Measured cost:** none measured. The live count is R-423's.

**Closes when:** a person says whether a steady withholding should fail the
row, note it, or fail only when it changes, and the check does that.

## R-517. A credited tombstone written before the companion existed still misses the provider shape

**Found:** 2026-09-19, the code review on `relay/179`, and driven:
`test_a_tombstone_that_already_stood_gains_no_companion`.

R-431 closed by having the recorder write a companion beside a credited
tombstone. The companion is written in the same write as the tombstone and
only when the tombstone is, so a tombstone that already stands gains nothing
when the same deletion is recorded again. And a deletion run does not record
it again anyway: `tombstone_predicate` reads the standing record as "a run
already recorded this" and retires the row. So every credited deletion made
before this build keeps R-431's cost in full. The provider shape resolves
missing, `intake missing` lists it, and the next download fetches back a file
somebody removed.

**Why not fixed there.** The other rule, write the companion whenever it is
absent, brings back a companion a person lifted on its own the next time a
duplicate row of that version is deleted, behind their back, which the review
also raised and which is driven in
`test_a_companion_lifted_alone_does_not_come_back_behind_a_persons_back`. And
a read that repairs the store is a read that can fail while a person is only
asking a question, which `tombstone_predicate` argues. What is missing is a
deliberate backfill.

**Measured cost:** board bar (a) and (b), for each credited tombstone already
in a store. How many the live store holds was not counted, since a session
does not read it.

**Meets the board bar. Its issue is owed**, since METHOD files an issue after
the merge that carries the entry and a Relay session exits before that merge.

**Closes when:** a verb, a backfill flag on `crate tombstone list` or a step
of `crate doctor`, walks the standing `version` records, writes the companion
each one strips to where none has ever existed, stamps the pointer, and says
how many it wrote. A companion that exists and was lifted is left lifted.

## R-518. The label sweep asks the tombstone store under the verbatim kind only

**Found:** 2026-09-19, the code review on `relay/179`. Read, not driven.

`label/sweep.py` builds its own consult, `tombstone.version_identity` over a
release's artist and title under `KIND_VERSION`, and never asks for a
companion. A release a label crawl returns as `Aurora Bloom` and `Sun Path
(Nightwave Remix)`, against a deleted library row that kept `(feat. Mira)`,
would miss and be queued, which is R-431's cost arriving by the other
entrance. `test_a_companion_is_never_the_answer_to_a_verbatim_lookup` pins the
miss on purpose: the sweep has no notion of whether a release spelled a credit
or billed a guest, and asking without those two guards is the over eager
direction.

**Measured cost:** unmeasured. A release is an album or a single, its title is
rarely a track's title with a mix name, and no producer of the colliding shape
was driven. It does not meet the board bar until one is.

**Closes when:** the sweep is driven with a single whose title is the stripped
title of a credited deletion, and either it asks for the companion behind the
same two guards `Wanted.uncredited_spellings` holds, or the drive shows the
shape does not arrive.

## R-519. A listing that names a guest anywhere cannot reach the companion of the deletion crediting that same guest

**Found:** 2026-09-19, on `relay/179`, as the cost of R-431's guards. Driven
in the refusing direction only.

A companion has had its guest taken out, so it cannot say which guest the
deleted row credited, and a listing that names any guest is therefore turned
away from it: a bracketed credit in the title, or a provider row billing more
than one artist. That is right when the guest differs and a miss when it is
the same one. The shapes that still resolve missing and are listed for
download:

- the provider bills `[Aurora Bloom, Mira]` with the title `Sun Path` and no
  credit in it, and the library row read `Sun Path (feat. Mira) (Nightwave
  Remix)`;
- the provider spells `(feat. Mira)` and the library row spelled `(ft. Mira)`
  or `[feat. Mira]`, so the verbatim consult misses on the spelling and the
  companion is not asked;
- the library row spelled its credit with no bracket, `Sun Path feat. Mira`,
  which `uncredited_title` leaves alone, so no companion is written at all;
- a payload the intake froze before `several_artists` existed, which thaws as
  billed.

Each is a missed suppression that is reported, the direction `tombstone_fold`
accepts, and each is R-431's own cost for the row it happens to.

**Measured cost:** board bar (a) and (b) where it lands. How often a provider
bills a guest without spelling it in the title was not measured, and the live
account is not a session's to read.

**Closes when:** the companion carries the folded names of the guests it
dropped, and the consult asks for it from a listing whose own guests, read
from its title and its artists list, fold to the same names. Or an attended
sitting counts the hearts that bill a guest and shows the share is small
enough to leave.

## R-520. `tests/test_deletion.py` fails one test on some full parallel runs

**Found:** 2026-09-19, on `relay/179`. The same family as R-470.

Two of six full `pytest` runs on this branch reported one failure, each time
a different test of `tests/test_deletion.py` that opens a real disposable
database: `test_delete_review_trashes_a_confirmed_file`, which exited 10
where it expects 0, and `test_the_real_binding_answers_the_version_columns_too`,
which reddened `scripts/mutate.py`'s baseline and refused table b once. Both
pass alone, the file passed three times in a row under `-n auto` beside
`tests/test_rebuild.py`, and the other four full runs were green. Whether
`main` does the same was not measured, since a Relay session does not leave
its branch.

**Measured cost.** Maintainer facing: a red battery over a sound tree, and a
refused mutation batch. The cause was not investigated.

**Seen again 2026-09-19 on `relay/182`, in a different file.** The null
control of mutation table `r501-d` killed 25 tests on its full suite run, every
one of them in `tests/test_rebuild.py`, which that branch does not touch, and
the driver declared the batch invalid. The file then passed alone three times
in three, 103 each, and the rerun of the batch was clean with a null control of
zero. Four full suite runs on that branch outside the driver were green. The
error text was not captured, since the driver records node ids and not
tracebacks. So the family is wider than `tests/test_deletion.py`.

**Seen a third time 2026-09-19, on `relay/111`, in the same file as the
second.** Mutation table `r424`'s `B4_warning_copied` row is a promoted zero:
it killed nothing on its own subset, and its full suite run reported 20 kills,
every one of them in `tests/test_rebuild.py`, which that branch does not touch
and which has no path to the line the row mutated. This time the null control
did NOT fire, so the batch was not declared invalid and the number was
reported as that row's. Driven afterwards: the same mutation applied to the
same site with `PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE=1` set leaves `tests/test_rebuild.py`
passing 103, and so does the restored file, and the branch's own full battery
is green at 8865. So this family can also present as a plausible looking death
count on an unrelated row rather than as a refused batch, which is the worse
shape: a batch that refuses is noticed, and a row that reports 20 deaths on a
line nothing guards reads as coverage.

**Seen a third time 2026-09-19 on `relay/180`.** The null control of mutation
table `r432-a` killed 20 on its full suite run, every one in
`tests/test_rebuild.py`, which that branch does not touch, and the batch was
declared invalid. The rerun was clean, null control zero of 8857, and so was
table b's. Two full suite runs on that branch outside the driver were green.
Still no error text, for the same reason.

**Closes when:** the state those tests race on under `-n auto` is found and
isolated, which R-470's closing line may already cover.

## R-522. `intake missing --job` over a job queued for another library rechecks it against this one

**Found:** 2026-09-19, on `relay/183`, R-502, while deciding which
configuration the recheck reads. Read, not driven.

`--run` keeps only the jobs queued for the current library's volume, and
`--job` has never compared the job's `library_id` with the current one. Before
R-502 that wrote another library's missing rows into this library's staging.
Now each row is also asked of THIS library, so a track this library holds and
the other does not drops out of the other library's list as owned since.

**Measured cost:** unmeasured. It needs two libraries on one installation and
a person naming the other library's job by hand. Nothing is deleted, and the
worst case is a list short of a track the other library wanted.

**Closes when:** `--job` refuses a job queued for another library, as `--run`
already filters one out.

## R-523. An unmapped row whose file is gone refuses `name apply` even under a folder that is on this machine

**Found:** 2026-09-19, on `relay/181`, R-500, while narrowing what dark means.
Driven, and pinned by `test_an_unmapped_row_whose_file_is_gone_refuses_even_outside_a_volume`.

A row recorded outside the library root under no rule is dark when its file is
absent. That is right for a volume that was renamed, and it also catches a
track imported from a downloads folder whose file was later moved or deleted:
the folder exists here, the recorded spelling is one this machine uses, and
the verb still refuses until a rule maps that folder onto itself.

**Measured cost:** unmeasured on a real library. One such row stops `name
apply` for every folder until a person writes a rule, and an identity rule is
not something the refusal's steps spell out. The deletion pass has the same
friction over the same row. Nothing is renamed wrongly, the cost is a verb
that will not run. **This meets board bar (c) and is owed an issue after the
merge**, which a Relay session cannot open because the number is not on
`main` until the runner merges.

**The options, a person's call.** Keep it, the conservative reading taken
here. Or answer a row whose leading prefix exists on this machine, the anchor
idea the deletion pass already uses to tell a missing file from a dead volume:
`/Volumes/VOLUME` absent is dark, a home folder present with the file gone is a
row that names nothing. The risk in the second is a row stranded earlier by a
move into the library, which is already stranded.

**Closes when:** one of the two is chosen and pinned, and if the first, the
refusal's steps say how to declare a folder outside the library.

**CLOSED 2026-09-23 on `unit/issue178`, inside R-675's fix, by a third option
neither paragraph above named.** A dark row refuses only when its file name is
the name of a file the pass would rename, because a renamed volume or a moved
mount changes a path's prefix and never its leaf, so a row under another name
cannot be a candidate under another spelling. A gone file under a folder on
this machine therefore refuses when the row carries a candidate's name and
passes when it does not, and the anchor idea was not needed. Pinned by
`test_a_gone_file_under_a_folder_on_this_machine_refuses_under_a_candidate_name`
and `test_a_gone_file_under_another_name_refuses_nothing`. Measured on the
live library: 184 tombstones and 9 rows under two home folders, none under a
staging file's name.

## R-524. A dark tombstoned row refuses `name apply`, and the deletion pass skips the same row

**Found:** 2026-09-19, on `relay/181`, by the built in review of R-500. Driven,

`name apply` counts a tombstone as a reference, U67's rule, because a restore
brings the row back pointing at what it recorded. So a track imported once
from a stick and deleted in rekordbox years ago is dark and refuses the verb.

resolved. R-500's goal was that the two writers agree about an unmapped row,

under a volume that is gone was not counted. The remedy works, a rule for the
dead volume, and it is an odd thing to ask for.

to a warning in the plan, or is passed over, and a test pins it.

**CLOSED 2026-09-23 on `unit/issue178`, inside R-675's fix: a dark tombstone
refuses, on the same condition as a live row.** It counts, because a restore
brings it back pointing at what it recorded, and it refuses only when its file
name is one the pass would rename (R-675), so the odd remedy is asked for only

skips the same row, R-500's deliberate difference, unchanged.

## R-526. `name apply` reads the collection after the tree walk, so a refusal over a dark row costs the whole walk first

**Found:** 2026-09-19, on `relay/181`, R-500. The brief asked for the refusal
before the tree walk and this is where it was not followed.

U67 pinned that the collection is read only when something would be renamed,
`test_an_empty_folder_needs_no_database`, and with no candidate a dark row
cannot change the outcome. Reading first would either break that or need the
read's refusal deferred past the walk. So the walk, which reads tags from
every audio file, still runs before the collection is opened. The refusal does
precede every plan item and every rename.

**Measured cost:** not timed. On a fresh setup pointed at a whole library it
is one full tag read across the tree, then a refusal, then the same walk
again after the rule is written. Sweep finding 112.6 is the same ordering
seen from the other side.

**Closes when:** the collection is read before the walk with the unreadable
case deferred until a candidate exists, or the ordering is kept and timed.

**Found:** 2026-09-19, on `relay/181`, by the built in review of R-500, against

## R-528. A landing whose import is proven stays an open session until a tree cuts over

**Found:** 2026-09-19, by R-501's unit on `relay/182`. A decision recorded, with
the option not taken. Driven.

`crate intake imported` cannot close the run it proves before a cutover,
because `routing_pass.close_run` refuses a run holding a deferred placement and
only a database native tree can place one. The unit left the run `open` with
`detail["import_verified"]` recorded, and taught the cutover precheck to excuse
a run that is open, holds no capture and carries that key. Doctor's session
check labels such a run "import proven, placement waits for a cutover".

**Measured cost.** One non terminal session record per landing until the first
cutover. Doctor lists every one of them at INFO. `restore.prune` with no owning
session named refuses while any exists; a search of `src` found no caller that
passes none, so that is not reachable from a shipped verb today. Every future
reader of `not record.terminal` has to know to ask
`owes_only_deferred_routing`, and nothing makes it.

**The options.** (1) What was built, a detail key on an `open` record. (2) A
sixth `SessionState`, say `awaiting-routing`, which makes the state first class
and costs a session log schema question, since a build that predates the state
cannot parse a record carrying it and the strict gate refuses on an entry it
cannot read. (3) Let the gated close through when no tree is native, which
changes U19's close for every caller and which its own tests pin against. The
built in review raised (2) as the deeper fix. (1) was taken as the conservative
call in an unattended session, because it changes no gate that guards a write.

**Closes when:** a person picks, or the first cutover lands and `route pending`
is driven closing these runs on a real library.

playlist node inside a file is matched to a run's tracks exactly and that is

**Found:** 2026-09-19, by R-501's unit on `relay/182`. A decision recorded.

An intake file is a whole collection export plus the landed rows, so it is as

leaves it at the library root, or beside the track for `intake file`.

**Measured cost.** Not measured on a real library. One export sized file per

## R-531. A landing's pending action is persisted on the intake session and still not on the run record

**Found:** 2026-09-19, sweep finding 117.2, half closed by R-501's unit on
`relay/182`.

The finding was that the `rekordbox_import` action went only onto the printed
envelope. It is now persisted on the intake session by `mark_awaiting_import`,
the envelope carries that same action read back, and doctor's session check
names every run still `awaiting-import`. It is still not assigned to
`ctx.run.pending`, so `crate run show` and doctor's run findings show nothing
for the landing's run.

**Why not fixed here.** Nothing clears a run record's pending action. Set
there, doctor would report the run as awaiting an import for ever, after the
import was proven, which is the product saying something false. Clearing it

rewriting it, a seam no verb has today.

**Measured cost.** None driven. The unimported file is remembered durably, on
the session and not the run.

**Closes when:** a verb can settle another run's pending action, or the run
surfaces read the session's.

## R-534. Two landings of one staging folder under two batch names are not kept apart

**Found:** 2026-09-19, by the `/code-review` of R-432's unit on `relay/180`.
Read, not driven.

`crate intake land` locks the BATCH NAME, which is what R-432 asked for, and
the default batch name is the run id, unique per run. So two landings started
over the same staging folder with no `--name` take two different locks, both
pass the engine's staleness check, and both rename out of one folder. Nothing
is overwritten, since the two batch folders differ, which is why this is not
R-432. `os.replace` has one winner per file. Both runs walk the files in the
same order, so with two fresh batch folders the loser fails on the first file,
having moved nothing, and is refused saying so. The loser can have moved a file
first only when the winner skipped one as occupied, which needs a batch folder
that already held that name.

**Measured cost:** none measured. By reading, a refused run and no lost file.
It does not meet the board bar.

**Closes when:** the verb also holds a lock keyed on the resolved staging
folder, or the two landing case is driven and the refusal it ends in is judged
enough.

## R-535. What the batch lock gives up, one zero row, and three rows not measured

**Found:** 2026-09-19, on `relay/180`, by the review and the author's mutation
tables. Maintainer facing except where it says otherwise.

**No lock on a platform with no `fcntl`.** `jobs.driver_lock` proceeds unlocked
there, which its own docstring defends for jobs because a claim is still a
transaction. A landing has no second guard, so on such a platform R-432's
window is as it was, and `docs/GUIDE.md` says two landings under one name never
run at once with no such limit. Not driven, since no such platform was to hand.
Refusing instead would make the verb unusable there. This half is user facing
and is the one that should be decided by a person.

**The key is the name and not the folder.** One batch name in two libraries on
one machine shares a lock, so the second is refused though its folder is
another one. That refuses a safe landing and never admits an unsafe one. Keying
on the resolved target was not taken, because two spellings of one path that
resolve differently would then admit two landings into one folder.

**One lock file per batch name stays for good.** About sixty bytes each, one
per landing, since the default name is unique per run and a lock file is never
unlinked, for the reason every lock here gives.

**An error from `flock` that is not contention arrives untyped.** Read, not
driven. It is raised before the first move. The unwritable state directory WAS
driven and is refused by name as `path-permission-denied`, pinned by
`test_a_lock_directory_this_account_cannot_write_refuses_by_name_and_moves_nothing`.

**Row A4, zero, the author could not kill it.** Dropping the release in
`batch_lock`'s `finally` kills nothing of 8857, twice, because CPython frees
the finished generator's frame and closes the descriptor at the same moment.
The composite A4c, the release dropped and the lock object kept alive, kills 7,
so a lock that outlives its `with` is held. The explicit release is kept for an
interpreter that does not count references.

**Three considered rows were logged as dropped and NOT MEASURED** in
`docs/mutation/r432-b-rows.toml`: the snapshot role of the state entry, a
reword of the refusal sentence, and the three other members of `_holder`'s
tolerated exceptions, which would likely read zero since only the empty lock
file is driven.

**Closes when:** a person decides what a landing does with no `fcntl`, and the
rest is either accepted at a retro or measured.

## R-536. `sync.favorites` declares destruction while writing only an add-only remote surface

**Found:** 2026-09-19, on `relay/111`, while closing the residual "`crate sync
favorites` declares a local colour and tag write it never performs". Raised by
the narrowing rather than by a drive.

The entry's `writes` came down to `remote`, and `destructive=True` stayed. The
flag is declarative: its only reader in `src` is the registry's own validation,
which forces it on for a verb that writes `files` or whose name begins with
`delete.`, and neither is now true here. Conformance 6 quantifies over it and
drives the shared session gates rather than the verb, so nothing about a live
run changes either way.

Two readings, and the argument runs both ways. KTD24 binds the destructive
gates to DESTRUCTION, and this verb destroys nothing: the engine has no remove
path, an argument shaped like one is recognised and ignored, and a heart is
added or left alone. `export.playlist`, the sibling that writes the same remote
surface and the same outbound ledger through the same shell, has never declared
it. Against that, the verb writes an account a person cannot roll back from
this side, and dropping the flag takes the verb out of the population a reader
would call dangerous.

**The decision taken here, conservatively.** The flag stays. Removing it is
narrowing a claim in the cautious direction, which is a different act from
removing a claim that was false, and this unit's brief is the second. Whether
an add-only remote write is destruction under KTD24 is a person's call.

**Measured cost:** none on any driven path. The suite is green with the flag
set, and the flag reaches no runtime branch.

**Closes when:** a person decides whether an add-only remote write is
destruction, and the entry either keeps the flag with that reason recorded or
drops it and joins `export.playlist`.

## R-537. A detached resume's report reaches the job log and never the terminal

**Found:** 2026-09-19, on `relay/111`, by the review of the closure above.
Read from the source and confirmed against `cli/jobs.resume`, not driven.

`crate job resume JOB_ID` reconciles, spawns the child through `jobs.spawn` and
returns an envelope carrying the job id, the state and any drift warning. The
child's own envelope, which is where a long running verb says what it did and
what it could not do, goes to `jobs.log_path(job_id)` under the queue root. No
verb surfaces that file: the shipped job verbs are `list`, `show`, `resume` and
`cancel`, and `show` carries the job's cause and not its output.

The closure above put a standing warning on `sync.favorites` saying the sweep
writes nothing in the library. It is on the queueing pass, which a person
always reads, and on the resume, which in the documented flow they do not. The
guide now says so rather than implying every report carries it, which is the
honest half; the other half is that a person who resumes a job has no shipped
way to read what that job printed.

**Measured cost:** unmeasured on a live run. Read from the source: any warning
a long running verb emits on its resume is invisible to a person who resumed it
through the documented command, not only this one.

**Closes when:** a verb surfaces a job's log, or the guide's resume section says
where the file is and a person is expected to open it themselves.

## R-538. A fetched mix is converted to MP3 whole before it is cut into chunks

**Found:** 2026-09-19, on `relay/149`, U104, by the code review. Read from the
source, NOT driven: driving it is a real download, which is attended.

The mix download is U80's argv with two edits, and U80's argv extracts the
audio and converts it to MP3 at the best quality setting. For one track that is
the file the library keeps. For a mix it is a file cut into chunks by ffmpeg
and then removed, so the conversion spends minutes of processor time on a lossy
to lossy encode of something nobody keeps, and the audio that gets
fingerprinted is one generation worse than the upload.

The alternative is to fetch the best audio stream as it is and let ffmpeg carve
from whatever container arrives. It was not applied, for two reasons. The
conversion is the source system's argv, run against the real services for a
long time, and the alternative has never been run here at all. And `landed_in`
accepts one MP3 exactly, so the landing rule would have to learn what else a
recording can be called.

**Measured cost:** unmeasured. No download was made.

**Closes when:** one real address is fetched both ways at an attended sitting,
and either the conversion is kept with its measured cost recorded, or the
stream is fetched as it is and the landing rule is widened to match.

## R-539. Whether a second fetch of one mix reproduces the bytes the recognition cache is keyed to is not known

**Found:** 2026-09-19, on `relay/149`, U104, while deciding when the scratch
folder is removed. NOT driven, for the reason R-538 gives.

The recognition cache is keyed by a digest of the recording's bytes. A fetched
mix is removed however the pass ends, so `intake identify` of an address
followed by `intake set` of the same address fetches twice, and so does a
second run after a pass that raised. If the two downloads are byte for byte the
same, the second pass is free, which is what U103 promises for a recording on
this machine. If the encoder's output differs at all, every chunk is paid for
again and nothing says so beforehand.

The scratch folder is removed on a raised pass too. Keeping it would have kept
the bytes the paid answers are keyed to, in a folder under the state root that
no verb shows a person, at a few hundred megabytes a mix. Removal was chosen as
the conservative half.

**Measured cost:** unmeasured. At worst, one full set of recognition calls per
repeat pass over an address.

**Closes when:** the same address is fetched twice at an attended sitting and
the two digests are compared. If they differ, the cache needs a key for a
fetched mix that is not its bytes, or the fetched file has to outlive the pass.

## R-540. `doctor` cannot say whether this machine can take a mix address

**Found:** 2026-09-19, on `relay/149`, U104. A decision recorded, not a defect
driven.

`intake.set` and `intake.identify` do not declare `binary.yt-dlp` in
`doctor_checks`. A declared check is one doctor FAILS the verb on, and only an
address needs the downloader, so declaring it would fail doctor on a machine
that identifies every recording it is handed. The cost of not declaring it is
that doctor passes a machine where `crate intake set` refuses an address. The
refusal is free, arrives before any fetch or spend, and carries the install
hint, which is why this was the conservative call.

**Measured cost:** one refused command, no spend.

**Closes when:** the registry can declare a check that doctor reports without
failing the verb on it, or a person decides the downloader is required.

## R-542. Two passes over one address at the same moment share a scratch folder

**Found:** 2026-09-19, on `relay/149`, U104. Read from the source, not driven.

The scratch folder is named by a digest of the address and cleared before every
attempt, so that a process killed mid download is cleaned up by the next run of
the same address. The cost of that choice is that a second pass over the same
address, started while the first is still identifying, clears the first one's
recording. The first then fails inside the carver, loudly and with its answers
so far kept by the recognition cache, which is R-539's question again.

**Measured cost:** unmeasured. One failed pass, reachable only by running the
same address twice at once.

**Closes when:** the scratch folder is held under `jobs.driver_lock` for the
length of a pass, as `landing.batch_lock` holds a batch name, or a person
decides two passes at once over one address is not worth a lock.

## R-543. A mix left in scratch by a killed process stays until the same address is fetched again

**Found:** 2026-09-19, on `relay/149`, U104. Read from the source, not driven.

A pass that returns or raises removes its scratch folder. A process that is
killed cannot. What it leaves is outside the library and is cleared by the next
fetch of the SAME address, and by nothing else: no verb sweeps `mix_scratch`,
and doctor does not report what is in it. A person who never runs that address
again keeps a few hundred megabytes under the state root.

**Measured cost:** unmeasured. Disk space only, never library state.

**Closes when:** a fetch sweeps scratch folders older than a bound it can
defend, or doctor reports the folder's size.

## R-544. Thirteen containment checks compare resolved paths as text, and `resolve` does not settle letter case

**Found:** 2026-09-19, on `relay/149`, U104. The code review raised it against
U104's own guard, where it was DRIVEN on this machine and fixed. The thirteen
sites below were found by grep and were NOT driven, so their reachability is
unmeasured.

On a case insensitive volume, `Path.resolve` follows links and leaves letter
case as it was typed. A lower case spelling of a mixed case folder therefore
resolves to a path that is not textually inside it, and a guard of the shape
`root in path.parents`, or `is_relative_to`, passes. Driven: a temporary folder
`Library`, a scratch path spelled under `library`, the same folder by
`samefile`, and the textual check said outside. U104's guard now also asks
`samefile` of every ancestor that exists.

The same shape, by `grep` over `src` for a parents membership test or
`is_relative_to`: `core/config.py:2122`, `core/pool.py:656`,
`core/restore.py:381`, `635` and `2427`, `core/snapshot.py:279`,
`setbuilder/cli.py:184`, `cli/doctor.py:2182`, `intake/ingest.py:89`,
`intake/landing.py:352`, `354` and `366`, and `session/restore_cli.py:408`.
Several guard a write or a refusal: the snapshot store inside its own source,
a landing whose source is in staging, a restore outside the configured root.
Each is reached only when a person or a configuration spells one folder two
ways, which is ordinary on the volumes a DJ library sits on and is not the
same as likely.

**Measured cost:** one site driven and fixed. Thirteen read and not driven, so
"nothing reaches them" is NOT what this entry says.

**Closes when:** each site is driven with two spellings of one folder, and
either asks the filesystem as U104's guard does or is recorded as unreachable
with the drive that showed it. One shared helper is the likely shape.

## R-545. Only the deletion pass asserts the identity of a volume a prefix rule points at

**Found:** 2026-09-19, on `relay/152`, by the built in review of the mapped
volume gate and then a sweep of every `PrefixRule(` and `resolve_recorded_path`
caller under `src`. Read line by line, NOT driven, except where it says so.

`session.assert_gates` asserts the library root's volume and nothing else. The
deletion pass now also asserts every rule target. No other pass does. The review
claimed the My Tags pass writes tags into files on whatever disk a rule reaches.
Read to the write, that is false: nine sites were read and none writes, renames,
moves or deletes a file through a rule today.

- `write/metadata_cli.py`, `write/routing_cli.py` and
  `modules/outbound/source.py` READ tags through a rule, and what they read
  decides database rows, an emitted XML's buckets and ratings, and provider
  matching. A different disk at the target mostly answers "not a file" and the
  row is skipped. A clone answers with the same tags.
- `write/routing_pass.py`, `write/rebuild.py` and `write/trees.py` use the
  resolved path as a dictionary key only.
- `write/naming_cli.py` renames files from a walk of the library root. A
  resolved path only decides which files are held back.
- `adopt/apply.py` DOES write a tag into a rule resolved file, through
  `revert.write_tag_with_record`, inside a gated session. It is disarmed: the
  shipped worker passes no `tag_value` and the write is skipped without one.
  `adopt/revert.py` writes to a recorded path that came from a rule, and its
  verb was not traced to a registry entry.

**Measured cost:** none today, nine sites read and none driven, so this entry
says "none of nine writes through a rule", never "nothing does". It becomes a
cost the day adopt's tag write is armed.

**Why not fixed here.** The brief is the deletion pass. Moving the assertion
into `session.assert_gates` would cover every destructive session at once, and
would also start refusing sessions that never follow a rule over a detached
archive drive, which is the availability question the residual finding "Five
findings the U24 review accepted, and the reason each stands" records as open.

**Closes when:** the unit that arms adopt's tag write asserts
`session.assert_mapped_file_volume` before it, or the assertion moves into
`assert_gates` with the offline assertion that finding asks for.

## R-546. A volume nested under the library root is not asserted for the files inside it

**Found:** 2026-09-19, on `relay/152`. Read and NOT driven, so its reachability
is unmeasured.

The mapped volume gate probes the directory of each file that went through a
RULE. A file under the library root goes through no rule, and the root's own
assertion asks about the root directory's volume once at open and once at close.
So a second volume mounted at a directory inside the library root, or a
directory there symlinked onto another disk, holds files the deletion pass would
trash with only the outer volume identified. The same probe closes it: ask
`containing_mount` of the file's directory against `library.volume_id`.

**Measured cost:** none measured. The layout is unusual and nothing was driven
to show a shipped setup produces it.

**Why not fixed here.** The refusal for a root resident file is the library
volume's and lives in `session.assert_volume_identity`, which takes no path.
Giving it one changes the gate every destructive session shares.

**Closes when:** `assert_volume_identity` can be asked about a path under the
root, and the deletion pass asks it per file as it now does for a mapped one.

## R-547. Nothing records a rule's volume identity for a person, and a target inside the root by another spelling refuses as unrecorded

**Found:** 2026-09-19, on `relay/152`, while deciding what an existing
configuration meets on the day the gate arrives.

Two edges of one rule. A prefix rule whose target is outside the library root
and records no `volume_id` now refuses `delete review` and `delete apply` as
`mapped-volume-mismatch`. The refusal names the rule's config key and the
identity the disk shows now, so the way through is one line typed into the
configuration file by hand. Setup writes no `volume_id` for a rule, no verb
records one, and doctor does not report a rule that will refuse. A rule whose
target is inside the library root, which is what `docs/cutover.md` describes for
the live library, needs nothing and is not affected.

"Inside" is the resolver's lexical test on folded text. A target under the root
by another spelling, a symlink or a different letter case on a case insensitive
volume, is answered as outside and refuses the same way, with a sentence that
says "not under the library root as configuration spells it". That errs toward
asking, on purpose, and it is the same two spellings shape the residual finding
about `Path.resolve` and letter case records for thirteen other sites.

**Measured cost:** a refusal with its remedy in it, on two verbs, for a
configuration with a rule onto another directory outside the root. Not driven
against a real configuration: the live one was not read.

**Closes when:** setup or a verb records a rule's identity from the mounted
volume the way setup records the library's, through `identity_source`, and
doctor names a rule that the deletion pass would refuse.

## R-549. The archive rotation purges the newest dated archive when a stray folder sorts after it

**Found:** 2026-09-19, on `relay/153`, looking for the shape this unit fixed one
function over. `latest_snapshot` sorted every folder name under the snapshot root
and took the last, so a folder made by hand was the newest snapshot.
`_prune_archive` in `modules/tools/backup.py` has the same line on the path that
DELETES: it sorts every name `lsf` returns under the archive root and purges all
but the last `archive_keep`.

**Driven at the engine, over a fake listing.** With the default keep of one and
a listing of `2026-08-01T000000Z`, `2026-08-02T000000Z`, `zz-kept-by-hand` and
`aa-notes`, the rotation purged BOTH dated archives and `aa-notes`, and kept the
stray folder. The newest dated archive is the one run of rollback the rotation
exists to keep.

**Measured cost, and what was not measured.** A person loses the only rollback
of their last backup, and a folder they made by hand, with the backup reporting
success. The PRODUCER was not driven: nothing in this product writes a non dated
folder under the archive root, so the input is a person's own folder or an
archive root shared with something else. One candidate was considered and none
was driven against a real remote.

**Closes when:** the rotation considers only names `is_snapshot_name` accepts,
which is already in the module, and never purges a name it did not write. Board
bar (a) and (d). **Its issue is owed**, since a Relay session cannot open one
before the merge puts the number on `main`.

**Changed shape 2026-09-19 on `relay/154`, still open.** The rotation now holds
every name sorting after the last completed mirror's stamp as one slot. A stray
folder named with a letter sorts after every date, so it is HELD for ever and
occupies that slot: the dated folders written since the floor are held with it
and are no longer purged, and on a run that overwrote nothing the settled dated
folders are all purged where the newest should have stayed. Re-driven over the
entry's own listing in reasoning only, NOT at the engine. The kept set is never
smaller than it was before that branch, so the branch made this no worse, and
the closing condition is unchanged.

## R-550. A snapshot with no identity marker is pulled on the word of the person who named it

**Found:** 2026-09-19, on `relay/153`. It is what is left of the residual finding
about a pulled snapshot belonging to this library, and it is a decision rather
than an oversight.

Every snapshot taken before the marker existed carries none, and so does every
snapshot the source system wrote. Refusing them would strand a person whose
drive dies before their first marked backup, so `--snapshot STAMP` over an
unmarked folder is accepted, and the offer shows `recorded_volume` as null.

**Measured cost:** under a remote root two libraries share, a person who names
the other library's PRE MARKER stamp restores that library's database over this
one, which is the original finding narrowed to a typed stamp, an unmarked
folder and a shared root at once. Driven at the engine and at the verb as the
accepted case. No shared root was looked for on a real remote.

**The options, for a person to choose between.** Keep it, which is what landed.
Require a second explicit word for an unmarked snapshot, which costs a flag on
the day somebody's drive has died. Or write markers onto existing snapshots
from an attended sitting, after which unmarked can simply refuse. Does not meet
the board bar: it takes a deliberate act over a value the offer shows as null.

**Closes when:** a person picks one.

## R-556. A settled run's attempts are counted one by one again at a keep above one

**Found:** 2026-09-19, on `relay/154`, by the built in review. NOT driven.

The rotation groups only the newest slot. At a keep of two, a run that failed
(folder a) and was retried to success (folder b) is held whole, and the NEXT
completed run sees a and b as two settled folders, keeps b and purges a while the
run a belongs to is still inside the keep. Grouping settled runs needs a record
of which folders made a run, which the floor alone does not carry.

**Reachability:** `archive_keep` is a parameter of `plan_backup` that no shipped
verb passes, so every real run keeps one, and at one the defect cannot occur. One
candidate producer was read, `backup/cli.py`, and it does not pass the value.

Maintainer facing until a verb or a configuration key exposes the keep.
**Closes when:** the keep is exposed and the rotation groups settled runs, or the
parameter is removed.

---

## R-557. Two asks in the same instant can still file two backup jobs

**Found:** 2026-09-19, on `relay/154`, by the built in review. NOT driven.

`_open_twin` and `jobs.enqueue` are two steps. `enqueue` opens its own immediate
transaction around the insert alone, so two `backup run` processes starting
together can both find no twin and both file. A person typing the verb twice is
sequential and is covered. Nothing in the product schedules the verb.

Sharing one transaction means `enqueue` accepting a connection it did not open,
which is a change to the job engine every queued verb calls, and it was left
alone for that reason. **The cost is smaller than it was:** two runs no longer
prune each other's archive, since both sit after the floor, so what is left is
two syncs interleaving into one mirror.

**Closes when:** the scan and the insert share one immediate transaction, or a
check after the insert cancels the later of two twins.

---

## R-558. Two backup jobs that are already open can both be driven at once

**Found:** 2026-09-19, on `relay/154`, looking for the closed shape on the
performing path. NOT driven.

The guard is at enqueue. Two open backup jobs can still exist: filed before this
branch, filed through R-557, or made by `crate job resume` re-arming a FAILED
backup while a newer one is open. Each takes its own driver lock, and nothing at
drive time asks whether another backup of this destination is running.

**The cost is two syncs interleaving into one mirror, and no longer a lost
archive**, for the reason in R-557. Eighteen other verbs also enqueue
unconditionally; which of them name a shared target was NOT measured. The
write verbs among them run under the library write lock.

**Closes when:** the resume branch refuses while another open backup of the same
destination holds its driver lock.

## R-559. A rename can land on a name the approved plan did not promise

**Found:** 2026-09-20, on `relay/155`, reading the apply loop for R-172. NOT
driven, and the reachability is UNMEASURED.

`write/naming_cli.name_apply` renders each file's target AGAIN after the gate and
renames to whatever that second render says, never comparing it with the `to` the
plan promised and a person approved. A spec that moved between the two passes
therefore lands a name nobody was shown.

**Why it is not fixed here.** Inside one invocation the two passes are
microseconds apart and nothing between them can edit a tag, and a run resumed
with a recorded decision rebuilds the plan and re-compares the digest, which
answers a moved world with `DecisionStale` before the loop is reached. So the
window needs another process editing a tag in that gap. That is a shape nothing
in this product produces and no candidate was driven, which is why it is a
residual and not a guard: METHOD's bar wants the producer driven, and "I could
not think of one" is not a measurement.

**Closes when:** the apply pass refuses, or reports as outstanding, a file whose
re-render disagrees with the name the plan promised, or a driven producer shows
the window is unreachable and this entry is closed as such.

## R-560. A rename chain is reported rather than ordered

**Found:** 2026-09-20, on `relay/155`, driven end to end by
`test_a_target_another_mover_still_holds_is_promised_and_then_reported`.

Two files where one renders onto the name the other currently holds are resolved
by sort order alone. When the occupant sorts first it moves and the chain
completes; when it does not, the first file's claim fails and R-172's new answer
reports it as outstanding. The plan cannot rule it out, which is why it is left
promised, and nothing orders the loop so that an occupant moves before the file
that wants its name.

**The cost is one extra run**, and after R-172 a person is told which file and
why. A second `name apply` completes the chain, because the occupant has moved by
then. A cycle of two files that render onto each other's names never completes
and is reported on every run, which was NOT driven.

**Closes when:** the apply pass performs the renames in an order that resolves a
chain, or the plan detects a true cycle and holds it as a collision.

## R-561. Two rendered names differing only in case are held where both could land

**Found:** 2026-09-20, on `relay/155`, the deliberate cost of R-172's collision
key, driven at the plan by
`test_two_targets_differing_only_in_case_are_one_name`.

`_collisions` keys targets through `_key`, NFC and casefolded, because the volume
a library normally sits on treats two such names as one. On a case sensitive
volume both renames are possible and both files are held instead, with no flag
to say so.

**The cost is two files left unrenamed on a volume nobody in this project has
used**, and it is the direction `_is_referenced` already chose for the same
reason. A person meets it as a `collides` item naming a file that looks
different from the one it collides with.

**Closes when:** the collision key asks the filesystem whether it distinguishes
case, the way a mount probe would, rather than assuming it does not.

## R-562. A lowercase padded key is not a head, so the file is never renamed

**Found:** 2026-09-20, on `relay/155`, measured against the naming engine while
deciding whether R-172 needed a case only rename branch.

`naming.parse_head` does not recognise `05a - 120 - Song.flac` as carrying a
head, so `strip_head` returns the whole name as the body, the rendered name
equals the name on disk, and the file is not a candidate at all. Measured at the
engine: `05a - 120 - Song - Artist` renders unchanged, while `5A - 120 - ...`
pads to `05A`. The file is silently outside the convention for ever, and no plan
mentions it.

**Why it is not fixed here.** It is the naming engine's head grammar and not
R-172's loop, and widening the grammar changes what every consumer of
`parse_head` reads as a head, including the byte level export rewrite. It is
recorded here because it is the reason this unit has NO case only rename branch:
a target differing from its source only in case is unreachable, so a guard for it
would have been a guard on nothing.

**Closes when:** the head grammar accepts a lowercase Camelot letter and the
rename pads its case, or a doctor check reports files whose names look like a
head the engine will not read.

## R-563. The one level audio walks skip every dot name, so a real title is dropped

**Found:** 2026-09-20, on `relay/167`, by the code review of R-289's first cut,
and driven against that cut before it was narrowed.

`analysis/cli._audio_in` and `write/routing_cli.py`'s walk both skip a file whose
name starts with a dot, and their stated reason is the AppleDouble sidecar
`._track.flac`. The rule is wider than the reason. A leading dot is not reserved
on any filesystem this product runs on, and a DJ library is full of titles that
open with one.

**Measured cost.** Driven on the identical rule inside `tagging.tag.audio_files`
before it was narrowed: over a folder holding `...Ready For It.flac` and
`Metallica/...And Justice For All/01 Blackened.flac`, the walk returned nothing
and the verb reported that the folder held no audio it could tag. The same input
through `crate analysis` is NOT driven, so the reachability at that verb is
unmeasured, but the walk is the item derivation there too, so a track named this
way is never queued for analysis and no report says it was skipped.

**Why not fixed here.** Out of scope by this unit's brief, which names
`audio_files` and nothing else, and R-288 already owns the consolidation of these
walks into one helper in `core` taking the recursion and dotfile rules as
arguments. A fix here would be a third opinion about a rule R-288 is going to
move.

**Closes when:** the one level walks skip the AppleDouble prefix and the product's
own staging directory names rather than every dot name, the way
`tagging.tag.audio_files` does since `relay/167`, or R-288's shared helper lands
carrying that rule for all of them.

## R-564. A refused landing is kept as evidence for ever and nothing says so

**Found:** 2026-09-20, on `relay/167`, as the half of R-291 the sweep
deliberately does not touch.

`checked_landing` refuses a landing the lossless policy does not admit and the
file stays in its item's staging directory on purpose, because it is the evidence
for diagnosing the next demotion. `sweep_staging` reclaims only empty
directories, so every such file and the directory holding it survive every sweep
for the life of the installation. Nothing counts them, nothing reports them, and
no verb offers to clear them.

**Measured cost.** Unmeasured in size and certain in direction. One refused
landing per refused item, under the configured download root, on a disk the
person is also filling with the tracks the run did acquire. `acquire audit` walks
the music library rather than the staging root, so it does not see them either.

**Why not fixed here.** Reporting them needs a surface and clearing them needs a
gate, since deleting evidence a person may be about to read is a destructive act
and this unit's brief names neither. Choosing an age at which the evidence stops
being evidence is the person's decision rather than a session's.

**Closes when:** a report names what is sitting in the staging tree, or a gated
verb clears landings older than a declared age.

## R-565. `sweep` means two unrelated things across the acquisition and label verbs

**Found:** 2026-09-20, on `relay/167`, by METHOD's hunt for one symbol meaning
two things in two modules.

Everywhere else in this product a sweep is a productive pass that queues work:
`label_cli.queue_sweep`, `favorites_cli.resolve_sweep`, `sweep_items`, and the
tagging verbs' own "nothing to sweep" no-op, which means nothing to tag.
`acquire.cli.sweep_staging` means the opposite kind of pass, reclaiming litter.

**Measured cost.** Maintainer facing and nothing else. The two live in different
modules, share no key, no registry and no cause slug, so there is no surface on
which they can collide the way `lossy-refused` did as both a cause key and a
finding kind.

**Why not fixed here.** `reclaim_staging` is the better name and renaming it
after the fact would invalidate the `old` text of eight rows across three
mutation tables measured against `sweep_staging`, which are the evidence for
every guard in this unit. A word is not worth spending that.

**Closes when:** somebody renames it in a unit that is measuring those guards
again anyway.

## R-566. Two different tests each failed once under the parallel suite and passed alone

**Found:** 2026-09-20, on `relay/167`. The first when `scripts/mutate.py` refused
a batch on a red baseline, the second on this unit's own final battery run.

Two failures, in unrelated modules, neither of them anything this branch touches:

- `tests/test_write_session.py::test_an_unresolved_session_keeps_its_capture_out_of_the_pruner`
- `tests/test_pool_sizing.py::test_the_real_probe_measures_a_freshly_spawned_child`,
  which asserts a spawned child that allocated 256 MiB measures at least three
  quarters of that, and measured 219021312 against an empty child's 33144832,
  which is 185.9 MiB against a floor of 192.

Each passed on its own file immediately afterwards, and the full suite was green
on the run before and the run after each one. Six full `-n auto` runs on this
branch, two of them red, never the same test twice.

**Measured cost.** Maintainer facing. A flaky merge gate answers differently to
the same tree, so a session either merges on a re-run it did not justify or goes
looking for damage on a branch that has none. The pool sizing one names its own
likely mechanism in the assertion message, a child that has already freed what it
was asked to measure, and both appeared while eleven cores were saturated, which
this session did for over an hour.

**Why not fixed here.** Neither module is this unit's, and one observation each
is not a rate. The honest statement is two reds in six full runs, different
tests, on a loaded machine.

**Closes when:** each is run under `-n auto` on a loaded machine until it either
reproduces and is fixed, or enough clean runs accumulate to write the observation
off. The pool sizing one should be measured against machine load explicitly,
since a real memory probe racing the allocator is a timing assertion wearing a
size assertion's clothes.

## R-567. The reload the retag now names is an instruction nothing can verify

**Found:** while closing R-246, 2026-09-20. Driven.

`tag.retag` ends by telling a person to reload the folder's tags in rekordbox,
because the database half of the verb has no caller and the library rows keep the
genre the files no longer carry. It is a WARNING on the envelope and a step on
the refusal, deliberately, rather than the `pending_human_action` field the
product already has for exactly this shape. That field takes a mandatory
`verify_verb` naming a registered verb that proves the act was done, and its
`blocks` list is what turns it from advice into a state.

**Measured cost.** A person who reads the instruction and does nothing is never
asked again, and no verb reports the folder as outstanding. It is the eleven
printed instructions the source system lives with, on one more surface.

**Why it is not fixed here, and the reason is not effort.** There is no honest
`verify_verb` to name. Nothing in this build reads a library row's `GenreID`
back, and a second retag over the folder cannot stand in for one: the corrected
file carries a specific genre, so the selection skips it and the run reports the
same clean zero whether the reload happened or not. Naming a verb that answers
the same way in both worlds would make the field say something false about
having been verified, which is worse than the warning it replaced. Driven on the
two flavours of that check, a rerun over a corrected folder and the refusal's own
retry, and neither distinguishes the states.

**Closes when:** a verb can read the row's genre back, which is the same reader
the database half of R-185 needs, or the pending action gains a kind whose proof
is a person's own acknowledgement rather than a verb.

## R-568. The retag declares two database preconditions while opening no database

**Found:** while closing R-246, 2026-09-20. Driven.

The `tag.retag` entry keeps `doctor_checks=("library.mounted", "rekordbox.pins")`
after its write surface narrowed to `files`. The pin check is about a binding
that drifts on every database open, read or write, and this verb performs none:
the plan walks a folder, the worker reads and writes file tags and the review
store, and nothing in either path opens rekordbox.

**Measured cost. NONE observable, and it was measured rather than argued.**
`doctor.requires_check` is an `any()` across every registry entry rather than a
per verb lookup, and `repair.paths`, the other verb in the same `repair` module,
declares `rekordbox.pins` too, so a profile that switches this verb on requires
the check either way and the health report does not move. Nothing else in `src`
reads `doctor_checks`.

**Why it is not fixed here.** R-246 names the `writes` set and nothing else, and
`name.apply` is the landed precedent for exactly this: it narrowed to `files` for
R-165 and kept both checks. Changing one of the pair and not the other would put
two verbs of one shape into two states with no recorded reason. R-275's closing
condition asks for "drops the database preconditions" as part of its own
narrowing, so the question is already owned there.

**Closes when:** the precondition set is decided for the whole class of file only
verbs at once, or this verb gains the database half and needs both checks again.
