## R-703. The vendored downloader swallows the provider's error and the adapter reports only that no file came back

**Found:** 2026-09-24 at the eleventh attended sitting, A5 line 6. Nineteen
downloads across three lists failed with `unavailable-transient: the
downloader reported no file`, on tracks the provider reports available,
streamable and lossless. The cause was found only by repeating the
downloader's own lookup, `session.track(id, with_album=True)`, outside it: the
album read answered `TooManyRequests`. `_validate_and_prepare_media` in the
vendored `tidal_dl_ng/download.py` catches every exception and returns
`None` without logging it, `item` turns that into `(False, "")`, and
`landed_file` in `acquire/vendored.py` can only say no file came back. The
adapter also hands the tool `_discard_tool_logging`, so even the causes the
tool does log are dropped.

**Measured cost:** one sitting's diagnosis. Every download failed for about
fifteen minutes, and the printed remedy, retry later, was right by accident.
Nothing on the screen or in the job named a rate limit, so the obvious reading
was a broken downloader or a delisted track.

**Closes when:** a failed item's cause names the provider's own error, a rate
limit reads as a rate limit, and a test drives a lookup that raises through the
adapter and reads the exception's name off the item cause.

**Not on the board bar by itself**, and filed for the feeder because it cost a
sitting and will cost the next one.

**Closed 2026-09-24 on `relay/215`, issue 215, built on R-705's gate.** The
vendored tree is unchanged. `acquire/vendored.py` hands the tool a fresh
`_ToolLogging` per fetch in place of `_discard_tool_logging`, which still
writes nothing and now keeps the first failure the tool logs from inside an
except, read off the interpreter, and stands an `_ObservedSession` in the
downloader's `session` attribute, which notes an exception on its way out of
any method call, because `_validate_and_prepare_media` swallows without
logging. `landed_file` names that cause on the no file answer, a rate limit
as "the provider rate limited the lookup (TooManyRequests: Album
unavailable)", and raises `NoFileLanded` with the cause as an attribute. The
words are for a person: `classify_unavailable` holds the error transient by
type, since tidalapi's "Object not found" from the album read would
otherwise quarantine a track the offer had just found, and the paced pool's
`classify_signal` reads it as no pacing signal, since a carried "forbidden"
would park the run as an account block. A carried exception is asked
`raise_if_session_dead`, so a session rejected inside the tool is AUTH_FAILED
and a defect class is AdapterBroken. The Closes when test drives the real
`Download` constructor and `item` with a session whose album read raises
`TooManyRequests`. Twenty three mutation rows in three batches: two user
facing zeros got a test each and were killed on re-measure, and O2 is a
maintainer facing zero, `docs/mutation/r703-notes.md`. R-715 filed from it.

## R-705. Nothing keeps a label sweep and a download from sharing one rate limited account

**Found:** 2026-09-24 at the eleventh attended sitting. The label sweep and
three `acquire download` runs ran in the same half hour on one provider
account, and the sweep's catalogue crawl drove the account into rate limiting,
which failed every download (R-703) and 20 of the sweep's own labels (R-704).
Each verb runs its own driver and neither knows the other is spending the same
allowance.

**Measured cost:** the whole download batch of a sitting and 20 labels. A full
`crate sync all`, which queues a labels job beside the playlist intakes it then
downloads, is the same shape on a larger scale.

**Closes when:** every provider call the product makes goes through one
pacing gate with a configured minimum interval; a rate limit that survives the
retry ladder stops the whole run with the remaining items pending and a
`Retry-After` honoured; the trip is recorded in a state file so every verb
that calls the provider refuses inside a cooldown of at least fifteen minutes,
naming the reason and the lift time; one driver holds the account at a time
across processes and a second waits or refuses with a named reason; every run
that called the provider reports its call count and rate limit answers; and
tests against a fake that rate limits drive each of those. Widened by Phillip
on 2026-09-24 to the Tidal call safety card, issue #217.

**Closed 2026-09-24 on `relay/217`, issue #217.** `core/provider_gate.py` is
the gate, attached to the `requests` session the provider's library keeps on
each client at the two sites the product builds one, `provider_session.
client_session` for the catalogue and the account and the vendored adapter's
own tool session, so logins, refreshes and the model objects' own reads all
pass it; a test walks the package and refuses a third site. It paces to
`[provider] min_interval_s`, one second by default, measured from the last
call any process made, under one lock held for the whole of each call and
released for a `Retry-After` wait longer than the interval. Six consecutive
rate limit answers, one spent ladder, or a `Retry-After` at or above
`cooldown_s`, fifteen minutes by default, trip it: the trip is raised as the
engine's `Parked`, so the item in flight returns to pending and the driver
claims nothing further, and it is written to `provider_gate.json` with the
lift time, which every opener asks before it logs in. A lock held past two
minutes plus one interval is refused the same way, `provider-gate-held`. The
dispatcher puts one `provider-spend` warning on every envelope whose run made
calls. Twenty five mutation rows, every one killed; the notes carry the
sweep's arithmetic, about 6,300 calls for the 47 label registry, one hour
and forty five minutes at the default interval. R-703 and R-704 stay open;
#216 was held behind this and is released by it.

400 in `intake/acrcloud.py`. The refusal was right to spend nothing. The only
way through was by hand: the recording was fetched, split into two even halves
with ffmpeg, and each half identified as its own set, 366 calls each, 24 and
28 tracks.

**Measured cost:** a sitting's hand work, and two intake jobs for one set whose
tracks then land as two batches named Part A and Part B. A long live recording
is an ordinary input for this author, so the next one costs the same.

**Closes when:** a set over the bound is split into even parts each under it,
each part is identified, and the parts' tracks resolve and land as one batch
under the set's own name, with the whole spend checked against the monthly
bound before the first call. Decided by Phillip 2026-09-24: joined back into
one playlist where that is not new building, else the parts named Part A, Part
B and Part C.

**Closed 2026-09-24 on `relay/218`, issue #218.** A part is a place in the
chunk grid and never a file: the carver reads any offset of the recording,
so `acrcloud.partition` cuts the grid into the fewest even contiguous parts
each at or under `MAX_CALLS_PER_RUN`, which stays at 400, and `identify`
walks them in one pass. Every part is asked of the run bound,
`assert_run_within`, and the month is asked once over the whole owed spend,
`assert_month_within`, both before the first call of any part. The
refusal the run bound was written for is kept at a ceiling of `MAX_PARTS`,
three, `assert_one_set`, with the same cause and `per-run` kind: a file over
about eight hours and twenty minutes is still refused as not one set. The
answers fold once across the cut, so a record playing across it is one row,
which the sitting's two hand made halves could not give. The set queues as
one job with `parts` frozen beside `calls`, so it lands as one batch under
its own name and neither the playlist join nor the Part A, B and C names
was needed; both verbs say `recognition-in-parts`. The eleventh sitting's
shape, 732 chunks in two parts of 366, is pinned. Seventeen mutation rows in
three batches, every one killed. R-712 to R-714 filed from it.

## R-707. A copy made before the origin record existed has no way to gain one, so every library set up before R-689 reads as unrecorded for life

**Found:** on `relay/205`, 2026-09-24, closing R-689. Setup writes the origin
record only with a copy it makes, and leaves an existing copy alone. No verb
records an origin on an explicit ask, so a library set up before the record
existed, which is every library there is today, has doctor say "nothing
records which shipped text the copy was made from" on every run, and once
the shipped template moves on again the stale and edited histories are as
indistinguishable for that library as they were before R-689.

**Measured cost:** the live library. Its copy was edited by hand at the
eleventh sitting to add `[long_tracks]`, so it differs from the shipped text
and carries no record; doctor's detail says so and can say nothing more. Not
driven on the live volume, which is off limits; the shape is the no record
branch in `tests/test_doctor.py`.

**Closes when:** a person can record the origin for an existing copy on an
explicit ask, a `crate taxonomy` verb or a setup flag that, given the copy
matches the shipped text as it ships now, writes the record for that text,
and refuses when it does not match, since the origin of a copy that already
differs cannot be established. A test drives the ask on a matching copy and
reads the record, and on a differing one and reads the refusal.

**Not on the board bar.** Maintainer facing, nothing false is said and no
write is held.

## R-722. Adoption files every track as if it had no energy reading, and the library's files carry one

**Found:** at the twelfth attended sitting, 2026-09-25, driving #212 plan only
on a disposable copy of the live database. `adopt scan` then `adopt apply` to
the gate `adopt.apply.approve`, answered abort, tree `genre_energy`: 7,773 to
route, 2,058 needing a genre, 167 excluded, 153 unmapped, no collisions.
**7,401 of the 7,773 route to their bucket's Unsorted sub** and none to an
energy sub; the rest go to the per bucket exceptions, chill and the non
electronic subs. `adopt/plan.py` `_sub_for` passes a level of None to
`routing.energy_sub` on purpose, its docstring saying adoption "has no analysis
of its own". But the energy reading the routing tree files by is a tag in each
file, which `rebuild.read_truth` already reads for the export path, and
`tags.read_energy_from_file` over the 7,773 planned files answers **7,726 with
a reading and 47 without**, 0 missing, in under nine seconds.

**Measured cost.** Adoption is the one way door a tree takes to the database,
and it is additive: approved as planned, 7,401 tracks would be added to an
Unsorted sub beside whatever energy sub they already sit in on the live tree,
and the record would say the tree was adopted. Nothing was written; the gate
was answered abort on the copy.

**Closes when:** the adoption plan reads each file's energy through the same
reader the routing pass uses and files by it, leaving None only for a file
that carries no reading, with a test that a tagged file lands in its energy
sub and an untagged one in Unsorted. Then #212 drives adoption plan only again
and the Unsorted count is read against the 47.

**Closed 2026-09-25 on `unit/issue219`, issue #219, fixed in the code, awaiting
the attended check.** The census, `adopt/scan.py` `scan_rows`, reads each
adoptable file's energy through `tags.read_energy_checked` and carries it on
`ScannedTrack`, so the plan layer still takes no library input. `_sub_for`

`read_energy_checked`; `read_tags` and `read_energy_from_file` are the same
body with each failure folded into None per field, so there is still one
reader. Measured on fixtures only: 18 tests in `tests/test_adopt_energy.py`.
The Unsorted count against the 47 is the next attended sitting's to read, on a
disposable copy, before #212 goes further.

## R-725. A revert stays refused after a restore that undid the native write

**Found:** at the built in review of issue #220, 2026-09-27, by reading, and
the refusing half driven. `tree_registry.native_writes` reads the session log,
which survives a rollback on purpose, and a restore does not record which
session it rolled back to. So a tree that cut over, took a native write, and
was restored to the capture that write took still has the write in its log,
and `crate tree revert` refuses `cutover-native-write-taken` over a database
that no longer holds the rows.

**Measured cost.** The refusal is driven,
`test_a_revert_after_a_native_write_refuses_and_the_tree_stays_native`. The
restore in front of it was NOT driven, so that a person reaches this state is
argued from the log's declared role and not measured. The way out exists and
the refusal names it: the registry is coupled to the database, so restoring a
capture taken BEFORE the cutover puts the tree back on the bridge by itself.
What is lost is the narrower undo, rows gone and tree reverted while keeping
whatever else happened since the cutover.

**Why not fixed here.** It needs a restore to say in the log which session it
rolled back to, which is `core.restore`'s record to change and a unit of its
own. Guessing from timestamps would make the guard fail open.

**Closes when:** a restore records the session it rolled back to and the
revert guard leaves out a write that a later restore undid.

**Not on the board bar.** A workflow still finishes, by the wider restore, and
nothing is damaged: the guard refuses in the conservative direction.

## R-726. A membership writer that passed its registry check before a revert took the lock still writes

**Found:** at the built in review of issue #220, 2026-09-27, by reading, not
driving. `write_tree_membership` asserts `anchored_root` against the registry
its caller read, BEFORE it opens its session. `revert_cutover` holds the
session lock while it asks and writes, so no write is in flight during a
revert. A writer that read the registry, then waited on that lock while a
revert ran, opens its session afterwards and writes membership natively under
a tree that is now on the bridge.

**Measured cost.** Unmeasured, no producer driven. It needs an approved revert
and a membership write started within the same moment, the writer between its
registry read and its lock.

**Why not fixed here.** The fix is the writer asserting again inside its
session against the registry as it is on disk, and the writer takes its
registry as a parameter that tests and callers build in memory, so that is a
change to `write/trees.py`'s contract and not to this unit's verbs.

**Closes when:** a database membership writer asserts the tree's medium inside
the session it writes in.

**Not on the board bar.** No producer driven.

## R-729. The cutover verbs take no backup acknowledgment and assert no volume identity

**Found:** during issue #220, 2026-09-27, as a decision made with nobody to
ask. Both verbs declare no write surface and are not `destructive`, since what
they write is this product's own registry file, so neither opens a
destructive session and neither asks for the backup acknowledgment or asserts
the volume identity.

**The options.** (a) As built: the precheck stands in, refusing without a
verified snapshot and a Fresh Export, behind an explicit gate. (b) Declare
them destructive and open a session around the record, which needs the
precheck's open run check to leave the verb's own session out, since it
refuses over any open run. (c) Assert the volume identity alone before
recording. **Taken: (a)**, because (b) changes what the precheck means and
the registry file is restored with the database by any capture.

**Measured cost.** None driven. The exposure is a cutover recorded against a
library root that is a different volume than the one recorded at setup, which
`library.identity` reports in doctor and nothing refuses here.

**Closes when:** Phillip picks an option.

**Not on the board bar.** A decision, not a defect a person pays for today.

## R-731. Adoption adds a second band sub beside the one a track already holds, and never says so

**Found:** sitting 14, 2026-09-27, by approving `adopt apply` on a disposable
copy after the `genre_energy` cutover and comparing the tree before and after.
The plan places each track by its genre and its file's energy reading and asks
nothing of where the track already sits. The writer is add only. So a track
the library files under `Tech House / Med` whose file reads energy 8 is added
to `Tech House / High` and stays in `Med`.

**Measured cost.** Plan digest `5eca58df932496a3`, 7,773 routed: 7,073 already
present, 700 added, none removed. Of the 700, **569 tracks gained a second
band sub in a bucket where they already held one**: 331 held Med and gained
High, 215 held Med and gained Low, 19 held High and gained Med, 4 held High
and gained Low. 15 more gained a second style sub under `NonElectronic`, 11 to
Jazz and 4 to Rock. 107 had no place in the tree before and 9 were added
beside `with vox` or `Candy` alone, which is what adoption is for. The live
database already holds 37 tracks in two bands of one bucket, so the shape is
not new, and this would multiply it by sixteen through a one way door. The
gate shows counts and entries and no word about an existing placement, so a
person approving cannot see it.

**Which reading is right is not decided here.** The file's energy tag and the
sub the track sits in disagree on 569 tracks, most of them rated three stars
and sitting in Med. Whether the tags moved after a recalibration or the tree
was filed from another signal is the author's to say, per track or as a rule.

**Closes when:** the plan reads the tree it is about to write, withholds every
entry whose track already holds a different band sub, or a different style
sub where the bucket has no energy dimension, in the same bucket, counts them
on the gate under their own name, and lists them where a person can review
them, so an approved adoption adds a track only where it holds no competing
place.

**On the board bar, 2026-09-27.** Database rows are damaged in the sense the
bar means, a filing the library did not have and cannot shed through any
shipped verb, and #212 cannot run live until it closes.

**Closed 2026-09-27 on `relay/221`, issue #221, fixed in the code, awaiting
the attended check.** `adopt/placements.py` reads the tree from the database
the census read, the configured path opened with read intent, walking down
from the adopted root by identifier. It answers `unread` only where
`tree_registry.anchored_root` refuses, the function the membership writer
asks, so a plan that could not see the tree is a plan whose apply lands
nothing. `routing.competing_subs` says what competes from taxonomy
identifiers: the bands and the no reading sub in an energy bucket, the style
subs where a bucket routes by source or has no energy dimension, never a sub
class. `adopt/plan.py` withholds an entry whose track holds a different
competing sub in its bucket, keeps its bucket and sub on it, and names what it
holds. The gate's facts carry `placements`, `withheld_by_placement` with a
total and a count per kind, and `held_elsewhere`, every row with the track,
the subs held, the sub planned and the reading. The digest covers the rows as
shown and whether the tree was read. Nothing is moved or removed.

**The decision the card asked for: the same disposition with a reason.** A
withheld entry is `Disposition.WITHHELD` whatever withheld it, and
`PlanEntry.withheld_by` says `verdict`, `band` or `style`. A disposition
answers what an apply will do and both answers are nothing. The enumeration
is also the key set of `adopt scan`'s summary, where a member only the plan
layer sets would read zero for ever. `counts()["withheld"]` is therefore every
withheld entry, and the count the tree caused is `withheld_by_placement`, a
block of its own.

**One thing the card did not name, found by the review and driven red.** A
track sitting in the planned sub through a playlist renamed in rekordbox read
as already placed, and the writer finds a playlist by its declared name, so it
would have made a second playlist and filed the track in both. Such an entry
is withheld too, its row showing the same sub held and planned with
`holds_under_another_name` as the reason. It counts under its bucket's kind.

**The 37 are untouched and unlisted.** A track already in two bands where one
is the sub the plan names is `already present`, as the card requires, so it
is not on the review list. R-734.

Measured on fixtures only: 36 tests in `tests/test_adopt_placements.py` and 8
in `tests/test_adopt_workers.py`, the second set on real containers with real
tags over a disposable database. The withheld count against 569 and 15 and
the added count against 107 and 9 are the next attended sitting's to read, on
a disposable copy with library state redirected, before #212 runs live.

## R-740. A landed track's rekordbox Name loses the key and tempo head its file carries

**Found:** sitting 16, 2026-09-29, by the author, reading the import file's
titles in rekordbox. `intake.ingest.read_meta` reads the title tag, strips
the head, and renders the library name again from a `NameSpec` that carries
the key and no tempo. The tempo lives nowhere but the head it stripped, since
no tempo tag is ever written, so the head renders empty and the Name is the
bare title.

**Measured cost.** 18 of 18 landed tracks: filename and title tag read
`01A - 112 - Ain't Gonna Hurt Nobody`, the import file's Name read `Ain't
Gonna Hurt Nobody`. The 61 rows landed at sitting 8 carry bare Names for the
same reason. The library holds 9,756 headed titles, so a landed track sorts
and reads unlike everything beside it. Repaired by hand in rekordbox with
Reload Tags, which also reads the genre again and undoes a genre set by hand.

**Closes when:** the library name a landing writes carries the head the
file's own title tag carries, read from that head and never from a tempo tag,
and a test lands a file whose only tempo is in its title.

**On the board bar, 2026-09-29.** A workflow a DJ needs does not finish: every
landing needs a hand repair in rekordbox before the row reads like the
library.

**Closed 2026-09-29 on `relay/222`, issue #222, fixed in the code.** The
guarantee broke in `naming.normalize_spec`, not in the landing. It stripped a
head from the stem and the title so rendering would be idempotent, and kept
nothing it stripped, so `render_all`'s three surfaces agreed with each other
and not with the file. The naming verb and analysis each rebuilt the head
themselves before calling it, and `read_meta` did not. A stripped head now
fills the fields the spec left empty, the title's head first and the stem's
second, and only when every value the spec supplies agrees with it, the key
compared on the wheel. A marker inside a stripped head marks the spec.
`read_meta` takes its key from the title's head, or the filename's when the
title has none, over the key tag, so the Name is the title tag rekordbox reads
on Reload Tags. No tempo tag, BPM field or tempo element is read or written:
the head is text in a name, and the intake row still carries no tempo element
and `AverageBpm="0.00"`, asserted before and after the change.

A file headed nowhere lands with the bare title, as before, and nothing
invents a tempo. `intake file` reaches the same `read_meta` through
`ingest_file` and is tested the same way. The routing pass does not call
`read_meta` and renders no Name. `tests/test_landing_head.py` lands real
files, one whose only tempo is in its title. The rows already landed with
bare Names, 18 at sitting 16 and 61 at sitting 8, are not repaired here.
Mutation tables `docs/mutation/r740-a.md` to `r740-c.md`. Filed R-748 to
R-750, none on the board bar.

## R-745. A Fresh Export can only come from rekordbox, so every landing and every cutover waits on a person at its menus

**Found:** sittings 15 and 16, 2026-09-29. `intake land`, `intake imported`
and `tree cutover` each take `--export`, a rekordbox xml export of the
collection, and the only way to produce one is File, Export Collection in
xml format, by hand, with the application open. The product already reads
the database those rows come from, through a disposable copy.

**Measured cost.** Three exports by hand in one afternoon, each a launch, a
menu, a save dialog and a quit, with every verb stopped until it is done. An
export also goes stale the moment the database is written, which sitting 16
met when the 9-25 export no longer described a library adopted that morning.

**Closes when:** a verb writes a collection export from a disposable copy of
the configured database, in the shape the verbs that take `--export` read,
with no beat grid invented: tempo data is carried from the rows only where
the database already holds it, and the file says which application version
the database was last written by.

**On the board bar, 2026-09-29.** A workflow a DJ needs cannot finish without
a person at another application's menus.

**Closed 2026-09-29 on `relay/223`, issue #223, fixed in the code.** `crate
export collection FILE` writes the document from a disposable copy of the
configured database, read through `rb_writer.read_only_copy`, so it refuses
while rekordbox or its agent is running under `rekordbox-running`. The
emitter is `write/collection_export.py` and opens nothing. The verb is
`cli/export_collection.py`. It is core, writes one XML, asks nothing and is
not destructive: the file is created exclusively and nothing is replaced.

**The tempo decision: the export carries none.** Every row is written with
the gridless constant `AverageBpm="0.00"` and no child element, whatever the
database holds. The closing condition above allowed tempo copied from the
rows, and it is not taken, for three reasons. No verb reads a tempo off an
export, measured by a sweep of every consumer. A landing splices into this
file and hands the result to an import. And the source scan in
`tests/test_no_beatgrid_ever.py` refuses an interpolated value in that
attribute, so carrying one would mean loosening the guard the standing rule
rests on. The emitter's row type has no tempo field and the module never
names the column. `test_no_tempo_the_database_holds_reaches_the_file` seeds
a stored tempo on every row and proves no spelling of it is in the file.

**The application version: not claimed.** The database holds its schema
version and, in the binding's schema, no application version. The file names
three things in a comment ahead of the document element, each labelled: the
schema version read off the copy, the application installed on the machine,
and the version the recorded pin names. A value that could not be read is
written `unknown`. `collection_export.provenance_of` reads the line and
answers None for a file rekordbox wrote. The `PRODUCT` line keeps
rekordbox's name and company, since a landing's output is imported. R-751
and R-753 record what that leaves open.

**Where the shape is the readers' and not rekordbox's.** A folder with no
children is written as an open line and a close line, where rekordbox self
closes it, because a landing inserts into the intake folder. Every line ends
in a carriage return and a line feed. Membership is one key element per line
in the one spelling the membership reader matches. An identifier is written
as the string the database holds and must be digits.

**What a rekordbox export carries that this one does not.** The repository
holds no export of a real library, so this list is the format's published
attribute list against the emitter, and the byte fixtures the splice suites
use, which were cut from one. Absent altogether: the `TEMPO` child elements
and their `Inizio`, `Bpm`, `Metro` and `Battito`, the `POSITION_MARK` child
elements, which are the cue points and loops, and the attributes
`DateModified`, `LastPlayed` and `Colour`. Present and always empty:
`Grouping` and `Mix`. Present and constant: `AverageBpm`. Present with a
source not measured against rekordbox: `DateAdded`, which is the stock date,
or the day the row was created on this machine's clock when there is none,
and `Kind`, which is empty for a file type code outside the five the binding
names. Smart playlists are absent, R-752. The 25 attributes a row does carry
are the ones the intake emitter writes, in its order, asserted by name.

**The cutover precheck was read and holds with no new rule.** It asks that
the export is a file of non zero size. A test drives `tree cutover` to a
recorded cutover against a file this verb wrote. R-755 records what the
check does not ask.

**Every verb that takes `--export` is driven against a file this verb
wrote:** `intake land`, `intake imported`, `intake file`, `tree cutover`,
`route inbox`, `route unplaced`, `export playlist`, `sync favorites` and
`sync all`. The population is derived from the shipped parsers, so a new
verb taking one fails the test that lists them. The import proof is driven
in both directions: proved against a second export written after the rows
were added, and withheld against one written before.

**The built in review raised ten findings.** Eight were defects and are
fixed, each with a test: an identifier written as a number in one place and
a string in another, a control character no parser accepts, a streamed
track's reference dressed as a file, a folder asked only after the database
was copied, a second look that could disagree with the exclusive create, an
unreadable playlist kind folded to a playlist, a query per distinct artist,
and a day taken in Greenwich. One was this record. One was the duplicate
validation pass, which stays: the read needs digits before it sorts and the
emitter is the guard for a caller that hands it rows directly.

Mutation tables `docs/mutation/r745-a.md` to `r745-c.md`, read in
`r745-notes.md`. Filed R-751 to R-756. R-755 meets the board bar and its
issue is owed after the merge. Verification is owed at the next attended
sitting: write an export, take one from rekordbox the same minute, and
compare track count, playlist paths and each playlist's membership.

## R-746. A landed file reaches the collection only through a hand import

**Found:** sitting 16, 2026-09-29. `intake land` moves the files and writes
an intake file, and ends `PENDING_HUMAN` on five steps: point rekordbox at
the file, import one playlist and never the folder, drag it into INBOX,
export again, run `intake imported`. The import is the xml bridge, whose
limits sitting 10 measured: a playlist lands at the root whatever folder the
file gave it (R-687), and attributes are set only on rows it creates (R-688).

**Measured cost.** About twenty minutes of a person's time per batch, and
each hand step is a place to import the wrong node. The routing tree left
the bridge on 2026-09-29; the intake did not.

**Not known.** Whether rekordbox analyses a row it did not create when it
next opens, or waits for the track to be loaded. pyrekordbox can insert a
content row. Nothing here has measured what 7.2.19 does with one.

**Closes when:** a verb adds landed files to the collection through the
guarded database writer, behind a plan and an approval, on a library whose
intake tree has cut over, writing no beat grid, no tempo and no analysis
data, and an attended sitting has opened rekordbox on the result and read
the rows analysed.

**On the board bar, 2026-09-29.** The same bar as R-745, and this is the
larger half.

**Held behind #225, the same day.** The source system designed the
experiment that decides whether this may be built at all,
`DJ_tools/docs/runbooks/2026-08-01-u9-A1-gridless-insert-notes.md`, and its
attended half was never run. Its standing decision is that intake stays on
the xml bridge unless that verdict is clean. Issue #224 waits on #225 (A8).

**Released 2026-09-29 by A8's clean verdict, sitting 17.** Built 2026-09-29
on `relay/224`, issue #224. `intake land` chooses its medium by the intake
tree's mode. On a tree recorded database native it opens the database with
write intent, plans one content row per file with every column it sets, the
batch playlist under the adopted intake root and the device whose
`MasterDBID` is the library's, reads the backup acknowledgment before the
gate, asks an explicit gate, then moves the files and adds the rows through
the binding's `add_content`, restamped with the path under `BaseDBDrive` and
the chosen device, one playlist and the memberships in listing order, behind
one guarded commit that names the content table on `creations`. The guard
admits that one creation with a column policy of ten, judged in memory and
read from SQL after the flush with the cue, mixer and file tables, and every
other commit refuses a content row as before (R-760 closed with it). The
rows are read back after the commit and the answer says they await analysis.
The intake tree's own cutover refusal is lifted, since the landing no longer
owes the bridge a splice on a native tree. **Not written, and asserted column
by column:** `BPM`, `Analysed`, `AnalysisDataPath`, `AnalysisUpdated`,
`CueUpdated`, `KeyID`, `SampleRate`, `BitRate`, `BitDepth`, `ImagePath`, and
no `djmdCue`, `djmdMixerParam` or `contentFile` row. Left for rekordbox and
Reload Tags as well: `Length`, artist, album, genre (R-747). No routing
intent is recorded for a native landing; the routing tree takes the rows
through `adopt`. **The attended half is owed**, on a copy with library state
redirected and then live on three files at most, and belongs to
`docs/cutover.md`: this entry is closed by the build, and the sitting reads

landing refuses a title tag whose head is not in the written form.

## R-757. A backup compares the whole library against the remote however little changed

**Found:** sittings 1 and 16. The mirror is `rclone sync` with 16 checkers
and 8 transfers. Sitting 1: both sides listed in 51 minutes before 52 files
were copied. Sitting 16, 2026-09-29: 176 files and 1.44 GB had changed since
the last backup, and the job took about 55 minutes.

**Measured cost.** Most of an hour per backup. An attended session may open
rekordbox only with both backup ages under one day, so every sitting waits.
Where the time goes, the local walk, the remote listing or the comparison,
has not been measured.

**Closes when:** a backup of a library where under one percent of the files
changed completes its comparison in under five minutes on the author's
library, measured, with no changed file skipped, a full comparison still
available, and doctor saying how long ago one last ran.

**On the board bar, 2026-09-29.** A workflow a DJ needs does not finish in a
sitting's time.

**Measured 2026-09-29 on `relay/226`, issue #226, read only against the
live volume and the live remote.** 91,265 files in 22,433 folders, not
10,000. The local walk took 1.5 seconds. The recursive listing of the remote
took 66 and 139 seconds on two runs. The product's own mirror command as a
rehearsal had compared 18,774 files after 220 seconds and was killed at
540; 64 checkers in place of 16 held the same steady rate, 37 files a second
against 59, so the rate is the remote's request pacing and not the checker
count. The same command with the recursive listing option compared all
91,235 files in 190 seconds and found 48 to send. The cost was the listing,
asked once per folder at about ten calls a second.

**Closed by build, 2026-09-29, the attended run owed.** The mirror carries
`--fast-list` by default and `crate backup run --full` builds the command
as it was. Both modes compare every file by size and modification time,
driven through the real rclone between two temporary folders: a file
changed in content and not in size is sent, an added file is sent and a
removed one is archived, and the two modes agree on what to send. The fact
file records when a full comparison last completed, `doctor` reports it
under `backup.full_comparison`, and the resumed verb says the mode, the
seconds and the counts. The closing condition's real run is the attended
sitting's, and a rehearsal of it measured 190 seconds against the 300 the
condition names.

## R-758. No verb moves a track from one competing sub to another

**Found:** sittings 14 to 16. Adoption withholds 585 entries whose track
holds a competing sub, 569 by band and 16 by style, and lists them. Every
membership writer adds and none removes, so a track whose file reads energy
8 and which sits in Med stays in Med.

**Decided by the author, 2026-09-29:** the tag is the current reading and
the track moves to the sub the tag names. The evidence is sitting 16's
calibration test, 59 of 59 sampled library tracks scored equal to the energy
tag their file carries.

**Closes when:** a verb plans, for each track adoption holds elsewhere, the
membership to add and the one to remove, shows both on a gate with the
reading that decides it, and on approval adds the one and removes the other
through the guarded writer in one session, so a failure leaves the track in
at least one of the two. The removal is a soft delete as rekordbox makes it.
A sub whose class is manual or derived is never a move source.

**On the board bar, 2026-09-29.** 585 tracks are filed where their own file
says they do not belong, and no shipped verb can correct one.

**Closed 2026-09-29 on `relay/227`, issue #227, by `crate adopt move`.** The
attended run on a copy and the live run are owed and are not this session's.

**A verb of its own, and not `route resort` given a removing mode.** That
verb is additive and its summary says the old membership stays. A gate is
declared per verb and conformance holds every declared gate to firing, so an
approval asked in one mode only is a gate the registry cannot state. It sits
in the `adopt` group because what it moves is the list `adopt apply`
withholds, read with the census that verb reads.

**The removal is a SOFT DELETE.** The membership row stays, its
`rb_local_deleted` is set and its `updated_at` is moved, and the binding
stamps the local update sequence at commit. `TrackNo` is left and no other
row is renumbered. Read from a copy of the snapshot taken at 19:50Z, 4,817
membership rows carry the marker and all of them are still there. The
binding's own `remove_from_playlist` deletes the row outright and commits by
itself, past the guarded commit, so it is not used. What the reading does
not show is R-761.

**The whitelist is widened on purpose, by one table and one kind of
change.** A changed marker is now judged as a removal, in every table, and
every commit refuses one unless it names the table in `removals`. The only
table that may be named is `djmdSongPlaylist`, and the only caller that
names it is the second commit of `trees.move_tree_membership`. A hard delete
is refused everywhere as before. **Before this unit the guard could not see
a soft delete at all**: the marker is a bookkeeping column and those were
dropped before anything was judged, so a row whose only change was the
marker passed in any table, the collection included. That is closed here.
Proven per table the binding maps, and against a real database for the
additive membership writer's session, an ordinary guarded commit, a removed
collection row under an admitting commit, and a hard delete under one.

**Two commits in one session, the additions first**, behind one capture. A
removal is made only for a track read back as sitting in its target. A
failure between the two leaves a track in both subs, the job's report lists
which, the job fails on a cause a resume retries, and the resume finishes.

**The approved rows are frozen in the job.** A move changes the tree the
plan is rebuilt from, so a digest rebuilt in the worker would refuse the
verb's own half finished work. The worker proves the rows against the
approved digest, then asks the plan's own rule of each row over the library
as it stands, and refuses the whole run as a stale decision when a track
moved in a way nobody was shown.

**The count on the gate will not read 585**, and the attended reader should
expect that. The plan also takes the tracks R-734 counts, already in the sub
their reading names and in a stale one as well, 37 at sitting 14, which have
only the stale one removed. It leaves every track with no reading, every
genre that names no style and every sub held through a renamed playlist, and
lists each with its reason. The split by band and by style is on the gate.

**Every reader of a membership skips a removed one**: `add_memberships`,
`read_tree`, and the two upward walks in the routing pass. The placement
reader skips a playlist rekordbox removed. The marker is read in one place,
`rb_writer.soft_deleted`.

**The built in review raised ten findings and all ten were fixed**, each
with a test that drives it: removed nodes read two ways, an interrupt and a
refusal both raised as an interrupted move, the worker's check narrower than
the plan's rule, a reader's contract changed, a resume that showed a gate
before proving the job, two endings missing from the summary, a reason that
was untrue of a bucket, a walk per track, a third copy of the marker read,
and no fingerprint after the additions.

**The numbers.** 87 tests in `tests/test_adopt_move.py` and 30 new in
`tests/test_rb_writer_guard.py`. The mutation tables are the author's,
`docs/mutation/r758-a.md` and `r758-b.md`: 25 distinct mutations, 25 killed
on the subset each ran, none promoted since none was a zero. 16 rows were
considered and not run, each named in `r758-b-rows.toml` with why it ranked
below the cap. No independent verifier ran.

Filed **R-761**, **R-762** and **R-763**.

## R-759. A timing test fails the gate when the machine is busy

**Found:** 2026-09-29, by the author's question and the log of issue #223.
`tests/test_provider_gate.py::test_two_processes_never_call_at_once_and_keep_the_interval`
asserts intervals between two processes. It failed in the task's own full
run at 22:03Z, the minute rekordbox was launched on the same machine, and
again at the runner's gate at 22:07Z with the load average at 9. Alone on a
quiet machine it passed three times of three, and #223 touches none of the
code it covers.

**Measured cost.** One finished card refused at its gate and then excluded,
since the retry was refused at pre flight on the branch the first attempt
left. Landed by hand after two green batteries on a quiet machine.

**Closes when:** the test measures what it means to without depending on
the machine being idle, or is kept out of the parallel run and says why.

**On the board bar, 2026-09-29.** A guard on a path that writes is reported
failing when it is not, and a finished unit did not land.

**Closed 2026-09-29 on `relay/228`, issue #228, fixed in the tests.** The
gate is unchanged. **The assertion that failed was a lower bound with a
tolerance**, every gap between two send starts at least nine tenths of the
interval; the log's list read 0.039 and 0.031 against 0.05. It had no upper
bound. What the gate spaces is its own stamp, and a send begins after the
stamp and after an fsynced state file write, whose duration varied by up
to 13.6 milliseconds between calls at a load average of 13. That put two
send starts 40.7 milliseconds apart while the stamps stayed at least 50.1
apart. The measurement is in `docs/mutation/r759-notes.md`.

The rewrite splits the test in two. The interval test reads the stamps the
gate wrote and asserts each is at least the last plus the interval, exactly,
and that no send begins before its own stamp, less a millisecond for the
monotonic and wall clocks. The one at a time test holds each call for a
tenth of a second against an interval of a hundredth, so only the lock can
keep calls apart, and judges overlap by an `O_EXCL` marker with no clock.
Both passed twenty runs of twenty beside a running full suite at a load
average of 7 to 11. Dropping the interval, halving it, measuring it from
now, skipping the wait, removing the lock and sharing it are each killed,
the lock removal ten times of ten, in `docs/mutation/r759.md` and
`r759-b.md`. Nothing is marked serial.

**The sweep for the same shape**, a wall clock assertion with an upper bound
or a tolerance, over every `time.time`, `time.monotonic` and
`time.perf_counter` in `tests/`:

- Fixed: `tests/test_adoption.py`,
  `test_the_deadline_ends_a_read_that_keeps_arriving_forever`, asserted the
  read ended in under two seconds. It guards the read deadline a revert's
  digest rests on before it writes, so it now counts blocks read, at most
  twenty against the eleven the arithmetic allows. A deadline honoured a
  second late reads fifty.
- Listed, not fixed, since none guards a write or a provider call:
  `tests/test_pool_sizing.py`, the hung loader probe under 60 seconds, the
  abandoned loader probe under 8, the dead child probe under 15, and the
  release leg's band of 0.36 to 0.50 seconds on the minimum of five reaps,
  whose own docstring measures its margin under load.
- Listed as hang guards and not measurements: the polling deadlines of 15 to
  60 seconds in `tests/test_config_update.py`, `tests/test_doctor.py`,
  `tests/test_job_resume.py`, `tests/test_job_seam.py` and
  `tests/test_jobs.py`, each of which fails only when an awaited event never
  arrives. `tests/_hardware.py` times a calibration and asserts nothing.

## R-760. The guarded writer refuses a content row, and a verb that lands one needs a column policy

**Found:** sitting 17, 2026-09-29. `commit_guarded` refused
`db.add_content` on a copy, both rows, and the rollback left the table as it
was. The source system's guard passed the same insert, since the flush
emptied `session.new` first; that hole is closed here. So R-746 cannot be
built by calling the binding: the whitelist has to admit a content row on
purpose, with a rule for what a new row may carry.

**Closes with:** R-746.

**Not on the board bar.** It is a requirement of R-746 and is carried in its
card.

**Closed 2026-09-29 on `relay/224` with R-746.** A commit admits a content
row by naming the table on `creations`, held to `ADMITTABLE_ROW_TABLES`, and
the row is judged against `CONTENT_ROW_EMPTY_COLUMNS` in memory and again
from SQL. The read back had a second blind spot beside the one this entry
names: it walked `session.new` alone, so a creation the binding had already
flushed, which is every row `add_content` makes, was never read back at all.
It now resolves the instances the binding's buffer records a creation for.

## R-761. How rekordbox records one track taken out of a living playlist was not observed

**Found:** on `relay/227`, 2026-09-29, building R-758. Read from a copy of
the snapshot taken at 19:50Z. 4,817 membership rows carry
`rb_local_deleted`, and every one sits in a playlist that was itself
removed or in no playlist at all. No living playlist holds a removed
membership, and every living playlist's live rows number from 1 with no gap.
So the library shows how rekordbox removes a playlist and does not show how
it removes one track from a playlist that survives. One snapshot was read.

**What the move does, and what it does not copy.** It sets the marker and
moves `updated_at`. It leaves `rb_data_status` at 0, where every row
rekordbox removed carries 258 or 262, 313 of them on rows with no `usn`. It
leaves `TrackNo`, so a playlist a track left has a gap in its numbering that
no playlist rekordbox wrote has. The binding numbers a new row from the
count of every row, removed ones included, so no number is given twice.

**Measured cost.** None measured, since rekordbox was not opened. If
rekordbox does not honour the marker on a membership in a living playlist,
a moved track shows in both subs, which is the state before the move plus
one playlist. If it honours it, the unknowns are the gap and the status.

**Closes when:** at the attended run on a copy, rekordbox is opened after an
approved move and each bucket's subs are read, a track is then removed from
a playlist by hand in rekordbox, and the row it leaves is read beside one
the move left.

**Not on the board bar.** It closes only at an attended sitting, and that
sitting is R-758's own verification.

## R-762. The additive find or create hands back a playlist rekordbox removed

**Found:** on `relay/227`, 2026-09-29, by the built in review of R-758.
`rb_writer.ensure_folder`, `ensure_playlist` and `top_level_folders` go
through the binding's lookup, which filters nothing, and read no marker, as
the last one's docstring says. With a removed playlist of the declared name
under a live folder, the first match may be the removed one, and
`write_tree_membership` would add a track to a playlist nobody can see and
report it added. `read_tree` reports a removed node to the convergence
comparison as it always did. It carries a `removed` flag since this unit and
only the placement reader acts on it.

**Measured.** On a copy of the snapshot taken at 19:50Z the library holds
1,554 removed playlist rows. None sits under the routing tree's root: its 18
folders are live, and no playlist under them is removed. The record labels
tree, the intake tree and the root playlists were not read. One snapshot was
read and no producer was driven, so whether a verb or rekordbox itself can
leave a removed node inside a governed tree is unmeasured.

**The move does not share it.** It resolves what it adds to and what it
removes from through one walk over live nodes, and creates a live playlist
where there is none, which two tests drive.

**Closes when:** the find or create skips a removed node, or refuses on one,
for every writer, and the comparison that reads `read_tree` says what it
does with a removed node.

**Not on the board bar, with the reason.** The input was looked for on the
one tree `adopt apply` and the routing pass write, and is not there. It
joins the bar the day a removed node is found inside a governed tree.

product's own state folder, and a run that published rewrote it after the
mirror, so the next run sends it. The count a person reads after a real run
of an unchanged library is one, not none.

**Measured cost.** A sentence that says one file was sent over a library
whose music did not change. The file is library state and should travel.

**Closes when:** the sentence names the product's own state separately, or
the count is taken over the library minus the state folder, and the test
`test_a_run_that_published_sends_its_own_record_next_time` is reworded.

**Not on the board bar.** Wording.

---

## R-765. A failed mirror's counts reach job show and not the refusal the terminal prints

**Found:** by the built in review on `relay/226`, 2026-09-29. The engine
reads the comparison whether or not the mirror returned zero, so a run that
failed after sending half of what changed records how far it got. The
resumed verb raises the job's cause before the comparison sentence is built,
so the terminal shows the refusal alone and the counts are under `job show`.

**Measured cost.** A person whose mirror failed has to run a second command
to learn how far it got.

**Closes when:** the refusal carries the comparison as a step, the way the
rehearsal word rides `_with_rehearsal_step`, with a test that a failed
resume prints it.

**Not on the board bar.** The run is reported failed, and the counts exist.

---

## R-766. The recursive listing was not compared with the folder by folder one on the real remote

**Found:** on `relay/226`, 2026-09-29. The folder by folder rehearsal was
killed at 540 seconds with 18,774 of 91,235 files compared, so whether the
two listings of the real remote name the same files was not measured. The
tests between two local folders prove the two modes agree on what to send
where the listing option changes nothing. If the recursive listing ever
omitted a remote file, the mirror would send it again, and a remote that
holds two files of one name would then hold two.

**Measured cost.** Unmeasured. Nothing was observed missing.

**Closes when:** an attended sitting runs `crate backup run` and then
`crate backup run --full` on the live library within one sitting, and the
full run sends nothing beyond the product's own state files.

**Not on the board bar.** Closes only at an attended sitting.

## R-767. A fact file rebuilt by hand without the full comparison key reads its files record as a full comparison

**Found:** by the built in review on `relay/226`, 2026-09-29. The absence of
`full_comparison` from the fact file is read as a file written by a build
that had one mode, whose every mirror was a full comparison. That is right
for every file this product wrote before this unit, and it is the live
library's file today. It is wrong for a file a person rebuilt by hand after
the upgrade with only `schema_version` and `portions`, which the
`repair-backup-facts` remedy invites: the latest fast run then reads as a
full comparison and the next record persists it.

**Measured cost.** `doctor` says a full comparison ran when none did, on a
file somebody wrote by hand.

**Closes when:** the remedy's repair writes the key, or a fact file gains a
field naming the build that wrote it.

**Not on the board bar.** Reached only through a hand edit.

## R-768. Every other rclone command still lists the remote folder by folder

**Found:** on `relay/226`, 2026-09-29. Only the file mirror gained the
recursive listing option. `restore run --from-backup` copies the whole
mirror back with `rclone copy`, the analysis share is synced with `rclone
sync`, and the settings are copied, each without it, so a restore of the
whole library lists 22,433 folders at the paced rate before it copies, the
same most of an hour the backup paid.

**Measured cost.** Not measured on those commands. The mirror's number is
the only one read.

**Closes when:** each is measured on the author's remote and the option is
added where it helps, with the restore's agreement on what it copies driven
the way the mirror's was.

**Not on the board bar.** A restore finishes, slowly, and is rare.

## R-769. A file changed in content with its size and modification time kept is sent by neither mode

**Found:** on `relay/226`, 2026-09-29. Both modes compare by size and
modification time, as every mirror before this unit did. A tag write moves
the modification time, so it is sent, and the tests hold that. A tool that
rewrites a file and puts the old time back, or a bit that flipped on the
disk, changes neither number and is not sent. rclone's `--checksum` would
read every local file to compare content, which on a library this size is
a read of the whole volume, and it was not measured.

**Decided by the author of the unit, conservatively:** `--full` is the
folder by folder listing and nothing more, so the flag the brief asks for
keeps a comparison that is known to work. Whether `--full` should also
compare by content is Phillip's to decide, with the cost of one such run
measured first.

**Measured cost.** Unmeasured. No such file was observed.

**Closes when:** a checksum run is timed on the author's library and the
full mode either takes it or the ledger records why not.

**Not on the board bar.** Unchanged from every backup before this unit.

## R-770. Every other xml intake writer refuses as a defect once the intake tree cuts over

**Found:** on `relay/224`, 2026-09-29. `intake land` chooses its medium by
the intake tree's mode. Nothing else does. `intake file`, `sync favorites`,
`sync all`, the label batch and every other verb that writes an intake
playlist into an export goes through `rbxml.insert_intake_playlist`, whose
emitter guard refuses a tree the database owns with `tree-unconverged` and
the remedy `report-defect`. After `crate tree cutover inbox` each of them
refuses, and the refusal tells the person to file a bug against a cutover
they chose.

**Measured cost.** Not driven on a cut over library; read off the emitter
guard and the suffixes `pending_intake_xml` walks. The bridge stays whole
for a library that does not cut the intake tree over, which is every
library today.

**Closes when:** each intake writer chooses its medium the way the landing
does, or refuses in its own words naming the landing, and a test drives
each on a native intake tree.

**On the board bar, 2026-09-29.** A workflow a DJ needs, the favourites
cycle, cannot finish on a library whose intake tree has cut over, and the
refusal says something false about whose defect it is. The issue is owed
after the merge that carries this entry.

---

## R-771. A manifest is refused on a native intake tree, so label filing has no native path

**Found:** on `relay/224`, 2026-09-29. `--manifest` files a manifest's label
rows under the record labels tree inside the intake file the landing wrote.
The native medium writes no intake file, and the record labels tree has no
database writer for a landing to call, so `intake land --manifest` on a
native intake tree is refused before the gate with the flag named, and the
files land without their labels when run again without it.

**Measured cost.** A label batch landed natively files nothing under its
label. Whether the label verbs' own sweep files the same tracks later was
not driven.

**Closes when:** the label rows are filed through a native writer for the
record labels tree, or the refusal is replaced by a warning once that tree
has a medium of its own.

**Not on the board bar.** Refused before anything moves, and said in the
person's terms.

## R-772. The stored path's base drive form and the prefix map are two records of one fact

**Found:** on `relay/224`, 2026-09-29. A landed row's `FolderPath` is stored
under `djmdProperty.BaseDBDrive`, swapped for `CurrentDBDrive`, which is
what rekordbox's own rows carry. Every reader of the collection resolves a
stored path through `library.location_prefix_map`, which setup offers from
the same two drives and a person may edit. When the two disagree, a row this
product stored resolves to nothing on this machine: the next landing of the
same file reads it absent and plans a second row, and the binding's own
duplicate check compares the mounted spelling and does not catch the base
drive one.

**Measured cost.** Not reached. On the author's library the map was written
from the drives, and on a library whose drives have never moved the two
spellings are one. A test holds the swap and a test holds the resolver; no
test holds them to agreeing.

**Closes when:** the landing refuses, before the gate, a base drive the
prefix map does not map to the current one, or the plan resolves its own
stored path through the map and refuses when it does not come back.

**Not on the board bar.** Reachability unmeasured; the input needs a map
edited away from what setup wrote.

## R-773. The collection export writes every Location under the base drive, so intake imported matches nothing it names

**Found:** at sitting 19, 2026-09-29, attended. `docs/cutover.md` sitting 19
is the measurement. `crate export collection` was written from the live
database and handed to `intake imported` for the batch sitting 18 landed.
It matched nothing and ended `PENDING_HUMAN`. A copy of the same file with
the base drive's mount name replaced by the current one through `sed` proved
the import, one track, and retired the intake file.

**The mechanism.** `write/collection_export.py` reads `FolderPath` from
`djmdContent` as the database holds it, and `_location` encodes a plain path
unchanged, so every `Location` carries `djmdProperty.BaseDBDrive`, which on
the author's library is the `BoatRx` rule's drive and not the mounted path.
rekordbox's own export writes the current drive. `intake imported` digests
each Location's decoded path through `routing_pass.track_id` and compares it
with the landed file's path under the mounted root. `library.location_prefix_map`,
the one rule that joins the two spellings and the rule `doctor` reports as
recorded, is applied by neither side. R-772, filed by #224 the same
evening, is the same two records seen from the native landing's duplicate
check; this entry is the export writer's side of it.

**On the board bar, (c):** the workflow `intake land` then `intake imported`
cannot finish over the export this product writes, and #223 was landed on
the claim that the verbs taking `--export` are driven against a file it
wrote. Nine were, and `imported` was driven against a fixture whose two
spellings agreed.

**Two remedies, and the first is recommended.** The export applies the
prefix map and writes the mounted path, since that is what a Fresh Export
holds and every consumer of an export already reads that spelling. Or
`imported` applies the map on the way in and the export stays a copy of the
database. The first keeps one spelling in every export; the second leaves
`adopt scan` and the routing verbs reading a file rekordbox would not have
written.

**Measured cost.** One batch, one track, one hand edit with `sed`. Every
landing until it lands.

**Closes when:** `intake imported` proves an import over a file
`crate export collection` wrote, on a library whose `BaseDBDrive` differs
from its mounted root, with no edit between the two verbs.
